Then: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <your-commit> <the build sha>` — exit 0 means your change shipped. **Always run a two-sided control in the same breath**: one literal that must be present (`build provenance`) and one sha that must be absent, or you cannot distinguish "not stamped" from "probe broken". Per SERVICE, never per fleet (`bugs_open/249`).
- **relations:** LANDMINES "a criteria check type the running browser-runner binary does not know is SKIPPED" (the sibling trap — short Go string literals compile to immediate comparisons and never reach rodata, so a short marker also greps 0 on a binary that fully supports it; together they mean **no `grep -c` of a short literal is evidence either way**) · CLAUDE.md "Building & deploying images" (which already says ask the binary, not git — this entry is why the *naive* way of asking returns the wrong answer) · `MEMORY/prove-a-deploy-at-the-artefact-index.md`
- **source:** flagged as a candidate by the `bugfix_281_tool_audit_ported` lane 2026-08-16; **written and verified first-hand 2026-08-17** by the session that took its handoff forward (the probe and both controls above are that verification, not a relay).
- **added:** 2026-08-17, `bugfix_281_tool_audit_ported` lane

### A stalled `audit_tool` item costs THREE Sonnet audits, not an unbounded retry — and the "every ~40 minutes" figure in the 281 handoff is a single item generalised

- **footprint:** `site_work_items` where `item_type='audit_tool'` · the claimed-item-timeout sweep · `orchestration_states` grouped by `collected_data->'input_data'->>'work_item_id'` · `tool-auditor` · any cost estimate for a stalled handler item
- **fires when:** you cost a stall. A `tool-auditor` run that never completes leaves its item claimed, the claimed-item-timeout sweep releases and re-dispatches it, and each re-dispatch pays for a **fresh Sonnet audit of the whole tool**. The trap is the *size* of that bill: the `bugfix_281` handoff recorded "a fresh Sonnet audit each ~40 min until `failed`", which reads as an unbounded loop and would justify emergency action.
- **the correction, measured 2026-08-17** across every `audit_tool` item with more than one orchestration: the per-item orchestration count **caps at 3** — 3 is the maximum anywhere in the table, not a sample — and the mean gap between attempts is **43, 59, 128, 129, 147, 147 minutes**. So the true cost is **≤3 audits over roughly 1–5 hours, then the item goes `failed`**. The single item that does show ~43 min (`1bfd5d1e-…`) is the 281 lane's OWN hand-filed probe, which is where the figure came from; generalising one item's cadence to the class overstated the rate by ~3x and the total by an unbounded factor.
- **the tell:** a rate quoted without the cap. "Every N minutes until X" is a claim about *two* numbers — the interval and the terminating condition — and the terminating condition is the one that decides whether the bill is bounded. If a doc gives you the interval and not the count, get the count before you act on it.
- **the check:** one query, and it answers both halves at once —
  ```sql
  SELECT collected_data->'input_data'->>'work_item_id' AS item, count(*) AS attempts,
         round(EXTRACT(epoch FROM (max(created_at)-min(created_at)))/60
               /GREATEST(count(*)-1,1)) AS avg_gap_min
  FROM orchestration_states
  WHERE owner_agent_type='<handler>' AND collected_data->'input_data'->>'work_item_id' IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10;
  ```
  Read the **top** `attempts` value as the cap, and never take the gap from one row.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/289` (the defect that stalls these runs — fixed `509e01e6a`, inert until the roll) · `bugs_open/294` (why the stalled orchestrations were then immortal) · `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-16 "a commit message is an argument, not an API" (same failure: a relayed figure adopted without re-measuring — this entry exists because the relay was checked)
- **source:** candidate flagged by the `bugfix_281_tool_audit_ported` lane 2026-08-16 with the ~40 min figure; **measured and corrected 2026-08-17** by the session that took its handoff forward.
- **added:** 2026-08-17, `bugfix_281_tool_audit_ported` lane

### A `banned_claims` pattern seeded through dollar-quoted JSON is DOUBLE-ESCAPED, compiles cleanly, and matches nothing for ever — and the `jsonb_array_length(...) = N` check you wrote to prove it landed passes either way

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/claims.go`, `docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/portfolio_positioning/`, `banned_claims`, `ScanBannedClaims`, `evidence_base`
- **also fires on** (prose, not footprints — these cannot be grep keys): any `SEED_*.sql` writing `site_specs.aspect='evidence_base'`, and any dollar-quoted `$tag$ … $tag$` **JSON** literal holding a regex or a `\uXXXX` escape.
- **fires when:** you seed a site's claims guard and verify it the obvious way — count the patterns, see the number you expected, move on. Two escaping layers are in play and only one is visible: the dollar-quoted SQL string passes bytes **literally**, and the JSON parser **then** unescapes. So `\\\\b` in the file stores `\\b` (a literal backslash then `b`), and `\\u00a3` stores the six characters `£` instead of `£`.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** `claims.go` compiles with `regexp.Compile("(?i)"+p)` and falls back to `regexp.QuoteMeta` **only when compilation ERRORS**. `\\bguaranteed …` is a perfectly valid regex — it just never matches English prose — so it compiles, **the fallback never fires**, and the guard is loaded, listed, counted and inert. There is no error, no log line and no failure row; the site simply has no claims guard. **A pattern that fails to compile is caught. A pattern that compiles WRONG is not.**
- > **CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (bugfix_414 lane, raised by the loancalculator_couk lane):** that
  > last sentence is **wrong for the per-site patterns this entry is about**. A non-compiling
  > pattern is caught **only in the fleet-wide set**, and only because that set is authored in
  > **Go** and pinned by `TestEveryGlobalPatternIsAValidRegex` (`claims_global_test.go:376`) —
  > a CI test, which by construction cannot see a pattern that arrives as **data**. A per-site
  > pattern from `evidence_base` JSON hits the identical silent fallback at `claims.go:348`
  > and **nothing anywhere reports it**: not the parser (no logger, no error path), not the
  > admin door (`site_admin_handlers.go` counts `banned_claims` and guards against emptying
  > the set — it never compiles a pattern), and not a migration (`ON_ERROR_STOP` cannot see a
  > regex that Postgres never compiles). So **both** halves are silent for site-authored
  > patterns, and the difference between them is only how inert you get: a non-compiling
  > pattern degrades to a literal of its own source text, a mis-escaped one compiles and
  > matches a literal backslash. Same outcome — armed, listed, counted, inert.
- **the check for the compile half, fleet-wide, in the right engine** — extract every live
  per-site pattern and compile it exactly as production does (`regexp.Compile("(?i)"+p)`),
  with a deliberately broken control in the same run so a silent checker cannot read as a
  clean fleet:
  ```sql
  SELECT s.domain, bc->>'pattern' FROM sites s
  JOIN site_specs eb ON eb.site_id=s.id AND eb.aspect='evidence_base' AND eb.is_current
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(eb.data->'banned_claims') bc;
  ```
  `[MEASURED 2026-09-02]` **239 patterns across 19 sites: 0 non-compiling, 0 doubled-backslash**
  — a clean baseline, established the day five finance sites gained hand-authored sets, and the
  controls (`best (loan|deal`, `\\bguaranteed`) both fired. **A clean result here is worth
  re-establishing rather than inheriting**: the population grows every time a site is seeded,
  and this census is stale by ADDITION the moment the next migration lands.
- **so, when you author patterns for a site: Go-compile them AND probe-fire each one before
  arming.** The loancalculator lane did exactly this for migration 707 (8/8 fired against real
  copy, then a 0-match census over all 28 served pages so arming could not refuse a current
  save) — that is the practice this entry is asking for, and it is currently the ONLY thing
  standing between a typo and an inert guard. The unbuilt option, if someone wants to close it
  properly: compile-check the patterns at the admin door, or add a data-driven sweep to
  `cmd/claimscan`. Nothing has fallen through yet, which is why it is recorded rather than built.
- **`[MEASURED 2026-08-17, remortgagecalculator.uk pilot seed]`:** all **6 of 6** patterns inert on the first apply. The seed's own verify block asserted `jsonb_array_length(banned_claims) = 6` and **passed** — a count comes out identical whether the guards work or not, which is the same shape as `WRONG_CALLS`' "a `[MEASURED]` figure is only evidence if it could have come out otherwise".
- **the check — probe, never count.** Assert BEHAVIOUR with strings that must match *and* strings that must not (a guard matching everything is as broken as one matching nothing, and only the pair tells them apart). **Do it in Go, not SQL:** Postgres ARE and Go RE2 disagree on word boundaries — PG spells it `\y`, and `\b` is *backspace* — so a `psql … ~ pattern` probe is a check in the wrong engine and will lie to you in both directions. Worked pair: `datahelpers/claims_banned_pattern_escaping_test.go` (semantics, compiled exactly as production does) + the seed's own structural guard.
- **for the structural half, avoid `LIKE` entirely — use `position()` + `chr(92)`.** In `LIKE`, backslash is itself the default ESCAPE character, so `'%\b%'` means *"the letter b"* and would pass on any pattern containing `b`; `position(chr(92)||'b' in p) > 0` has no escape semantics to reason about. `chr(92)` also survives an authoring channel that rewrites `\uXXXX` into the character it denotes — which is how the same file's `£` check ended up searching for `£`, the very thing it was meant to confirm, and refusing correct data twice (MEMORY: `escape-sequence-emission-trap`).
- **prove the guard can fail before you trust it:** run the new structural check against the **still-broken** rows and require it to flag them (it reported 6 bad / 6 total), then against the fixed rows and require zero. A guard only validated on good data is untested.
- **relations:** `MEMORY/mutate-the-code-to-prove-the-guard.md` · `MEMORY/a-pass-from-a-blind-check-outlives-the-blindness.md` · LANDMINES "Adding a template variable to a prompt WITHOUT adding its field to that step's `input_fields` renders EMPTY and errors nothing" (same family: applied, silent, and structurally verifiable while functionally dead) · `bugs_open/012` (a rewrite that reports success having persisted a fragment) · `portfolio_positioning/SEED_2026-08-17b_remortgagecalculator_uk_fix_banned_claim_escaping.sql` (the correction, with the mechanism in its header)
- **added:** 2026-08-17, portfolio_positioning lane (found on its own Phase C pilot seed, minutes after applying it — by probing rather than counting)

### The whole build pipeline stops dispatching and NOTHING says so — items stay `triaged` with `attempt_count 0`, the dispatch loop COMPLETES every ~90s, and the reason is one row in `ai_endpoint_health`

- **footprint:** `ai_endpoint_health` · `platform/orchestration/actions/claim_work_item_action.go` (`extractAIEndpointFromHandler`, the health gate at ~line 218) · `build-dispatch-loop` · `build-pipeline-trigger` · `site_work_items.status='triaged'` · `scheduled_tasks` `ai-endpoint-health-check` · any hand-raised work item (`tool_acceptance_run.sh`, `090`/`097` triggers, `improve_tool`, `add_tool`)
- **fires when:** you raise a work item at the fleet and follow it. Every published symptom says "working": the item exists, `build-pipeline-trigger` fires on its 30s tick, `build-dispatch-loop` runs and reaches `status=COMPLETED`, its `pending.item_count` is 1 with `rows_dropped: 0`, and there is **no `__step_error` anywhere**. Your item simply never leaves `triaged`, and `attempt_count` stays 0 — so even the retry counter tells you nothing happened.
- **the mechanism:** `claim_work_item` looks up the handler agent's AI endpoint and reads `SELECT healthy FROM ai_endpoint_health WHERE endpoint_url = $1`. If the row says false it **releases the claim and sets the item back to `triaged`**. That is correct, deliberate behaviour — the work resumes when the endpoint recovers, nothing is lost — but it is invisible at every level a session normally looks. Note the asymmetry that makes it worse: **no row at all is treated as healthy** (a deliberate choice, commented in the code), so absence and health look the same and only the false row bites.
- **the second-order trap: one stuck item monopolises the dispatcher fleet-wide.** `build-pipeline-trigger`'s `find_dispatchable_site` is `ORDER BY wi.created_at ASC, wi.priority ASC, wi.id ASC LIMIT 1` — **one site per tick, strictly oldest item first**. An item that can be selected but never claimed is re-selected every cycle for ever, so every other site starves. Measured 2026-08-17: `webdesign.co.uk` took **18 of 18** dispatch-loop runs in one hour while two other sites' items sat untouched; over the preceding day the same site took **95** runs. Do not read "my site never gets a run" as a rotation problem — read the oldest triaged item in the fleet.
- **the check, and it is one query — read the CLAIM, not the item:**
  ```sql
  SELECT collected_data->'claim_result' FROM orchestration_states
   WHERE owner_agent_type='build-dispatch-loop' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;
  -- {"claimed": false, "reason": "ai_endpoint_unavailable", "endpoint": "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages"}
  SELECT endpoint_url, healthy, last_healthy, error FROM ai_endpoint_health;
  ```
  `execution_path` is `[]` on these runs, so use `collected_data`'s keys instead: `process_item_iter_0_check_claim` present with no `spawn_handler` IS the signature.
- **⚠ and the reason may not be a fault at all — it may be a spend cap.** Hit live 2026-08-17 11:08Z: `healthy=f`, error `API request failed with status 400 … "You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on 2026-09-01 at 00:00 UTC."` That is an **account limit set in the provider console, not an outage**, so no amount of waiting, retrying or re-dispatching helps and the health check (hourly) will keep confirming it. 26 items were blocked within the hour. **Read the `error` column before diagnosing anything**, and confirm against a second source — `SELECT created_at, agent_type, error_message FROM llm_call_log WHERE provider='anthropic' AND NOT success ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5` — because a health table is an instrument and this entry is exactly the situation where a believable outage story invites you to trust it unchecked.
- **source:** 2026-08-17, leopardess lane, while following a hand-raised `acceptance_run` that never got claimed; the endpoint cap was found four queries later and explained three sites' stalled items at once
- **relations:** MEMORY [[detection-works-schedule-and-dispatch-do-not]] · [[a-plausible-external-cause-is-when-to-doubt-your-instrument]] · [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] · LANDMINES "Enabling a `scheduled_tasks` row proves nothing" (the sibling shape: the task fires and dispatches nothing)
- **added:** 2026-08-17, leopardess voice/acceptance lane

> **⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-17 12:55 BST (11:55Z) by the loanandmortgagecalculator lane, ~50 minutes
> after the entry above was written.** The entry is right that the 400 is an account limit rather
> than an outage, and right that `ai_endpoint_health` must be read for its `error` column. **Its
> practical conclusion — "no amount of waiting, retrying or re-dispatching helps" until
> 2026-09-01 — did not hold, and a session that believes it will not dispatch anything for two
> weeks.** Measured just now, `[MEASURED 2026-08-17 11:55Z]`:
>
> ```sql
> SELECT provider, success, count(*), max(created_at) FROM llm_call_log
>  WHERE created_at > now() - interval '90 minutes' GROUP BY 1,2;
> --  anthropic | f |  4 | 2026-08-17 11:09:53Z
> --  anthropic | t | 97 | 2026-08-17 11:54:39Z   <-- 23 seconds before the query
> SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT success) FROM llm_call_log
>  WHERE created_at > now() - interval '20 minutes';   -- 28 calls, 0 failures
> ```
>
> So live `provider='anthropic'` traffic recovered within minutes and is healthy now, while
> `ai_endpoint_health` **still reads `healthy=f` with `last_healthy = 11:07:15Z`** and the
> September message in `error`. The limit was window-scoped in practice; the row is not tracking
> the recovery, because nothing has re-probed it successfully since.
>
> **So the check inverts: `ai_endpoint_health` is the instrument and `llm_call_log` is the
> traffic.** Read the health row for *why* something failed at a moment in the past; read the
> call log to answer "can I dispatch now?". A red health row with a fresh successful call log
> means the row is stale, not that the fleet is down — which is the same lesson the entry itself
> draws one line earlier about believable outage stories, applied to its own conclusion.
> `[UNMEASURED]` whether the 4 failures and the 97 successes share one key/limit bucket; the
> dispatchable-now answer does not depend on it.
> - **added:** 2026-08-17, loanandmortgagecalculator D6 planner lane

## The BUILD QUEUE can be fully stopped while every liveness check says the fleet is healthy — `claim_work_item` gates on `ai_endpoint_health`, and that row is re-probed ONCE AN HOUR

- **footprint:** `ai_endpoint_health` (the `claude` row, `check_interval_seconds`) · `platform/orchestration/actions/claim_work_item_action.go` (the "AI endpoint health check" block, `reason: ai_endpoint_unavailable`) · `check_endpoint_health_action.go` (the prober, `claude_ping`) · `build-dispatch-loop` (`load_items`/`process_item`) · `build-pipeline-trigger` (`find_dispatchable_site`) · any question of the form "why has my work item not dispatched?"
- **fires when:** you create a work item, see the dispatch loop running on schedule, confirm the loop LOADS your item, and confirm LLM calls are succeeding fleet-wide — and conclude the queue is merely slow. It is stopped. One 400 from the AI endpoint (an intermittent usage cap: `bugs_open/243`) flips `ai_endpoint_health.healthy` to false; `claim_work_item` then RELEASES every claim fleet-wide and sets the item back to `triaged`; and because `find_dispatchable_site` is `ORDER BY created_at ASC … LIMIT 1` across ALL sites, the whole fleet queues behind one item that can never clear. The row is re-probed on `check_interval_seconds` = **3600**, so the stop outlives the outage by up to an hour
- **the tell — and why the obvious checks all read GREEN:** the dispatch loop runs to COMPLETION every ~90s (not stuck, not erroring); `pending.has_items = true` with your item in it; `orchestration_states` shows healthy completed runs; and `llm_call_log` shows real successes THROUGHOUT (measured 2026-08-17: 93 of 99 calls OK, latest 11:52:32Z, while zero items had been claimed since 10:32:33Z). **`SELECT max(created_at) FROM llm_call_log WHERE success` — the fleet's own recommended liveness query — reports UP while nothing can be claimed.** The only honest tell is in the loop's own `collected_data`: the path runs `claim → check_claim → done`, `spawn_handler` is never reached, and `claim_result` reads `{"claimed": false, "reason": "ai_endpoint_unavailable"}`
- **the check, before diagnosing any "my item won't dispatch":**
  ```sql
  SELECT healthy, last_checked, last_healthy, check_interval_seconds, left(error,120)
    FROM ai_endpoint_health WHERE name = 'claude';
  SELECT max(claimed_at) FROM site_work_items WHERE claimed_by = 'build-dispatch-loop';
  ```
  `healthy=f` plus no claim since about `last_checked` IS this, and no amount of waiting on your own item will show it. Read the claim result rather than the loop's status: a loop that claims nothing COMPLETES successfully. **Do not infer dispatch health from LLM health** — they are independent, and under an intermittent cap they disagree for an hour at a time
- **source:** 2026-08-17, webdesign_uk_build_service lane — found because it blocked a `bugs_open/285` acceptance run; full mechanism, timings and the three fix shapes in the 2026-08-17 addendum to `bugs_open/243`. The prober samples ONE call on `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` while live traffic is sonnet/opus, and `llm_call_log` holds zero haiku rows in 24h — so the probe's own model is cross-checkable from nothing
- **⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-24 (`bugfix_243_provider_cap_resilience`) — THE PROBE CANNOT DETECT THIS CONDITION, so two things above read as more benign than they are.** (a) **The probe is a TIMER, not a health check, for a usage cap.** `pingClaude`'s status switch (`check_endpoint_health_action.go:220-231`) is 200→true, 402→false, 401→false, 529→true, **default→true** (*"any non-auth error means API is reachable"*), and the cap arrives as a **400**. So the hourly probe writes `healthy=true` on its next tick **whether or not the provider is still refusing us** — the stop is bounded by `check_interval_seconds`, not by the outage, and a probe that "recovered" is not evidence the cap lifted. This also retires the "lost coin-flip" reading of the probe in the 08-17 addendum: the probe cannot fail on this condition, so it cannot lose that flip. (b) **The write is ONE-DIRECTIONAL from live traffic.** `grep -rn "update_endpoint_health" --include=*.go platform/ internal/ pkg/` returns **exactly one** hit — `ai_actions.go:634` — and it **only ever passes `false`**; there is no SQL trigger on the table and it is the only `pg_proc` naming it, and the **sole** writer of `healthy=true` is the probe at `check_endpoint_health_action.go:138`. **So any single refused call can stop the whole fleet's dispatch, and nothing that succeeds can restart it** — the recovery path is unrelated to the failure that set it. **Consequence for anyone fixing this: an "N consecutive failures" rule belongs on the LIVE-TRAFFIC writer (`ai_actions.go`), NOT on the prober**, which is where the 08-17 addendum's first suggested shape aimed it and where it would never fire
- **relations:** `bugs_open/243` (the cap this is downstream of) · `bugs_open/244` (the spend that triggers the cap) · LANDMINES "A stopped queue provokes exactly the kind of activity that makes the aggregate look alive" (the sibling shape, one level up) · MEMORY [[a-plausible-external-cause-is-when-to-doubt-your-instrument]]
- **added:** 2026-08-17, webdesign_uk_build_service lane

## A parked `field_updates` payload is a FULL-FIELD REPLACEMENT frozen at the moment it was computed — applying it later silently reverts every change made to that field since, and both the item and the apply report success

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/section_editor_actions.go` (`applyContentEdit`, the `for k, v := range updates` merge at :746-748) · `apply_section_edit` · `site_work_items` rows whose `spec` carries `field_updates` (`section_edit`, `content_edit`, `copy_edit_proposed`) · `checkpoint_for_review` (`on_approve`) · any item parked at `needs_human_review` holding a proposed edit · `copy_quality_two_stage/gate_stage2_edit.py`
- **fires when:** you approve or hand-apply an edit that was proposed earlier — an hour, a day or a fortnight earlier — because a human had to look at it first. **The merge is per-FIELD, not per-change**: every field the payload NAMES is overwritten wholesale with the value captured when the proposal was written. If anything rewrote that field in between (a rerender, an improvement sweep, another lane's `content_rewrite`, a regeneration off a corrected plan), the apply throws it away and restores the older text. Nothing errors: `apply_section_edit` reports success, `content_edit_mode: field_updates`, `updated_field_count: 1`, the item completes, the page renders and deploys. **The reverted copy is well-formed and plausible, which is why nobody notices.**
- **why the review queue makes this the DEFAULT case, not an edge case:** the whole point of `checkpoint_for_review` is that time passes between proposing and applying, and `bugs_open/033` means that time is unbounded — 735 items sit at `needs_human_review`, the oldest from 2026-03-15. An estate that reviews before applying is an estate whose payloads go stale by design.
- **worse on a single-field component, which is common:** where a component declares ONE field (e.g. `ported-prose` declares only `content`), "the fields being edited" IS the whole component, so a stale payload reverts everything — headings, links, markup and all. The blast-radius argument for preferring `field_updates` over `replacement_content_data` (PLAN §9) buys exactly nothing there, and PLAN §10 already withdrew the stronger claim.
- **the check, before applying ANY parked edit:** re-grade against the CURRENT row, never against the payload's own record of what it edited. The proposal's stored "before" is the trap — it will agree with itself for ever.
  ```sql
  -- did the field move after the proposal was written?
  SELECT pc.updated_at AS component_changed_at, swi.created_at AS proposal_written_at,
         pc.updated_at > swi.created_at AS PAYLOAD_IS_STALE
    FROM site_work_items swi
    JOIN page_components pc ON pc.id = (swi.spec->>'page_component_id')::uuid
   WHERE swi.id = '<item>';
  ```
  A `t` in the last column means re-run the proposer, not the applier. `gate_stage2_edit.py --item <id>` does this the honest way round — it loads the component's live `content_data` as the "before", so a stale payload shows up as dropped links, lost classes or vanished figures rather than as a clean pass.
- **do NOT reach for `stop_reason` when checking whether the proposing call was truncated** — `llm_call_log` has no such column. Compare `output_tokens` against the step's configured `max_tokens`; equality means the completion was CUT and the payload may be a fragment that will still apply cleanly.
- **AND THE ADDRESS GOES STALE TOO, not just the content (added 2026-08-18, same lane).** A rerender does not update the component row — it **replaces** it with a new `id`. The proof case's `page_component_id` `d6c9198b…` was gone within a day, replaced by `f05d59e5…` at 09:55:37Z with `created_at = updated_at` (the content came through intact). So a parked proposal can hold a **dangling** `page_component_id`, and a tool that resolves it reports `no page_component <id>` — which reads like a typo or a bad copy-paste, not like "a rerender happened here". Resolve a parked edit by **(page_name, slot_name)** and treat the stored id as a hint: 016b §9's rule, arriving from the proposal side rather than the repair side. `CQ-023`'s classifier already keys this way and says why; anything that stores an id for later must expect it to die.
- **source:** 2026-08-17, `copy_quality_two_stage` — found while writing the apply instructions for stage 2's first proposal (`copy_edit_proposed` item `6dce90f1`, computed against a component that had been byte-stable for five days, which is what made the risk visible rather than what made it real). Register `CQ-024`; the re-grade step is step 1 of that lane's `HANDOFF_2026-08-17`.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/033` (the queue that makes payloads old) · `bugs_open/260` (the retype hazard on the same merge) · `bugs_open/238` (save REPLACES / rerender MERGES — the sibling shape one level up) · MEMORY [[a-stale-page-holds-every-improvement-since-it-rendered]] · MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]]
- **added:** 2026-08-17, copy_quality_two_stage lane

### `create_work_item` with no `status` key births the row at 'triaged' — an item whose TYPE says needs_human_review still DISPATCHES
- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/create_work_item_action.go` (`status` default), any `agent_definitions` step whose `action` is `create_work_item`, `site_work_items.status`, `handler_agent`
- **fires when:** you write or copy a `create_work_item` step config for a parked/human-facing item and set `item_type` to a state-sounding word (`needs_human_review`) without an explicit `"status"` key — or you name a `handler_agent` you have not checked against `agent_definitions`. The filed item LOOKS right (row exists, type says human review, workflow reports success) and is actually in the dispatch queue: the omitted status defaulted to `'triaged'`. If the handler is also unregistered, the item detonates to `blocked` at claim (or, since commit `c8400e452` rolled, at the write door) and pins its dedup slot so later findings for the same key are silently dropped — `bugs_open/291`: tool-auditor bled 14 real findings this way over 3 days, and the wrong shape had been copied onward once already ("matches the existing pattern") before it was caught
- **the tell:** none at filing time, which is the point — `item_created` reports success either way. Later: rows at `status='blocked'`, `error='Handler agent not registered: …'`, `created_by` = your producer
- **the check:** in the step config, always set `"status"` explicitly. To park for a human: `"status": "needs_human_review"` and NO `handler_agent` (migration 217 idiom; the relaxed validation accepting that shape from config rolled with `c8400e452` — on an older binary a parked item must still name some inert handler, which is exactly how the phantom spread, so check the binary first). To dispatch: name a handler and prove it exists — `SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='<handler>' AND deleted_at IS NULL);` — the docs' item-type tables are where `hitl-review` lived for four months as if real

### Firing `build-site-planner` at an ADOPTED site rewrites `pages.url`, CLEARS `pages.sections` and INSERTS canonical-name twins — and `honour_realised_identity='true'` alone did NOT stop it

- **footprint:** `agent_definitions` `type='build-site-planner'` (steps `reconcile_site_plan`, `validate_plan`, `write_site_plan`, `sync_pages` — 14 in all), `platform/orchestration/actions/write_site_plan_action.go:487`, `site_identity_policy.go` (`siteIdentityPolicyFor`, `honour_realised_identity`, `twin_identity_snap`, `stem_twin_snap`), `normaliseRealisedToPlanPage` / `parentSectionFromURL` in `v3_site_actions.go`, `datahelpers.CanonicalisePage`, `pages.url`, `pages.sections`, `site_nav_items.url`, `loancalculator_couk/canary_replan_407.sh`
- **fires when:** you replan ANY site the platform adopted rather than built — a D6-style "teach the planner what this site is" run, a `recompose_pages` release, or a canary after widening the planner's menu. The trap is about the WRITE-BACK, not the plan: a plan can be faithful and the sync still moves the site.
- **the tell: none from the run, which reports COMPLETED, and none from a page count.** Measured 2026-08-17 on `loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk` (corr `6fe6ee93`, chassis `v1.0.1305`, 3m19s): the plan was *exactly* right in shape — 45 pages, role mix `tool 19 / guide 13 / content 9 / blog-post 2 / section-index 1 / landing 1`, identical to the live census — while the same run **INSERTED 19 twins** (`mortgages-stamp-duty` beside a new `tool-mortgages-stamp-duty` at `/tools/mortgages-stamp-duty/index.html`), **moved 21 real URLs** (`/guides/x.html` → `/guides/x/index.html`, `/loans/index.html` → `/loans.html`), **cleared `sections` to `[]` on 24 real pages**, and **repointed 2 of 5 `site_nav_items` at URLs with no deployed file**. Page count went 45 → 64, which reads like the growth an improvement loop produces.
- **the check, and do it BEFORE you fire, because afterwards a digest tells you only that *something* moved:**
  1. **Measure the fixed-point population first.** Call the real `datahelpers.CanonicalisePage` over the live page list through the descriptor `write_site_plan_action.go:487` builds — `Role`=stored `page_type`, `Slug`=`firstNonEmpty(slug,name)` (a realised page has no slug, so it is the stored NAME), `ParentSection`=`parentSectionFromURL(url)`, `FlatURLs`=`siteUsesFlatURLs`. **Never re-derive the rule in SQL** (`bugs_open/215`'s own note). Put a positive AND a negative control in the harness — a canonical page that must not move, a legacy page that must — or "nothing moved" and "the harness canonicalises nothing" print identically. On this site: **7 fixed points of 45; 38 moved; 17 by name, every one a calculator.**
  2. **Snapshot `pages` and `page_components` into bak tables**, and record `md5(name||'|'||url||'|'||page_type||'|'||status)` ordered by name. Assert the digest inside the repair transaction, not after it.
  3. **Cancel the run's `needs_rerender` item before anything claims it** — "assemble and deploy pages after plan reconcile" is what turns a DB-only mistake into a deployed one. On this run nothing had claimed it, and the live site was untouched throughout (real URLs 200, twin paths 404).
- **what SAVED this site was `rebuild_policy='owned'`, not the identity flag:** all 17 owned calculator pages came through unmodified — the run filed an `owned_page_review` item per page instead. The 24 pages it mutated were the `generic` ones. So a site whose pages are all `generic` has no such floor.
- **⚠ FIXED IN CODE 2026-08-20 — read this before acting on any line below it.** The hole the 08-19 sharpening describes is closed: `reconcilePlanWithRealised`'s Pass B2 now stamps the realised identity for a plan entry that names a realised page by its **exact stored name** (`stampSameNameRealisedIdentity`, `v3_site_actions.go` — anchor on the symbol, this file's line numbers have drifted ~300 twice in a week). Council APPROVED round 1, corr `27cccfbd-3bf5-4744-a9f6-a5602e38cd30`; commit `75f0b9920` plus the code half inside another lane's `80b9c6235`. **So `honour_realised_identity` ALONE is now the correct and sufficient configuration for this shape, and the snap layers stay OFF** — they carry the false-positive risk and buy nothing here. ⚠ **INERT UNTIL THE CHASSIS ROLLS**, and no live re-plan has been through it, so before firing at an adopted site: probe both replicas for the literal `PLAN_PAGE_SAME_NAME_TWIN_PENDING` with a one-letter near-miss negative control and an older literal (`PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY`) as the instrument positive. Until that probe passes, every step below still applies in full. **Two things the fix does NOT cover, so the pre-fire census is still owed:** a realised row whose `build_status` is outside `{deployed, needs_rebuild}` on a site with a current plan is invisible to the reconciler entirely and its twin is still mintable (`bugs_open/340`), and a same-name pair whose roles disagree is deliberately REFUSED and recorded as `PLAN_PAGE_IDENTITY_TYPE_CONFLICT` rather than stamped.
- **⚠ AND DO NOT TAKE THE 08-19 ADDENDUM'S CANDIDATE (1) — it is an INERT EDIT.** That write-up (and this entry's sharpening below) name the `eligible` closure's `rname == lname` clause as the thing that declines a correctly-named page, and candidate (1) proposed dropping it from the canonical layer. **[MEASURED by mutation 2026-08-20]** the closure holds two refusals in series and the second subsumes the first — a candidate whose name equals the plan entry's name is necessarily a name the plan carries, so `planNames[rname]` fires wherever `rname == lname` would. Removing either clause alone leaves the whole package suite green; removing both is what changes behaviour. Anyone taking candidate (1) would have shipped a no-op, re-measured, found the counters still zero, and had **no way to distinguish an inert edit from an empty population** — which is this entry's own trap one rung down. The description of the hole below is right; only the proposed remedy was wrong.
- **⚠ SHARPENED 2026-08-19, and this REPLACES the remedy in the line below: NEITHER snap layer could have prevented the twins, so "seed the snap layers" is the wrong fix.** All three twin layers share one `eligible` guard (the closure inside `matchTwinIdentity`, `v3_site_actions.go` ~`:6091` at 2026-08-19) which returns false when `rname == lname` — i.e. **when the planner names the page CORRECTLY.** Our run's stored `validate_plan` output carries the realised names exactly (`mortgages-stamp-duty`, not a variant), and the plan entries carried no URL, so path-key was skipped and canonical-name and stem-twin both declined; the twin was then minted DOWNSTREAM by the canonicalisation the layers exist to predict. Corroborated by a measurement that reads as nothing until you know it is durable: `recordIdentitySnaps` writes one `agent_error_log` row per twin event (three `PLAN_PAGE_*` codes) *because a chassis pod retains under a second of log* — and there are **ZERO of all three fleet-wide, all time** (only 2 × `PLAN_PAGE_MERGE_LOSSY`, 08-11). The code IS live: controlled `/proc/1/exe` probe on `v1.0.1314`, positive control PRESENT and negative control ABSENT, all four subject literals PRESENT. **So the narrow statement of the hole: the layers cover a page named DIFFERENTLY from its stored name; a page named CORRECTLY whose stored name is not a canonical fixed point is unreachable by all three, and `honour_realised_identity` can never fire for it.** On this site that is 17 of 45 pages. Addendum filed to `bugs_open/215`.
- **⚠ RESOLVED SAME DAY (2026-08-17, and the entry below is superseded by this line): the flag has an undocumented PRECONDITION — it is inert unless a SNAP or a UNION paired the page first.** `v3_site_actions.go `reconcilePlanWithRealised` (:6616 at 2026-08-19; was :6476 on 08-17 — anchor on the symbol)` strips `identity_authority` from every LLM page and it is *"re-stamped only by a snap or a union"*; with `twin_identity_snap` and `stem_twin_snap` absent, nothing re-stamps it, `realisedIdentityOf` returns `ok=false`, and `honour_realised_identity` is never reached. Established from the run's own `collected_data->'validate_plan'->'pages'` (realised names present, marker/url/parent_section absent, `sections: []`), `reconcile_result.pages_restamped: 0`, and the plan's URLs landing at the role's DEFAULT hub (`/tools/…`) rather than the realised parent (`/mortgages/…`) — that hub is the positive discriminator. **So seed all three switches together, and note the damage originates at the PLAN WRITE, not at `sync_pages`.**
- **⚠ superseded, kept for the shape of the mistake — the flag was ON.** `honour_realised_identity='true'` was verified live in the current structure row before the fire, and the twins were minted anyway. **Cause NOT established, deliberately** — the pairing layers `twin_identity_snap`/`stem_twin_snap` were absent on this site (the firing session's own "one canary, one question" choice, and the prime suspect: honouring a realised identity cannot help a plan page the reconciler never marked `identity_authority='realised'`), and whether the site-spec reader is in the running binary could not be settled (the sha probe of `/proc/1/exe` returned absent for its **negative control** too, so it was uninformative, not negative; the startup provenance line had scrolled). **So do not read this entry as "the flag does not work" — read it as "the flag was not sufficient on its own here, and one canary should not have been asked to answer a compound question."** 090 run correlation `33d4d7bc-62f8-4886-a8e2-7c39f0c0a302`.
- **the empty sections are a separate, older mechanism:** the plan carried 10 sections in total, all for the four pages the framework itself had built; the 41 adopted pages got none. Their slots are positional (`prose-0`, `tool-1`), which are neither a component `name` nor a `function` — `bugs_open/204`'s blindness, reaching the plan-write path on a site where 204's own fix is live. **Not `bugs_open/282`**, which is about tool-LEVEL functions missing from validate's resolver; a slot name that names nothing cannot be rescued by accepting the menu.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/215` (the twin-minting mechanism + this lane's contribution), `bugs_open/204` (positional slots), `bugs_open/241` (the URL-move hazard, measured the other way round on the sibling), `bugs_open/282`, LANDMINES "Re-adopting a site silently drops the `structure` spec's opt-in flags" (same spec row, different way to lose the same protection), `loanandmortgagecalculator_couk/NOTES_…md` entry 2026-08-17 (d) for the full account and the repair transaction
- **added:** 2026-08-17, loanandmortgagecalculator D6 planner lane

### The database is UTC and your shell is BST — so "how long has this been stuck?" done by eye is an hour wrong, and the wrong answer is a plausible incident

- **footprint:** `orchestration_states.last_activity` / `created_at` / `updated_at`, `scheduled_tasks.last_triggered_at` / `last_completed_at`, `site_work_items.updated_at`, any `::timestamp(0)` you print, and the shell's own `date`
- **fires when:** you are watching something live — a sweep, a dispatch, a scheduled task — and you compare a timestamp psql printed against the clock in your terminal to judge whether it is progressing. No symptom first: both numbers are correct, and neither is labelled.
- **the trap:** `psql` prints UTC (`current_setting('TimeZone')` = `UTC` on `postgres-clients-0`); the shell's bare `date` prints **BST = UTC+1** for the British summer. So a row that last moved **two minutes ago** reads as **sixty-two** minutes ago, and one that moved forty minutes ago reads as a hundred. **The failure is one-directional and always toward alarm** — the DB timestamp always looks older than it is, so healthy work reads as stalled, and a scheduled task that is on time reads as overdue.
- **the tell: there isn't one, and the false reading is internally consistent.** Measured 2026-08-17: an `improvement-loop` sweep at `call_dispatch` since `12:25:11` looked, against a shell clock reading `13:27`, like a **72-minute stall** — which is exactly what `bugs_open/294`'s "stalled in RUNNING and unreachable by every recovery path" looks like, so there is a bug file waiting to confirm the mistake for you. The true idle time was **2 minutes 28 seconds**. Nothing about the numbers announces the offset; a stalled sweep and a healthy one differ only by the hour you did not add.
- **the check — never subtract across the two clocks; make the DATABASE do the arithmetic:**
  ```sql
  SELECT current_step, status,
         now() - last_activity AS idle_for      -- one source of truth, both operands
    FROM orchestration_states WHERE ...;
  ```
  `idle_for` is computed entirely inside the DB, so the offset cannot enter it. If you must print a wall-clock time next to a DB one, print `now()` from the DB in the **same query** as the row, so the reader sees both from one clock. And when you want the shell's clock for a note, use `date -u` — never bare `date`.
- **the wider rule:** this is the [MEASURED]-marker discipline one level down. A dated figure is only evidence if the two things being compared came off the same instrument; here the marker rule is satisfied in full — both timestamps are real, current and correctly read — and the *comparison* is still meaningless. **Before subtracting two times, ask which clock each came from.**
- **relations:** `bugs_open/294` (the stalled-orchestration bug this mimics, and the reason the false reading is believable), `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-17, LANDMINES "A `090` diagnosis run … looks exactly like a run still in progress" (same shape: a healthy state and a broken one made indistinguishable by a missing piece of context)
- **added:** 2026-08-17, vigilant_designer_offer_analysis lane, caught mid-sweep before it reached the owner

## A new action's optional keys are counted as ZERO by the RFC_022 budget cron until someone regenerates its literal — and the test that catches it lives in a package nobody runs

- **footprint:** `deployments/kustomize/services/optional-key-budget-check/base/check.py` (`OPTIONAL_KEY_COUNTS`) · `cmd/config-key-audit/optional_budget_cron_parity_test.go` · `docs024_key_docs_latest/architecture_review/optional_key_budget_acks.json` · adding or widening any `ActionInputSpec.Optional` · adding a NEW registered action
- **the trap:** the daily budget check runs a **python** script from a ConfigMap, so it cannot read the Go registry; it carries a hand-generated literal of every action's optional-key count. An action added to the registry but not to that literal is counted as **ZERO optional keys** — permanently invisible to the accumulation check RFC_022 exists to provide, while the cron keeps writing a clean `doc_notes` row every morning. `[MEASURED 2026-08-17]` two actions were in exactly that state (`retract_asset_files` 4 keys, `publish_site` 3, both read as 0). The parity test that catches it, `TestBudgetCronCountsLiteralMatchesTheRegistry`, **was failing at HEAD and had been for days** — it sits in `cmd/config-key-audit`, a package no ordinary change touches, and the pre-commit hook does not run it.
- **the second half of the trap: fixing the FILE does not fix the CLUSTER.** The literal ships as a ConfigMap; editing `check.py` and committing leaves the running CronJob on the old ConfigMap. `kubectl apply -k deployments/kustomize/services/optional-key-budget-check/overlays/production/uk_001` is what moves it, and the check is at the LIVE object: `kubectl -n ai-persona-system get configmap $(kubectl -n ai-persona-system get cronjob optional-key-budget-check -o jsonpath='{.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.volumes[?(@.name=="check-script")].configMap.name}') -o jsonpath='{.data.check\.py}' | grep '"<your_action>"'`.
- **the check, whenever you touch an ActionInputSpec:** `go test ./cmd/config-key-audit/` — it is two seconds and it is the only thing that compares the two. Regenerate with the command in `check.py`'s own comment (`go run ./cmd/config-key-audit --specs | python3 -c ...`), then apply, then verify at the ConfigMap.
- **why a clean run is not reassurance here:** the cron reports per-action counts from the literal, so an unlisted action cannot appear over budget however wide it grows. The failure mode is an absence inside a green report — the same shape as this file's `write_audit_findings` entry, one layer up.
- **source:** 2026-08-17, while verifying RFC_022 for the owner (who had asked for the counter to be BUILT — it already was; CLAUDE.md's clause was three days stale and is now corrected). Found by running the parity test rather than trusting the cron's clean row.
- **relations:** `RFC_022` · register **WFA-013** · `optional_key_budget_acks.json` (the acknowledgement source of truth, mirrored by the same literal mechanism) · MEMORY [[detection-works-schedule-and-dispatch-do-not]] and [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]]
- **added:** 2026-08-17, RFC_022 verification

## `make -n release` descends into NOTHING, so "is my service in the release?" answers 0 whether it is or not

- **footprint:** `makefile` (`release`, `release-backend`, `pinned_sweep`, `deploy-core`, `deploy-agents`, `update-kustomization-images`) · any verification of the form `make -n release | grep <service>` · `bugs_open/237`, `bugs_open/249`
- **fires when:** you change what a release deploys — adding a service, changing a tag-update list, wiring a gate — and you check your work by dry-running the release. No symptom first; the command succeeds and prints plausible output.
- **the trap:** `release` used to be a plain prerequisite list, so `make -n` walked into every sub-goal and printed the real actions. Since `21b9772a9` (the `bugs_open/249` fix) it is `$(call pinned_sweep,…)` — **one shell block** that loops `make $$goal` internally. Under `-n`, make prints that block and executes none of it, so the entire release expands to **three lines of shell**. `make -n release | grep -c render-audit-adapter` returns **0** at a HEAD where render-audit-adapter is fully wired into the release and rolls correctly — `[MEASURED 2026-08-17]`, on the very commit that wired it.
- **why it is worse than a plain false negative:** the recipe is written down as a *passed* check. `bugs_open/237`'s own 2026-08-10 verification table records "`make -n release` reaches the render-audit overlay → **3** actions", and that was true *the day it was written* — 249 landed the next day and silently invalidated it. So the file hands the next reader a check that now returns 0, and 0 reads as "my change is not in the release", which invites re-fixing something that is already right. The failure is one-directional and always toward "absent".
- **the check — measure at a goal the sweep CALLS, never at `release` itself:**
  ```bash
  make -n deploy-agents | grep -c render-audit-adapter          # the retag loop
  make -n deploy-core   | grep -c "Release coverage OK"         # the gate, via update-kustomization-images
  ```
  and prove the instrument can fail: break the input and require the opposite answer —
  `make -n deploy-core AGENT_DEPLOY_SERVICES="agent-chassis"` must print `RELEASE COVERAGE:` failures.
- **the related half:** `make -n` does not expand a **shell `for` loop** either. Now that the release's service lists are loops (`AGENT_DEPLOY_SERVICES`), counting `make -n deploy-agents` action lines reads **9** where the old copy-pasted blocks read **37**, and the sets are identical. Never compare those counts across the refactor — compare the **resolved service set** (run the loop under `kubectl`/`sed` stubs, or expand the make variable and test each overlay path), which is what the two numbers were always standing in for.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/237` (the enumeration class; its own verify recipe is the worked casualty), `bugs_open/249` (`pinned_sweep`, the change that broke it), `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-17, MEMORY [[measurement-discipline-index]] and [[a-pass-from-a-blind-check-outlives-the-blindness]] (a check that passed while blind, quoted afterwards as evidence)
- **added:** 2026-08-17, bugs_open/237 class-fix lane — caught because a check that had "passed" for another session returned 0 on a tree where the thing it tests demonstrably works

## A deploy that restarts the pods can ship NO NEW CODE — same `IMAGE_TAG` serves the node's CACHED image, so "a fresh build was deployed" and "your commit is live" are unrelated facts

- **footprint:** `makefile` (`IMAGE_TAG`, ~line 16), `make build-*` / `push-*` / `deploy-*`, `make release`, `kubectl -n ai-persona-system get pods -l app=<service>` (replicaset hash + age), `/proc/1/exe`, any sentence of the form "a fresh build has been deployed"
- **fires when:** someone (owner or session) builds and deploys **without bumping `IMAGE_TAG`**. Kubernetes sees the same image reference, the node reuses the layer it already has, and the rollout is REAL — new replicaset, new pod names, fresh ages, healthy status — while the binary inside is the previous one. Every surface that normally means "new code shipped" is telling the truth about the ROLLOUT and nothing about the BYTES
- **the tell:** none from the outside, and three separate signals actively mislead — new pod names, recent `startTime`, and a successful deploy event. Measured 2026-08-17: pods ~92 min old on a NEW replicaset hash, tag still `v1.0.1305`, running binary still commit `6a782274b` (the same one as that morning), with **203 commits in HEAD but not in it**, including a great deal of `platform/` code from several lanes. Everyone's Go work that day was inert; every lane's config work was live, because `agent_definitions`/migrations do not care about the image — **that split is what makes it so confusing: your config change behaves and your code change does not**
- **the check — and the control is the load-bearing half:** probe for a SPECIFIC sha, never discover one, and run BOTH controls in the same breath:
  ```bash
  kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec deploy/<service> -- grep -aq "$(git rev-parse <previously-confirmed-commit>)" /proc/1/exe  # POSITIVE: must MATCH if unchanged
  kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec deploy/<service> -- grep -aq "deadbeef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef" /proc/1/exe        # NEGATIVE: must be ABSENT
  kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec deploy/<service> -- grep -aq "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" /proc/1/exe                            # the question
  ```
  then `git merge-base --is-ancestor <your-commit> <the stamp>`. **⚠ THE NEGATIVE CONTROL MUST BE CAPABLE OF BEING ABSENT.** On 2026-08-17 I used a 40-zero string as the "must be absent" control and it **MATCHED** — every binary contains a run of zeros — so that entire probe could not discriminate and its five "absent" readings were worthless. A control that is present in every possible world is decoration, not a control. Use a plausible-but-fake hex sha. This is the sibling of the filed trap where a discovery grep for "some 40-hex string" matches Go's internal digit table
- **prevention, not detection:** bump `IMAGE_TAG` for every build (the makefile line says so and this is what it is for), or `make release REF=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` which pins one revision across the sweep
- **source:** 2026-08-17, webdesign_uk_build_service lane — found while checking whether an owner-announced "fresh chassis build" carried the day's platform work. It did not
- **relations:** LANDMINES "A 'FIXED AND LIVE on v1.0.NNNN' close-out EXPIRES" (the same tag lying in the other direction) · "one release can straddle several revisions — compare LABELS, not the tag" · CLAUDE.md "Bump `IMAGE_TAG` for every build" · MEMORY [[a-fresh-deploy-can-ship-no-new-code]] · [[prove-a-deploy-at-the-artefact-index]]
- **added:** 2026-08-17, webdesign_uk_build_service lane

### A same-tag rebuild leaves the OLD binary running under new pods — and the one-command proof is the image DIGEST, not the tag, the pod age, or the deploy event
- **footprint:** `makefile` `IMAGE_TAG` (~line 16), `make build-*` / `push-*` / `deploy-*` / `release`, `kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{...imageID}'`, `docker inspect --format '{{json .RepoDigests}}'`, any question of the form "is my Go fix live?"
- **fires when:** anyone builds and deploys WITHOUT bumping `IMAGE_TAG`. `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` + an unchanged tag means the node keeps serving its CACHED image for ever: new replicaset, fresh pod start times, a real deploy event, and **not one line of new code**. Measured twice independently on 2026-08-17 — one lane found the running chassis was still commit `6a782274b` with **203 commits in HEAD but not in it**; this lane found its own guard absent from the running binary while the LOCAL image of the same tag contained it. Config work (`agent_definitions`, migrations) is live regardless, which is what makes it confusing: your config behaves, your code does not
- **the tell:** none — every surface says "deployed". The startup `build provenance` line is a STARTUP line and has usually scrolled on a busy service, so its absence reads as "unstamped" rather than "out of range"
- **the check (10 seconds, no exec, no `strings`): compare the two digests.**
  `docker inspect aqls/<svc>:$TAG --format '{{json .RepoDigests}}'` (what your build produced)
  vs `kubectl -n ai-persona-system get pods -l app=<svc> -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.containerStatuses[0].imageID}'` (what is RUNNING).
  **Different digests under the same tag = your code is not live**, whatever anything else says. Worked case 2026-08-17: local `sha256:6039e19c…` vs running `sha256:f90a7e88…`.
  If you probe the binary instead, **the negative control must be capable of being absent** — a control of 40 zeros MATCHES every Go binary, so that run cannot discriminate and its "absent" readings are worthless; use a plausible fake (`ZZZ_NOT_A_REAL_SYMBOL_<bug>`, `deadbeef1234…`) and run a positive control in the same breath
- **the fix:** bump `IMAGE_TAG` for EVERY build (it is `?=`, so `make release IMAGE_TAG=v1.0.<next>` works without editing the file). Releases are whole-fleet and owner-run — do not paper over it with a one-service apply at the same tag, which re-serves the same cache
- **CHEAPER STILL, added 2026-08-17 (third independent hit, `bugfix_281`/loop-engine lane): the image TELLS you its commit — read the OCI label, do not probe the binary.**
  `docker inspect aqls/<svc>:$TAG --format '{{json .Config.Labels}}'` returns `org.opencontainers.image.revision` (the exact build commit) and `…image.created`. **It works on the RUNNING image too**, addressed by digest, which is the whole answer in one command:
  `docker inspect aqls/<svc>@sha256:<the imageID from kubectl> --format '{{index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision"}} {{index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.created"}}'`
  Then `git merge-base --is-ancestor <your-commit> <that revision>`. This **retires the "walk back from the tip probing candidate commits with `grep -acF`" recipe** in the sibling entry below (the one-sha stamp trap) for any case where the image is locally addressable — there is nothing to guess and no control to get wrong, because the label is not a heuristic.
  Worked case, same day: running `sha256:f90a7e88…` → revision `6a782274b`, created `2026-08-16T21:53:27Z`; local `v1.0.1305` → revision `89a0cbeb7`, created `2026-08-17T14:30:02Z`. **252 commits in HEAD absent from the running binary, 24 touching `platform/`/`internal/`/`pkg/`** across bugs 275/283/285/287/289/291/292/293/295/299, several already council-APPROVED.
- **HUMAN VERIFICATION SUPPLIED 2026-08-17 16:35Z.** The landmine-verifier returned `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` on this entry, and correctly: its code index holds `.go` files only, so the `makefile`, the `docker inspect`/`kubectl` commands and `imagePullPolicy` — the primary footprint — are all outside its scope (it did confirm the entry internally consistent, and found the Go-side `image_tag` handling matches). **Those unverifiable parts were measured by hand the same hour** and are the worked pair recorded above: running digest `sha256:f90a7e88…` → revision `6a782274b` (2026-08-16 21:53Z) vs local `v1.0.1305` `sha256:6039e19c…` → revision `89a0cbeb7` (2026-08-17 14:30Z), `makefile` line 17 read as `v1.0.1305` and now `v1.0.1306`. **Note for anyone reading a verifier verdict on any entry: `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` from a `.go`-only index is a statement about the INDEX, not a doubt about the entry** — an entry whose footprint is shell, SQL, YAML or a makefile can never come back `STILL_VALID`, so treat that verdict as "unchecked here" and check it yourself.
- **THE SECOND-ORDER DAMAGE, added 2026-08-17 night (`299` skipped-render-audit lane): a CLOSE CRITERION run against the cached binary fails, and the failure reads as "my fix does not work".** This is the direction that costs real work, because every other symptom of this trap looks like *nothing happening* whereas this one looks like *evidence against your change* — and the natural response is to go and "fix" code that was already correct, or to reopen a bug that was already closed. It is the exact inverse of the false-green this estate usually guards against: a **false RED**, manufactured by the deploy layer, landing on a change that has already passed review. Worked case the same day: `bugs_closed/299`'s criterion (a page-less-site dispatch) would have failed at 14:43Z on `v1.0.1305` for reasons having nothing to do with the fix; run at 18:23Z on `v1.0.1307` — tag bumped, both replicas probed with a positive AND a negative control first — the identical dispatch completed on the normal edge with the honest no-op. **So the ordering is not optional: prove the binary carries the change BEFORE you run the grading dispatch, never after, because a criterion is only a measurement of your code once you know your code is what is running.** Corollary for the bug file you are about to write: "inert until the next roll" is a dependency phrased as a schedule — the condition is *a build whose tag differs from the deployed one*, and `grep '^IMAGE_TAG' makefile` beside `kubectl get deploy -o custom-columns=…IMAGE` answers it in two commands (`WRONG_CALLS.md`, same date).
- **this entry existing did not stop it — the remedy is a manual act, and nobody had done it.** The trap fired a THIRD time on 2026-08-17 at 14:43Z: pods were re-rolled at the SAME `v1.0.1305` after the entry above was written, and the owner was told twice that a fresh build was deployed. `makefile` line 17 is now `v1.0.1306` (committed `aa9c7b74f`, with the measurement in the message). **So: if you are the one who notices, BUMP THE TAG in the same session — reporting it is not fixing it**, and the next same-tag roll erases the evidence that anything was wrong.

### The council gate REFUSES a config-only migration, and the refusal reads as "this is out of scope" when the ruling meant docs

- **footprint:** `097_TRIGGER_council_review_v1.sh` (`SCOPE_RE='^(platform|internal|pkg)/'`),
  any submission whose edits are all `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/NNN_*.sql`,
  any bug fixed by an `agent_definitions` migration alone
- **fires when:** your fix is config-only — you rewrite a live agent's step in
  `agent_definitions` and change no Go — which is a large share of this estate's bug
  fixes, since DB config is live on apply and needs no roll.
- **the tell:** none you would distrust. The script `exit 2`s with
  `REFUSED: no edit touches the review scope (platform/, internal/, pkg/ — owner ruling
  2026-07-17)` / `Docs and site content do not spend council credits.` It is a stated
  owner ruling, quoted accurately, and your paths really are under `docs/`. So the
  natural reading is "the council does not cover this change" — and you skip the round,
  correctly following a rule that was never aimed at you. **A refusal that cites a real
  ruling is far more convincing than a bug, and there is no second signal to contradict
  it.**
- **why the reading is wrong:** the filter is a PATH filter standing in for an INTENT —
  keep docs and site content from spending credits. A migration under
  `sql_for_agents/` is neither: it rewrites what a live agent DOES, with no image
  rollback and no roll to gate it, so it reaches production faster than any Go change.
  And it is empirically the shape this gate catches things in: in `bugs_open/275`'s
  round the sharpest objection of the whole round (`bug_historian` — an unmarked column
  truncation, a silent cap one level down) was against the MIGRATION half, not the Go
  half, and it changed the fix.
- **the check:** decide by what the edit CHANGES, not by where the file sits. If the
  submission rewrites live agent behaviour, submit it with `FORCE=1` **and say so in the
  first paragraph of the rationale** — the script prints
  `WARN: FORCE=1 — submitting despite no in-scope files`, which no reviewer sees, so an
  unexplained force looks like someone dodging the filter. Reviewers judge the plan
  against the rationale; the scope note belongs there. Conversely `FORCE=1` is NOT a
  licence for docs: if what you changed is prose, the refusal is right and the credits
  are better spent elsewhere.
- **added:** 2026-08-17, `bugfix_297_tool_recreation_context` lane (migration 453, corr

> ### ⚠ THE CRONJOB FACE OF THIS, added 2026-08-20 — a DAILY job makes it invisible
>
> Everything above is about a Deployment you can look at. On a **CronJob** the same trap has no
> observer at all: the job runs once a day, exits 0 (or 1 for findings), writes its report row, and
> **reports findings computed by whatever binary the node had cached** — the schedule, the history and
> the doc_notes row all look exactly as they should.
>
> It fires the moment a check image is enrolled in `RELEASE_IMAGES` / `AGENT_DEPLOY_SERVICES`, because
> a fleet release then REBUILDS it **at the tag the overlay already pins**, and the default policy for
> a pinned tag is `IfNotPresent`. **Measured 2026-08-20:** a fleet sweep repinned four check overlays
> to `v1.0.1320` while one of those services' code had moved to `v1.0.1322`; the live CronJob was
> already serving the older image, and nothing in the CronJob, the Job history or the report said so.
>
> **the check — probe the BEHAVIOUR, never the tag,** because the tag is what lied. Pick a
> discriminator only the new code can produce (a new column in its report, a count only the new logic
> yields) and fire a manual run:
> ```bash
> make <check>-now
> kubectl -n ai-persona-system logs -l job-name=<the job> --tail=400 | grep -E '<discriminator>'
> ```
> In the measured case the new binary reported `9 of 25` with a `regulatory (left alone)` column and
> the old one reported `12` with no such column — one grep, decisive.
>
> **the fix, and it belongs in the base manifest rather than in a habit:** `imagePullPolicy: Always`
> on any CronJob whose image rides a shared tag sequence. One pull a day is not a cost worth defending
> against, and it removes the only version of this trap nobody is watching.

  `4b9265c3`), after reading the enforcement block rather than the header comment —
  the header says "is refused", line 146-153 is where it `exit 2`s.
- **✅ FIXED 2026-08-19 (`bugs_open/314`, owner direction) — the gate now ADMITS appliable
  migrations without `FORCE=1`.** `scripts/council-scope.sh` is the single source of the scope,
  read by 097 (admission), `scripts/council-coverage-nudge.sh` (the commit-msg nudge) and 098
  (the coverage report) — three hand-maintained copies before this. In scope now:
  `platform/`/`internal/`/`pkg/` **or** `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/NNN_name.sql`. Still
  refused, and controlled for: prose, site content, and the SQL that is NOT the change
  (`_ROLLBACK`, `_VERIFY`, `_SUPERSEDED`). ⚠ **`_HOLD.sql` IS in scope** — the first cut
  excluded it by reusing the runner's `SIDECAR_RE`, which answers *"will `--apply` run
  this?"*, as a proxy for *"is this the change?"*. A `_HOLD` is held back for ORDERING and
  applied BY HAND (see this file's own `_HOLD` entry at the `--no-probe` check), so it is
  live config reaching production — exactly what this fix exists to catch. Caught by the
  council's editquality seat at medium severity, corrected 2026-08-20; the drift guard now
  censuses the directory for UNCLASSIFIED suffixes rather than only confirming a copy. `DRY_RUN=1 ./097_TRIGGER_council_review_v1.sh <sub.json>` decides admission
  and stops, so admission is testable for free in both directions.
  **What is left of this entry, and it still bites:** the FORCE-and-say-so rule above is
  unchanged for everything the widening does NOT cover — a submission whose edits are all
  *tooling* (`scripts/`, the 097/098 scripts themselves under `docs/`), all prose, or all
  sidecars is still refused, correctly, and still needs the force explained in the first
  paragraph of the rationale. The fix for this entry was itself submitted that way.
  Also: 098's pathspec now over-selects `sql_for_agents/` and applies the exact predicate as a
