- **the check, before you file a markup-handling tool:** count the pairs in any candidate template — `for p in '<script' '<style' '<div' '<section' '<fieldset'` compare against the closing form. **Both live tools of this class pass with EXACTLY ZERO MARGIN**, surviving only because the generator wrote its regex as `/<(pre|textarea|script|style)\b[^>]*>/`, an alternation group in which the substring `<script` never occurs. Write the same regex as `/<script[^>]*>/` and the identical tool becomes unbornable. **Zero margin means this is not a comfortable pass, it is one word from rejection.**
- **the workaround that works today:** put a constraint in the `add_tool` description itself — refer to elements by NAME ONLY in comments and visible text (never with angle brackets), always write tag names inside an alternation group in regexes, and never build tag strings by concatenation. That is a prompt-level dodge of a code defect, not a fix.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/303` (this, with fix candidates and a verification recipe) · `bugs_open/046` / `021` INSTANCE 1 / `012` (the real truncation class the guard exists for — it is right to exist; this is a precision defect) · `bugs_open/024` (the previous misclassification in the OPPOSITE direction, which is why `toolTemplateValid` was split from `sectionTemplateValid`) · `architecture_review/RFC_036` (the other birth-time blocker: three uniqueness gates on one INSERT) · CLAUDE.md "`output_tokens == max_tokens` means the completion was CUT" — **the converse does not hold, and this entry is the counter-example**
- **added:** 2026-08-18, `webdesign_tool_rebuilds` lane (hit while acting on an owner bug report — the fix path is exactly where this bites hardest)
- **remedy status (2026-08-18, `bugfix_303_tool_birth_guard` lane):** ~~FIXED AT SOURCE, NOT YET LIVE~~ **LIVE 2026-08-19 on `v1.0.1314` (build `d3590ca46`, binary-probed both replicas; all fix commits ancestors) — THIS ENTIRE ENTRY IS NOW HISTORICAL and the workaround is RETIRED.** All the counting above is markup-context (`content.StructuralTagCounts`, commits `6d962bcf8` + `e21b172f0`, register CLC-019): mentions in scripts/comments/regexes no longer count, the refusal message states measured per-pair counts, and the ADDENDUM class (tools that OUTPUT a script tag) needs no concatenation obfuscation — pinned by test. **Stop writing the no-angle-brackets constraint into `add_tool` descriptions.** Two tools born post-roll, zero refusals with demand present; full close-out in `bugs_closed/303`. ⚠ One instrument refinement from verifying this: when you binary-probe with a must-miss control, **never use 40 zeros as the control — it HITS legitimately in Go binaries** (measured 2026-08-19 on agent-chassis; WRONG_CALLS). Use a high-entropy sha that is in no repo.

## Cancelling a site's queued work items does NOT stop the build — and the deploy is in the PAGE BUILDER, not the rerender

- **footprint:** `site_work_items` · `page-build-handler` · `platform/orchestration/actions/retract_page_deployment_action.go` · `scripts/initial_messages/020_build_pipeline/082_submit_domain_unified.sh`
- **fires when:** you need to stop a build that is already running — a wrong direction, a
  compliance problem, a runaway cost — and you reach for the queue.
- **why the wrong result looks right:** setting the pending items to `cancelled` returns a
  satisfying `UPDATE 33` and the queue then reads clean. Two things are still moving.
  (1) An item another agent has already **claimed** runs to completion; cancellation only
  stops an item being picked UP. Measured 2026-08-18 on loanzy.uk: 33 items cancelled
  13:57:24Z, one already-claimed page deployed **14:01:55Z**, four minutes later, straight to
  the public edge. (2) Holding `needs_rerender` holds nothing — **`page-build-handler` has its
  own `deploy_page` step**, so each page publishes itself as it finishes; the rerender is a
  site-level pass, not the publication gate.
- **the check:** before believing a build is stopped, ask what is still in flight —
  `SELECT item_type,status FROM site_work_items WHERE site_id=… AND status IN
  ('claimed','in_progress')` — and treat anything claimed as already gone. To know where
  publication actually happens for any handler, read its step list rather than the pipeline
  diagram: `SELECT jsonb_object_keys(default_config->'workflow'->'steps') FROM
  agent_definitions WHERE type='<handler>' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false`.
  If a page must not reach the public, the only reliable hold is arranged BEFORE dispatch
  (no worker route / a domain that does not resolve) — a queue edit is a race you may lose.
- **and when you do have to unpublish:** `page-retraction` **refuses a live page** ("page is
  active — retracting a live page is not what archiving means"). Archive the row first
  (`UPDATE pages SET status='archived' …`; there is no writer, it is hand-run), then dispatch
  the retraction. Its `success:true` names a git delete in `gqls/sites`, NOT the edge — a
  bucket sync and cache purge follow, so verify at the URL and expect minutes.

### `md5sum` on a deployed binary cannot tell you WHICH SOURCE it was built from — Go builds are not byte-reproducible across build environments, and the mismatch looks exactly like a failed deploy

- **footprint:** `docs024_key_docs_latest/webdesign_uk_build_service/box/chat-service/` · `/usr/local/bin/sitechat` on `webdesign.vs.mythic-beasts.com` · `make box-verify` / `box-release` / `box-status` · any `md5sum`-based "is my build live?" check on a binary you did not just push · RUNBOOK "One binary, several sites"
- **fires when:** you want to know what a deployed binary was built from, and reach for the obvious check — rebuild the commit you believe is live, `md5sum` both, compare. It is the check the runbook told you to use.
- **the tell: none, and it points the wrong way.** A mismatch reads as "the deploy did not land" or "someone deployed something else", when the truth can be "same source, different build environment". Measured 2026-08-18: rebuilding the EXACT commit behind the live binary (`84202f061`) gave md5 `65da9971` and **9381552** bytes against the box's `f07fb146` and **9381544** — eight bytes and a different digest from identical source. Absolute build paths and toolchain differences get into the binary; `-trimpath` narrows this but does not guarantee it across machines.
- **what md5 CAN do, and only this:** prove that the file now on the target is the file you pushed **in this same session**, because it is literally the same bytes copied. That is worth checking (it catches a failed scp or an install to the wrong path) and it is NOT provenance. Do not let a passing md5 check stand in for "the right code is live".
- **the check: make the binary say what it was built from, then ask it.** Stamp at link time — `go build -trimpath -ldflags "-X main.buildCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` — and log it at startup in the SAME line shape the backend fleet uses (`build provenance: git_commit=<sha>`), so one grep idiom works everywhere: `journalctl -u <unit> -o cat | grep 'build provenance'`. An unstamped build must SAY `unstamped`, never print an empty commit, or "no stamp" and "stamped empty" become indistinguishable. Verify the stamp reached the binary with **both controls in the same breath**: the real sha must be PRESENT and a 40-zero sha must be ABSENT — 40 zeros matches Go's internal digit table on every binary, so a discovery grep gives the same wrong answer every time.
- **the general form:** this is the VM-side instance of the fleet rule "prove a deploy at the artefact, never at git or the tag", and it is worse here than in k8s: there is no image digest and no `org.opencontainers.image.revision` label to fall back on, so an unstamped VM binary has NO provenance at all and the digest that looks like one is not one.
- **relations:** MEMORY [[prove-a-deploy-at-the-artefact-index]] · [[a-fresh-deploy-can-ship-no-new-code]] · the LANDMINE above on `strings`/discovery greps and 40-zero controls
- **source:** 2026-08-18, webdesign_uk_build_service lane, found while proving the ROLLBACK path before overwriting the live chat binary — i.e. by checking a thing nobody had thought to check, not by a failure. Fixed in `main.go` (`buildCommit`) + makefile `box-build`/`box-verify`; RUNBOOK corrected in place
- **added:** 2026-08-18, webdesign_uk_build_service lane

## A site's `voice` spec never reaches the writer — it feeds the DETECTOR, so careful register guidance written there changes what gets FLAGGED, not what gets WRITTEN

- **footprint:** `site_specs` aspect `voice` (also `tone_of_voice`, `voice_and_tone`) · `platform/orchestration/actions/write_site_plan_action.go:161` · `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/check_voice_tells.go:238` · `page-content-writer`'s `input_fields` (`site_specs`) · `llm_call_log.prompt_rendered` · any task of the form "set this site's tone/register properly"
- **fires when:** an owner or a lane specifies a register ("friendly and expansive, not dense", "direct, anti-hype, no vendor-speak") and you encode it in the site's `voice` spec — the obviously-named place, already populated on many sites, and listed in the writer's own `input_fields` via the bulk `site_specs` field. The spec saves, `is_current` flips, the row looks live and authoritative, and **the writer never sees it.** The next build produces copy in whatever register it was already producing, and the only visible consequence is that `check_voice_tells` starts flagging the mismatch — i.e. the spec makes the DETECTOR complain about output the spec was supposed to prevent.
- **the tell:** the spec is present and current, the copy is unchanged, and voice-tell findings go UP rather than down after you set it.
- **the check — read the artefact, and bring a positive control** `[MEASURED 2026-08-18: 0 of 1,338]`:
  ```sql
  SELECT count(*) AS calls,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE prompt_rendered ILIKE '%tone_guardrails%')   AS voice_spec_present,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE prompt_rendered ILIKE '%key_differentiators%') AS control_identity_present
    FROM llm_call_log
   WHERE agent_type = 'page-content-writer' AND success AND created_at > now() - interval '7 days';
  ```
  `voice_spec_present = 0` while `control_identity_present > 0` is this landmine. **The control is not optional** — without it a zero reads as "my LIKE pattern is wrong" and the finding evaporates; with it, identity data demonstrably reaches the same prompts and the absence is real.
- **where register actually lands, in order of measured force:** `identity.key_differentiators` (drives the LEAD — a differentiator written as a subtraction produces copy that leads with a loss) · `content_direction.example_phrases.characteristic` (**exemplars beat rules**; and the writer reads `content_direction.formatted`, NOT the array, so editing the array alone is inert) · `strategy`. The fleet house voice is separate again: one row in `agent_default_configs.voice_style_block`, injected only into templates naming `{{.voice_style}}` (CQ-022).
- ⚠ **Two neighbouring aspects are entirely dead:** `tone_of_voice` and `voice_and_tone` have **zero references** in `platform/` or `internal/`, yet sites carry them as current rows (finetuning.uk has all three). Writing into either is inert with no signal at all — worse than `voice`, which at least drives detection.
- **source:** 2026-08-18, `copy_quality_two_stage`, answering `finetuning_uk_service`'s question "is friendly-expansive encodable in the spec rather than per edit?" — the answer is yes, but not in the aspect named after it. Related: `bugs_open/305` (the fleet voice block did not reduce define-by-negation either: 2.72 → 2.85 per 1,000 words across the v2 flip).
- **relations:** MEMORY [[a-dead-config-key-looks-like-a-live-one]] · [[grep-the-config-key-before-calling-it-a-win]] · [[a-print-statement-is-not-a-config-row]] · CQ-017 (per-site voice specs) · CQ-020 (`ScanVoiceTells`) · CQ-022 (the fleet carrier)
- **added:** 2026-08-18, copy_quality_two_stage lane

### A `_HOLD` migration you hand-apply can NEVER be ledger-recorded — the runner refuses to record any sidecar, so `schema_migrations` says "unapplied" for ever and its `doc_notes` row is the only record

- **footprint:** `scripts/migration/run-migrations.sh --record-only`, `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/NNN_*_HOLD.sql`, `schema_migrations`, `doc_notes`
- **fires when:** you follow the house pattern in full — hold the ordering-critical half as `NNN_name_HOLD.sql` (the entry above), apply it by hand at the right moment, then reach for `--record-only` because the migration practice says recording is part of applying. **The runner refuses:** `ERROR: '<file>' is an UPPERCASE-suffixed sidecar (rollback/verify), not a migration. Sidecars are never applied by the runner, so recording one is meaningless.` That is deliberate — `SIDECAR_RE` is one regex serving two different populations, ROLLBACK/VERIFY files (which genuinely must never be recorded) and HOLD files (which are real migrations that WILL be applied, just not by the runner). Measured 2026-08-18 on `455_repair_287_..._HOLD.sql` after a clean hand-apply (UPDATE 35, verify passed).
- **the tell is a FALSE NEGATIVE, and it points the dangerous way:** `schema_migrations` has no row, so every later reader — a session checking "did this land?", a coverage sweep, you tomorrow — reads an applied, live, verified change as **pending**. The natural next move is to apply it again. A well-fenced file survives that (replay = `UPDATE 0`); a file whose fence is weaker, or whose side effects are not idempotent, does not. On 2026-08-17 the same call was ALSO refused by the session harness's permission classifier, which is a different cause with the identical symptom — so "permissions" is a red herring you can waste a cycle on.
- **the check, before you go looking for a permissions problem:** `./scripts/migration/run-migrations.sh --record-only <file>` on any `_HOLD` name is *structurally* impossible; do not retry it, do not hand-write the `INSERT` (the practice forbids that for good reasons). Instead **make the file record its own application**: every HOLD migration should carry a fenced `INSERT INTO doc_notes …` naming the file, what it changed and what was verified — `452_build_dispatch_loop_result_goes_strict_HOLD.sql` and `455_repair_287_spawn_record_results_HOLD.sql` both do, and those rows are now the audit trail for both. Then say so in the file header, because the next reader will check the ledger first and find nothing.
- **query that answers "was this HOLD file applied?" without the ledger:** `SELECT created_at, left(body,80) FROM doc_notes WHERE body LIKE '## <NNN>:%' ORDER BY created_at;` — plus the change's own live evidence (for a config flip, read `agent_definitions`; for a data repair, count its provenance key: `result ? '_repaired_by'`).
- **the fix nobody has built yet, stated so it can be:** either split `SIDECAR_RE` so `_HOLD` is applyable-by-hand-and-recordable while `_ROLLBACK`/`_VERIFY` stay unrecordable, or give the runner a `--record-only --force-sidecar` arm. Until then this is a permanent gap between the migration practice ("recording is part of applying") and the tooling, and the gap is silent.
- **source:** `bugs_closed/287` (spawn_record) lane, 2026-08-17/18 — hit on `452` (misdiagnosed as a permissions block, corrected in that file's header) and then reproduced deliberately on `455`. Extends the `_HOLD` entry above, which specifies the naming but not what recording does afterwards.
- **verified (HUMAN, 2026-08-18) — because the automated verdict could not have been anything else.** The landmine-verifier returned `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` and said why: *"the critical footprint items (run-migrations.sh, SIDECAR_RE regex in the shell runner, --record-only flag, _HOLD.sql files, schema_migrations table) all live in .sh/.sql files outside the .go-only code index and could not be checked. No contradicting evidence found; entry is internally consistent."* Its corpus is **7,859 `.go` symbols at the last pushed tip** — a footprint made of a shell script, a regex, a CLI flag, filenames and a DB table is unverifiable there **by construction**, so this verdict is a coverage statement, not a doubt. First-hand checks, all run at HEAD on the live cluster: (1) `scripts/migration/run-migrations.sh:65` — `SIDECAR_RE='_[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*\.sql$'`; (2) same file `:246` emits the refusal verbatim (`ERROR: '$f' is an UPPERCASE-suffixed sidecar (rollback/verify), not a migration.`), and it fired on a real `--record-only` for `455_..._HOLD.sql` **after** that file had applied cleanly; (3) `SELECT count(*) FROM schema_migrations WHERE filename LIKE '452%' OR '455%'` → **0**, while both changes are live and verified; (4) their `doc_notes` audit rows exist and are the trail (`## 452:` 2026-08-17 16:28:57Z, `## 455:` 2026-08-18 16:20:18Z); (5) `schema_migrations.checksum` is an **md5** — `448`'s row is `75426e00b63fb5620fffc67ac602d456` and matches `md5sum` of the file byte-for-byte, which is why editing a recorded migration (even a comment) drifts it and why `448` keeps a stale doc pointer deliberately.
- **added:** 2026-08-18, bugfix_287_spawn_record lane

### `site_work_items` is a ~7-DAY WINDOW, not a history — `work-item-archiver` moves terminal rows to `site_work_items_archive`, and the archive is BIGGER than the live table

- **footprint:** `site_work_items` · `site_work_items_archive` · `scheduled_tasks.work-item-archiver` · any "has this ever…", success-rate, lifetime-count or first-time-ever query over work items · `scheduled_tasks.detected-item-promoter` pre_query · migrations `430`, `444`, `454`, `465`
- **fires when:** you write `FROM site_work_items` and mean *history*. `work-item-archiver` is **enabled**, runs daily, and its description is explicit: *"Archives terminal work items older than 7 days to `site_work_items_archive`"*. [MEASURED 2026-08-18] archive **20,184 rows**, live **8,702** — so the majority of the history is in the other table and every "lifetime" figure taken from the live table alone is really "the last 7 days".
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** the query is well-formed, the number is plausible, and it **drifts downward on its own with no code change** — a pair read 11 complete / 13 failed one morning and 3 / 12 that afternoon. Worse, it fails *asymmetrically*: a busy pair keeps its recent rows and looks fine, while a **good but quiet** pair loses everything and reads as *never having worked*.
- **it had already caused live damage:** the `detected-item-promoter`'s known-good rule held `empty_internal_href → page-build-handler` as "never completed" while that pair held **nine** lifetime successes (0/1 = 0% live vs 9/5 = 64% true); `empty_section → page-build-handler`, a **316**-success workhorse, read as marginal at 43% against a true 91%.
- **the check:** for any lifetime claim, query both — `SELECT … FROM site_work_items UNION ALL SELECT … FROM site_work_items_archive`. And **before trusting any absence** (`0 rows`, `never happened`, `first time ever`), ask whether the thing you are looking for would be older than 7 days and terminal.
- **⚠ the searches that will NOT find this, all three tried 2026-08-17 and all three came back clean:** `grep -rn "DELETE FROM site_work_items"` (the archiver **moves** rows, it does not delete), grepping the `scheduled_tasks.pre_query` column (the archiver's `pre_query` is **NULL** — it is `fire_message=true`, so its SQL lives in an agent definition), and grepping for `retention` (its description says *"Archives"*). Read `scheduled_tasks.description` for the whole `maintenance` group instead.
- **⚠ and the control that cannot come out otherwise:** *"the oldest surviving row fleet-wide is 2026-03-15, so there is no systematic sweep"* — that row is **non-terminal**, and the archiver only takes terminal ones. An oldest-row check is blind to a status-scoped sweep by construction. Scope your control to the same statuses the sweep takes.
- **relation:** the fourth member of one family on this table — `failed` rows carry no `completed_at`; `verified` is a second terminal success status; the row set is not stable; the row set is only a window. All four are **a population assumed rather than enumerated**, and none was caught by council review (12 seats approved `444`).
- **source:** 2026-08-18, `bugfix_277_required_fields_repair` lane. Filed `[UNDIAGNOSED]` on 08-17 after the three failed searches above; found by noticing `work-item-archiver` in an unrelated list of `maintenance` group-mates in migration `458`'s header. WRONG_CALLS 2026-08-18.
- **added:** 2026-08-18, bugfix_277/083 lane

### `kubectl get pods` always shows pods that started minutes ago, because most of the fleet is EPHEMERAL — so "it just rolled" is what a listing looks like even when no image has been built

- **footprint:** `kubectl -n ai-persona-system get pods` (any deploy verification) · `.status.startTime` · `agent-build-dispatch-loop-*` / `agent-page-build-handler-*` / `agent-css-patch-agent-*` / `agent-component-creator-*` / `agent-page-content-writer-*` and the other per-job handlers · `IMAGE_TAG` (makefile) · `git merge-base --is-ancestor`
- **fires when:** you are told a fresh build has been deployed, or you are checking whether your own fix is live, and you look at the pod list. **52 of the namespace's pods run the `agent-chassis` image** and most are spawned per job and exit, so the newest start times are always a few minutes old and the fleet looks freshly rolled continuously.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** on 2026-08-18 the five newest pods in the namespace had started **55 minutes after** the running build's commit was made — `agent-page-build-handler`, `agent-css-patch-agent`, `agent-build-dispatch-loop`, `agent-component-creator`, `agent-page-content-writer` — and every one of them was on the **OLD** tag. There had been no build at all. The tell is negative and easy to miss: **the two long-lived `agent-chassis` pods had not restarted** (same names, same `startTime` as hours earlier). A same-tag restart is also indistinguishable from a roll in a listing, and CLAUDE.md's warning that a same-tag rebuild ships the node's stale cached binary is the neighbouring trap.
- **the check, and it is cheaper REVERSED than the way everyone writes it:** do not ask "is my commit in the stamp" — ask whether **the stamp is an ancestor of your commit**:
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <the stamp> <your commit> && echo "the build was cut BEFORE your code existed"`. One exit code, no controls needed, and it settles it: if the build's own commit predates yours, nothing further can make your code present. (`f0117fb8b` at 16:26 vs the fix at 17:28, 46 commits between.) Corroborate with `grep -m1 '^IMAGE_TAG' makefile` — an **unbumped** `IMAGE_TAG` means no build was cut, since every build must bump it.
- **the stamp itself must come from the BINARY, not the log:** `kubectl exec <pod> -- sh -c "grep -oa 'buildinfo.GitCommit=[0-9a-f-]*' /proc/1/exe | head -1"`. See the sibling entry on why grepping the log for `build provenance` returns another lane's payload — and note that the pods which actually ran your code may already be gone, so a log-based proof of *execution* has the lifetime of an ephemeral pod.
- **source:** 2026-08-18, `bugs_closed/293` lane, on the third "a fresh chassis build has been deployed" notice of one thread — the first two carried new code and this one carried none, and only the ancestry check separated them
- **added:** 2026-08-18, bugfix_293_whole_page_shrink_axis lane

### The estate's config checks carry a registry COMPILED INTO the binary — so a frozen image has a frozen INVENTORY, and the check reports clean about the actions it cannot see

- **footprint:** `cmd/config-key-audit` · `datahelpers.ListActionInputSpecNames` · `datahelpers.RegisterActionInputSpec` · `datahelpers.ListDeclaredConfigKeys` · `datahelpers.ListRemovedConfigKeys` · CronJobs `removed-config-keys-check` / `shared-output-fields-check` / `component-render-check` / `verifier-remit-check` · `deployments/kustomize/services/*-check/overlays/production/uk_001/kustomization.yaml` · `build/docker/backend/*-check.dockerfile` · any "the daily check found nothing" claim
- **fires when:** you take a clean run from one of these CronJobs as evidence about the estate — or you register a new action and assume the daily checks now cover it. `cmd/config-key-audit` drives its whole audit from `ListActionInputSpecNames()` (`main.go:277`, with `ListDeclaredConfigKeys()` at `:229` and `ListRemovedConfigKeys()` at `:260`). That list is built by ~169 `RegisterActionInputSpec(...)` calls **compiled in at build time**. An action registered after the image was built is not in the list, so the loop never visits it — `GetActionInputSpec` returns `!ok` and the code `continue`s at `:297-300` with **no output**.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** a check that skipped a third of the estate and a check that found nothing wrong emit the **same empty report**. There is no "N actions skipped" line, no warning, no non-zero exit. And the reports accumulate: every clean run vouches, retrospectively, for actions the binary could not look at. [MEASURED 2026-08-18] `removed-config-keys-check` (v1.0.1285) carries **165 of 169** production actions, `shared-output-fields-check` (v1.0.1265) **161 of 169**, `component-render-check` (v1.0.1258) **160 of 169** — and all four ran that morning on those tags, unsuspended. `publish_site` and `retract_asset_files` are absent from **all four**.
- **⚠ these images are frozen BY CONSTRUCTION, and the release-coverage gate cannot see it.** `make check-release-coverage` fails a release only when an overlay pins an image **the release builds**; these four pin images the release does not build, so they are outside its predicate. Each overlay was written once, on the day its service was created, and never again. Do not read a green coverage gate as covering them (`bugs_open/237`, Decision B).
- **the check, and it is a DELTA so it can come out either way:**
  ```bash
  acts () { git grep -h -A1 'RegisterActionInputSpec(' "$1" -- platform/ internal/ \
            ':(exclude)*_test.go' | grep -o '"[a-z0-9_]\+"' | tr -d '"' | sort -u; }
  acts HEAD > /tmp/h; acts <build-commit> > /tmp/b; wc -l /tmp/h /tmp/b; comm -23 /tmp/h /tmp/b
  ```
  `<build-commit>` = the commit that last touched that service's overlay (`git log -1 -- <overlay>`), which for these four is also the day they were created. Equal totals ⇒ the registry was quiet and the question is closed.
- **⚠ two ways to get this census wrong, both of which produced a wrong number first:** (1) **`':(exclude)*_test.go'` is mandatory** — test-only registrations (`test_action_removed_keys`, `strict_marker_test_action`, `test_validator_removed_*`, …) are ~22% of the raw count and are in no shipped binary; without the exclusion HEAD reads **201**, not 169, and four of the "missing" names are obviously fixtures. (2) **`-A1` is mandatory** — five non-test registrations wrap the action name onto the next line, so a same-line grep undercounts by five. Run both ways: here the *missing sets* came out identical, and that robustness is what licenses the figures.
- **⚠ and a count inherited from a LINKED package is not a property of the service.** `verifier-remit-check` also reads 165/169, and it is the **least** affected of the four: it links the package that holds the registry but never reads it, references only two internal symbols, and **neither definition has changed** since it shipped. Before acting on one of these numbers, grep the service's own `cmd/` for `datahelpers.`/`actions.` and confirm it actually consumes the thing you measured.
- **⚠ the Dockerfile `CMD` is the whole behavioural difference between two of them.** `shared-output-fields-check` and `removed-config-keys-check` are the **same binary** (`cmd/config-key-audit`) under different `CMD`s (`--shared-output-fields --report --ack …` vs `--removed-keys-in-use --report`); neither CronJob sets `args`. So "has this service's own `cmd/` directory changed?" is ambiguous for both — `cmd/config-key-audit` is shared with `optional-key-budget-check` too — and a wrong `CMD` would be invisible in the kustomize manifests. Read `build/docker/backend/<svc>.dockerfile` before reasoning about either.
- **prove the freeze at the cluster, not the repo:** `kubectl -n ai-persona-system get cronjob -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,SUSPEND:.spec.suspend,IMAGE:.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image,LAST:.status.lastScheduleTime'`. The overlay is what *would* be applied; this is what *is*. The same command resolves the neighbouring confusion — the estate's other daily checks (`optional-key-budget-check`, `single-owner-carriers-check`, `concept-register-drift-check`, `component-fallback-check`, `site-discovery-staleness-check`) run **`postgres:16-alpine`** with their logic in SQL/ConfigMap, carry no build of ours, and are a **different** staleness mechanism (the ConfigMap literal — see the `check.py` note in CLAUDE.md).
- **relation:** the same two actions, `publish_site` and `retract_asset_files`, are ALSO the pair CLAUDE.md records as having "entered the registry counted as **ZERO**" for `optional-key-budget-check` — a wholly independent mechanism (a hand-maintained literal in `check.py`, with its own parity test `cmd/config-key-audit/optional_budget_cron_parity_test.go`). **Two unrelated blind spots landing on the same pair is the signal:** both fail whenever the registry grows, and neither announces it. If you add an action, assume no daily check covers it until you have checked both paths.
- **source:** 2026-08-18, `bugs_open/237` Decision B costing (`docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_237_release_enumeration/`). Found by reading `main.go` rather than diffing it — the 2026-08-17 sizing had correctly narrowed the risk to "a shared helper they link has moved", which is true and still understates it: a stale helper might compute the right answer, a stale *inventory* never asks the question.
- **verifier note:** the footprint is part Go (`cmd/config-key-audit`, `datahelpers.*`) and part not (CronJobs, overlays, Dockerfile `CMD`s), so expect a partial or `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` verdict on the non-Go half. The hand-run check is the census block above, and it is cheap.
- **added:** 2026-08-18, bugfix_237_release_enumeration lane

### A scheduled task's "N-day limit" is really N-to-N+1 days, and predicting the day it fires from a DATE is off by a full tick — the miss looks exactly like the task being broken

- **footprint:** `scheduled_tasks` · `scheduled_tasks.interval_seconds` · `scheduled_tasks.last_triggered_at` · `held-pair-canary-escalation` · `detected-item-promoter` · `work-item-archiver` · `stuck-task-reaper` · `claimed-item-timeout` · any `pre_query` containing `now() - interval` · any handoff sentence of the form "expect X to fire on \<date\>"
- **fires when:** you predict *when* a periodic task's age-based predicate will next select a row, and you compute it as `(oldest + interval)::date`. A task can only act **on its own tick**. `held-pair-canary-escalation` has `interval_seconds=86400` and last fired at **12:57:48 UTC**, so it evaluates `min(created_at) < now() - interval '3 days'` **once a day at 12:57** — a row created at 19:17 is 6h20m short of three days at that moment and waits a **further full day**. The stated limit is 3 days; the delivered limit is anywhere in **[3, 4) days**, set by the offset between the row's creation time and the task's tick phase.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** the prediction fails as a **silent zero**. On the day you were told to watch, the task runs, correctly escalates nothing, and logs `escalated=0` — which is indistinguishable from the task being broken, from the migration not having applied, and from the rows having been fixed. There is no "not yet due" line and nothing errors. [MEASURED 2026-08-18] a handoff in the `277/083` lane predicted `placeholder_contact` would escalate 08-19 and `literal_markdown` 08-20; the true first ticks are **08-20 12:57** and **08-21 12:57**. Both were written as instructions to the next session.
- **the check — predict the TICK, never the date, and it can come out either way:**
  ```sql
  SELECT name, to_char(last_triggered_at,'MM-DD HH24:MI') AS last_tick, interval_seconds,
         to_char(last_triggered_at + (n || ' seconds')::interval * interval_seconds,'MM-DD HH24:MI') AS tick
  FROM scheduled_tasks, generate_series(1,5) n WHERE name = '<task>';
  ```
  then ask, for each tick, whether the predicate is satisfied **at that instant** — `oldest < tick - interval '<N> days'`. Phrase the answer as *"the first tick that fires it is …"*, which forces the join between the clock and the predicate. **A predicted date with no time of day attached has not been computed against the thing that will run.**
- **⚠ the prediction is conditional on the selected set not changing, and the clock usually keys on an aggregate.** Where the predicate is `min(created_at)` over a *group* (as here — the clock runs on the pair, not the row), the oldest row leaving the selected status moves `min()` **later** and pushes the fire date **out**. So the tick you compute is the earliest it can fire, not a commitment.
- **⚠ do not "fix" this by shortening the limit.** The gap is phase, not threshold: with a daily tick, a 3-day and a 3.5-day limit fire on the same tick for most rows. If a deadline genuinely needs to be honoured to the hour, the task's interval is the thing to change, not its interval literal.
- **relation:** this is the same shape as the four traps already recorded in the `277/083` lane (`failed` rows carry no `completed_at` · `verified` is a second success status · the row set is not stable · the row set is only a 7-day window) — **a population or a domain assumed rather than enumerated.** Here the assumed domain is the **clock**. See `WRONG_CALLS.md`, 2026-08-18, "I predicted two escalation dates from DATES".
- **source:** 2026-08-18, `bugfix_277_required_fields_repair` lane, correcting its own `HANDOFF_2026-08-18b` §3.1 before the predicted day arrived
- **added:** 2026-08-18, bugfix_277_required_fields_repair lane

### `render_audit.py` prints "0 contrast failure(s)" and exits 0 for a page it never measured — and a snap-confined Chromium makes that the DEFAULT outcome

- **footprint:** `scripts/render_audit.py` · `internal/adapters/browserrunner/render_audit_action.go` (the Go port carries the same probe) · `/snap/bin/chromium` · any `CHROME=` override pointing at a snap · using the audit as a gate in CI or a pre-deploy check
- **fires when:** you run the render audit on a page to check what a visitor actually sees. It prints one ERROR line per page, then a summary that counts only the pages it DID measure, and returns 0. So the last thing on screen is *"1 page(s): 0 contrast failure(s), 0 broken image(s)"* — on a page it never looked at. As a gate it PASSES WHILE BLIND, which is worse than failing.
- **the mechanism, and why snap makes it the default:** the probe fetches the page, injects `AUDIT_JS`, writes the result to a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` (i.e. under `/tmp`) and renders `file://…`. **A snap-confined Chromium cannot read `/tmp`** — it renders its own error page instead, so the `AUDIT_RESULT` block is absent and every page returns `{"error": "probe produced no result"}`. Reproduce in one line: `/snap/bin/chromium --headless=new --dump-dom file:///tmp/x.html` returns Chrome's `<meta name="color-scheme">` boilerplate, while the identical file under `$HOME` returns its real content.
- **fixed 2026-08-18, both halves:** errored pages are now counted (`%d not measured`), printed as *"the zeros above are silence, not a pass"*, and included in the exit status; and the workdir is overridable with `RENDER_AUDIT_TMP=$HOME/…`. **The exit-status half is the load-bearing one** — the workdir will bite again on any confined browser, but a non-zero exit means it bites loudly.
- **⚠ and the fix does not make the tool work under snap.** Measured the same day: with `RENDER_AUDIT_TMP` under `$HOME` the probe STILL returned no result, so `file://` is not the only confinement in play. The route that does work is running the audit's own `AUDIT_JS` against the LIVE url over CDP (`docs/leopardessconsulting/scripts/audit_live.py`) — which is also more faithful, since it measures the served page rather than a re-injected copy of its HTML.
- **the check:** never read a render-audit zero without reading the line above it. `%d not measured` must be **0**, and `jq '[.[]|select(.error)]|length'` on the `--json` output must be 0 too.
- **source:** 2026-08-18, leopardess home-page presentation work; the first run reported a clean home page it had never measured, and the page it had not measured turned out to contain a genuinely invisible chart bar
- **relations:** MEMORY [[a-pass-from-a-blind-check-outlives-the-blindness]] · [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]] · register VIZ-010 / VIZ-012
- **added:** 2026-08-18, leopardess home-page lane

### `evidence-chart`'s `tone: "muted"` can render a bar that is INVISIBLE — the figure is right, the length is right, and the comparison the chart exists to make cannot be seen

- **footprint:** `content_components.function='evidence-chart'` · `site_specs.evidence_base.charts[].points[].tone` · `--color-secondary` · `.evidence-chart__bar--muted` · any site adding an evidence chart to a LIGHT section
- **fires when:** you copy the working chart shape from another site. `muted` is the natural tone for "the smaller, contextual bar", and it is what the only prior live example uses — but on fundamentallyai.com that bar's value is **0%**, so it draws nothing and its colour has never mattered.
- **the trap:** `.evidence-chart__bar--muted` is `background: var(--color-secondary, rgba(127,127,127,.6))`, drawn on a track of `var(--color-card-bg, rgba(127,127,127,.08))`. Where a site's `--color-secondary` is a pale tint, bar and track are the same value and **the bar reads as an empty track** — i.e. as "this figure is zero", the opposite of what it says. Measured live 2026-08-18 on leopardessconsulting.co.uk: a 937-against-2338 bar (40% of the track) was indistinguishable from empty next to a full-width black primary bar.
- **why nothing catches it:** the numeric label prints correctly beside the bar, so the page is factually right; the render audit measures **text** contrast and a bar is not text, so it passes; and the claims gate cannot see inside `<svg>`/graphical furniture at all (VIZ-009). Every automated check is green on a chart whose only job — the comparison — has failed.
- **the check:** after adding any evidence chart, **look at it** — clip-screenshot the `.evidence-chart` element itself, at 1280 and at 390 (`docs/leopardessconsulting/scripts/shot_clip.py`). If a bar's fill is not obviously distinguishable from its track, switch that point to `tone: "accent"` (`--color-accent`), which is a brand colour rather than a tint. Fix is one `jsonb_set` on the ASPECT (`site_specs.evidence_base.charts`), never on `content_data` — both `facts` and `charts` are aspect-sourced and a content_data edit is re-derived away.
- **source:** 2026-08-18, leopardess home-page presentation work — caught by eye, not by any check, one rerender after it shipped
- **relations:** register VIZ-001 / VIZ-009 / VIZ-011 (chart furniture and the 3.0 threshold) · LANDMINES "A `site_specs.<aspect>.<path>`-sourced field…" (the aspect-is-the-authority half) · the render-audit entry above
- **added:** 2026-08-18, leopardess home-page lane

### The Go constant is `PAUSED_FOR_HUMAN`; five production SQL sites guard `PAUSED_FOR_HUMAN_INPUT` — wire pause-for-human and its Kafka topics are deleted out from under it, silently

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/state.go` (`StatusPausedForHuman`) · `platform/orchestration/actions/cleanup_stale_topics.go` · `getActiveOrchestrationTopics` · `internal/core-manager/admin/topic_cleanup_handler.go` · `internal/core-manager/admin/dashboard_handlers.go` · `platform/orchestration/monitoring.go` · `orchestration_states.status` · any work wiring `pause_for_human_input`
- **fires when:** you implement or re-enable pause-for-human. You write the status through the constant — `StatusPausedForHuman OrchestrationStatus = "PAUSED_FOR_HUMAN"` (`state.go:28`) — which is the obviously correct thing to do. **Every production SQL site that is supposed to protect a paused run matches on the string `'PAUSED_FOR_HUMAN_INPUT'` instead, which that constant cannot produce.** [MEASURED 2026-08-18] five sites: `cleanup_stale_topics.go:209` and `:213` (topic protection, both halves of the UNION), `topic_cleanup_handler.go:85` (the admin path), `dashboard_handlers.go:353` (the active-workflow count), `monitoring.go:168` (the `paused` metric). `test/tools/db-inspector/check_state.go:127` uses `'PAUSED_FOR_HUMAN'` — **the test tool has the correct string and production has the wrong one.**
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** nothing errors and nothing is missing. A paused run's `requests_topic`/`responses_topic` simply fall outside the protected set, so the topic reaper deletes them as unreferenced — while the row sits in `PAUSED_FOR_HUMAN` looking perfectly healthy. The dashboard reports zero active workflows and the `paused` metric reports 0, both of which read as "nothing is paused" rather than "the query cannot see it". The failure surfaces later as an unexplained dead orchestration, nowhere near the string that caused it.
- **it is LATENT today, which is exactly why it is here rather than in `/bugs_open/`:** nothing writes the constant. `grep -rn "StatusPausedForHuman" --include="*.go" .` returns its definition and one e2e assertion (`test/e2e/scenarios/human_in_loop_test.go:107`); `pause_for_human_input` appears only in `platform/governance/fuel.go`'s cost table and a `contracts.go` doc comment, with no registered action; and `SELECT DISTINCT status FROM orchestration_states` returns six values, none paused. **So it cannot bite until someone wires the feature — and it bites that person, with no symptom to warn them.**
- **the check, before you write the first line of a pause implementation:** `grep -rn "PAUSED_FOR_HUMAN" --include="*.go" --include="*.sql" .` and read **both** spellings. Settle on one, change the other five sites in the same commit, and prove it at the artefact rather than by reading — park a disposable row in the status and confirm `getActiveOrchestrationTopics` returns its two topics. A grep for the constant alone will not find the mismatch, because the constant is not what is wrong.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/310` §"Adjacent finding" (filed there with the full site table) · `bugs_closed/294` (the same class: a status the recovery paths do not enumerate) · MEMORY [[a-doc-comment-is-not-an-enforcement-mechanism]] · [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]]
- **added:** 2026-08-18, bugfix_281_tool_audit_ported lane, found while enumerating the status vocabulary for `310`'s fix candidate 2

### An `orchestration_states` status census is a ~24 h WINDOW for `COMPLETED`/`FAILED` and a LIFETIME count for `INITIALIZED`/`CANCELLED` — the same `GROUP BY` mixes both and looks uniform

- **footprint:** `orchestration_states` · `database-cleanup` (`scheduled_tasks`) · any `SELECT status, count(*) FROM orchestration_states GROUP BY 1` · any per-agent success-rate or stall-rate computed from this table
- **fires when:** you census the table to size a problem — "how many runs stall?", "what fraction of X completes?", "is this status accumulating?". The `database-cleanup` task deletes `status IN ('COMPLETED','FAILED') AND updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'` and `status IN ('EXECUTING_STEP','AWAITING_RESPONSES') AND updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '4 hours'`. **It names no other status**, so `INITIALIZED` and `CANCELLED` rows are never deleted at all. [MEASURED 2026-08-18] `COMPLETED` reached back to 08-17 while an `INITIALIZED` row survived from **2026-07-13** and 24 `CANCELLED` rows from July — in one `GROUP BY` result that looks like a single population.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** every row is real and every count is correct. Nothing is NULL, nothing errors, and the numbers are plausible in both directions. A stall rate computed as `stalled / total` is wrong by the **retention ratio**, not by a little: the numerator is lifetime and the denominator is one day, so a rate that is genuinely ~0.1% can be computed as a catastrophic-looking figure, or a real accumulation can be dismissed as "only two rows" against a denominator that has been silently emptied.
- **the check — decide, per status, which side of the pruner it is on, and say so where you write the number.** Read the live predicate, never a migration file's intent: `SELECT pre_query FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE name='database-cleanup'`. Then bound each figure explicitly: `SELECT status, count(*), min(created_at), max(created_at) FROM orchestration_states GROUP BY 1` — **a `min(created_at)` far older than the retention window is the tell that this status is a lifetime count**, and one close to it is the tell that you are looking at a window and must not call it a total.
- **⚠ the corollary that bites hardest:** a rate needs its denominator taken from the *windowed* side and its numerator from the *same* window, or it needs a separate demand control. `310` states its stall rate as "~1 in 969, n=1" for that reason — 964 `COMPLETED` in the window is what makes two lifetime `INITIALIZED` rows interpretable, and without it the two rows would have read as a dead pipeline.
- **relations:** MEMORY [[measurement-discipline-index]] (a filtered count can ship inside a DENOMINATOR) · LANDMINES "`site_work_items` is a 7-DAY WINDOW" (the same shape, different table) · `bugs_open/310` · `bugs_closed/294`
- **added:** 2026-08-18, bugfix_281_tool_audit_ported lane

### A component with a `function` but no `section_type` is INVISIBLE to the selector and IMMOVABLE to the writer — the two halves key on different columns, and the site that loses is the SECOND one to want the tool

- **footprint:** `content_components.section_type` / `.function` · `platform/orchestration/actions/component_selector.go` (`SelectComponentByType`, `queryCandidatesBatch`) · `platform/orchestration/actions/store_generated_component_action.go` (`StoreGeneratedComponentAction`, `schemaFieldSet`) · `plan_sections_action.go:resolveSectionComponent` · `site_work_items` types `needs_new_component` / `needs_section_data`
- **fires when:** you plan a section on a NEW site whose name matches a tool or widget another site already has, or you seed a component and set only one of the two columns. You do not need a symptom: the trap is laid at seed time and springs on whoever builds next.
- **the mechanism, in one line:** selection reads `WHERE section_type = $1 AND component_level = 'section' AND is_active AND forked_from IS NULL` (`component_selector.go:186`); storage reads `WHERE function = $1 AND forked_from IS NULL` (`store_generated_component_action.go:229`). A row with `function` set and `section_type` NULL is missed by the first and matched by the second — so the planner is told "no such component, generate one", and the generated one is then refused for overwriting the other site's field contract. **No retry can ever succeed**, and the pair of errors points at schema fields, never at the column mismatch that caused it.
- > **CORRECTED 2026-08-19 (bugfix_311_component_keys lane) — the selector is not the FIRST resolver, and "no `section_type`" is not by itself what hides a row.** `plan_sections` Path 1 (`loadSectionComponents`, `v3_site_actions.go` pass 2) matches `function` directly, before the selector — a NULL-`section_type` row with a **valid** template resolves there and is NOT in this trap. The 2026-08-18 incumbents were hiding for a second reason: hand-seeded **tool-shaped** templates (no `</section>`, ending `</script>`) that `sectionTemplateValid` drops at load as "truncated", which is what routes the flow to the selector at all. **So do NOT "fix" a row in this trap by backfilling `section_type`** — for a guard-dropped row that makes the selector offer what the loader then refuses (`selector_error` → the section ships "as-is", a QUIETER failure than the work item you have today). The check stays the same two queries, plus one more column: `sectionTemplateValid` needs `html_template LIKE '%</section>%'` (or <100 chars) for `component_level='section'`. Cost of the incomplete version: fix candidate 2 in `bugs_open/311` stood for a day and would have shipped a harmful backfill. The DEADLOCK half is closed in code by CLC-020 (`resolveStorageIdentity`, store-side diversion) once a chassis image ships it.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** the guard that refuses is CORRECT and its message is accurate — it is protecting a real site's stored `content_data` from being stranded. Read at face value it says "your generated schema dropped 8 fields", which reads as a generation-quality problem and invites you to regenerate. Regenerating cannot work. Meanwhile the requesting site's page **builds and deploys with one fewer section**, `status='active'`, looking finished: a page with 5 sections instead of 6 has no tell in the artefact. Measured 2026-08-18: `remortgagecalculator.uk` — a site whose whole proposition is a calculator — served with no calculator, three identical rejections in its queue, and a live 200.
- **the check, before you plan or seed:** ask the two columns whether they agree, and ask who already depends on the row.
  `SELECT name, function, section_type, component_level, is_active FROM content_components WHERE function='<name>' OR section_type='<name>';`
  then `SELECT DISTINCT s.domain FROM page_components pc JOIN pages p ON p.id=pc.page_id JOIN sites s ON s.id=p.site_id JOIN content_components cc ON cc.id=pc.component_id WHERE cc.function='<name>';`
  **`content_components` has no `site_id`** — ownership is only visible through that join, which is precisely why the writer's lookup cannot see it is about to overwrite a stranger. A row returned by the first query but with an empty `section_type` is the trap, and the second query names the site that will win the collision.
- **the class is 26 wide and that is a floor** [MEASURED 2026-08-18]: of 140 active base `component_level='section'` rows, 26 carry no `section_type` (89 have `section_type = function`, 25 differ). A further 79 `component_level='tool'` rows are invisible to this selector by construction. **Check before concluding a component does not exist** — `remortgagecalculator.uk` generated against a collision while an active, section-typed `tool-mortgage-repayment` (10,760-char template, live since 2026-05-06) sat unused.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/311` (the full case, `090` verdict CONFIRMED) · `bugs_open/275` (tool-suggester's LIMIT 30 — the library is there and the site does not get it, different cause) · `bugs_open/283` (literal element ids block reuse on one page) · MEMORY [[a-helper-with-no-callers-is-not-a-refactor]] · [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]]
- **added:** 2026-08-18, portfolio_positioning lane, found because the owner noticed a calculator site had no calculator

### `rebuild_policy='generic'` answers ONE of at least **6** independent refusals in `save_page_sections` (as of 2026-08-18) — "so the rebuild will not be refused" is a non-sequitur, and it reads as a completed pre-flight check

- **footprint:** `pages.rebuild_policy` · `platform/orchestration/actions/save_page_sections_action.go` · `save_sections_shrink_guard.go` · `save_sections_component_floor.go` · `save_sections_prune_floor.go` · `single_slot_floors.go` · step config keys `section_shrink_floor` / `refuse_save_without_sections_metadata` · any sentence of the form "this page is `generic`, so the rebuild will go through"
- **fires when:** you are about to dispatch a rebuild or a section-writing save and you check whether the page is `owned`. It is the one gate everybody knows, it is genuinely necessary, and answering it feels like clearing the path. **You do not need a symptom** — the trap is that the check you ran was real and its answer was true.
- **the mechanism:** ownership is checked EARLY and refuses loudly, so it dominates the folklore. But `save_page_sections` refuses on several further, independent grounds (**5** more as of 2026-08-18), each with its own config key and its own message — the **shrink floor** (a same-named prose slot losing more than 50% of the text a reader sees), the **component floor**, the **prune floor**, the **single-slot floors**, and `refuse_save_without_sections_metadata`. None of them consults `rebuild_policy`, and a `generic` page meets all of them at full strength. `generic` does not mean "permitted", it means "not blocked *by ownership*".
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** the query is correct, the answer is correct, and it is the answer to a question that was worth asking. What makes it damage is the sentence written next to it. On `ai-agent-orchestration.com` a handoff recorded *"✅ `pricing` is `rebuild_policy='generic'`, **so the rebuild will not be refused** — checked 2026-08-18"* and listed the rebuild as *"approved, not yet dispatched"*. Both were false at the time of writing: the page-scoped rebuild had been filed **~16 hours earlier** (item `889a0687-cc0a-4f5e-8693-9ee6ca98751a`, `page-rerender` → `page-build-handler`, `spec.reason='content_data_backfill'`, 2026-08-17 20:28Z) and had already **failed** on the shrink floor — *"SECTION SHRINK REFUSED for page "pricing" — call-to-action 483→213 chars of VISIBLE text (44% kept, floor 50%). Nothing was written."* A green tick against the wrong gate is worse than no check, because the next session stops looking for the refusal that already happened.
- **the check, and it is two queries, not one.** First ask whether this page has ALREADY been refused, before reasoning about whether it would be:
  ```sql
  SELECT id, item_type, status, attempt_count, created_by, created_at, left(error,200)
  FROM site_work_items
  WHERE site_id='<site>' AND spec->>'page_name'='<page>'
    AND item_type IN ('needs_page','needs_content_page','page_rerender')
  ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5;   -- a 'failed' row here IS the pre-flight answer
  ```
  Then, if it has not, name which floor your write could trip rather than asserting none of them can — the shrink floor is the one that fires on a *regeneration*, because a fresh LLM write of an existing prose slot is routinely shorter than what it replaces.
- **⚠ the remedy is a safety control, so treat it as a decision and not a config tweak.** The error names its own escape hatch (`set section_shrink_floor in the step config`), which makes it read like a threshold to nudge. The floor exists for the class where an agent rewrites a whole artefact and persists a fragment while reporting success (`bugs_open/012`; CLAUDE.md's `output_tokens == max_tokens` rule). Lowering it to admit a known-56%-shorter rewrite is choosing to accept that copy — an owner-facing judgement about a live page. **Nothing is written when it refuses, so there is no time pressure and no damage to undo.**
- **⚠ and do not reach for the whole-domain hammer instead.** `082_submit_domain_unified.sh <domain>` is the documented "never hand-build" route and it is **WHOLE-SITE**: `needs_domain_research → strategy → briefing → site plan → design cascade → needs_content_page × N → rerender`. Firing it to fix one page regenerates every page and re-runs the design cascade. The page-scoped route is `needs_page` / `needs_content_page` → `page-build-handler`, which is what filed the refused item above. The owner ruling of 2026-08-04 forbids hand-building a site; it does not require a domain-level resubmission to rebuild one page.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/178` (the shrink floor) · `bugs_open/293` (the whole-page path still measures the tag-stripped axis) · `bugs_closed/285` · LANDMINE "The per-slot TEXT floor counts CSS and JAVASCRIPT as text…" (the same floor's *axis* problem — this entry is about mistaking one gate for all of them) · MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] · [[grep-the-config-key-before-calling-it-a-win]]
- **added:** 2026-08-18, site_ai_agent_orchestration lane, found while checking whether the "approved and unblocked" pricing rebuild was ready to dispatch

### LCO-009's silent-cap WARN cannot be censused from the logs it writes to — but `collected_data` already holds every fact it reports, retroactively and per run

- **footprint:** register **LCO-009**, `platform/orchestration/actions/query_row_cap.go`, `resultHitItsRowCap`, `"EQUALS the query's LIMIT"`, `QueryDatabaseAction`, `orchestration_states.collected_data`, `bugs_open/275`, `bugs_open/298`, `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_275_silent_row_caps/`
- **fires when:** you ask "have any silent row caps actually bitten?" and reach for the detector — grepping pods for the WARN, as the lane's own handoff instructed until 2026-08-18. The sweep returns **0 WARNs**, which reads as "no cap has fired", and both the detector and the census command are working exactly as designed.
- **why the wrong answer looks right:** the WARN is a log line on the chassis, whose retrievable window is **seconds** (measured 2026-08-18: 3 s, 15 s, 21 s, 34 s, 91 s across five samples on pods up 27 minutes with **0 restarts**; see the two entries above for the general class). The steps it watches run **6-hourly**. So the probability that any given human-run census overlaps a cap event is near zero, and *every* census returns the same clean zero whether the caps bite constantly or never. A second, independent cause of the same zero: the first release carrying the detector (`v1.0.1309`) shows an earliest evidenced roll of **2026-08-18 15:45:31Z**, so a "last 24h" sweep run that afternoon covered mostly hours in which the detector was not in the fleet at all. **Two sufficient causes, one indistinguishable reading.**
- **the check — census the durable channel, which needs no new code:** `QueryDatabaseAction` writes each result to the step's `output_field`, which lands in `orchestration_states.collected_data` and survives rolls. Compare it against the step's own cap (the full query is in the lane RUNBOOK, "Census the caps from `collected_data`"):
  ```sql
  CASE jsonb_typeof(out) WHEN 'array'  THEN jsonb_array_length(out)      -- output_format: array
                         WHEN 'object' THEN (out->>'count')::int END     -- output_format: object
  ```
  ⚠ **Handle BOTH formats or you re-create the blind zero in SQL.** A first pass counting only arrays reported **0 of 4** hits for `content-feed-trigger`; the true answer was **3 of 4**. ⚠ `orchestration_states` is pruned to roughly **2 days** (5,701 rows, only 25 older than that) — ~3,000× the log window, still not "all history". ⚠ Take the agent→cap map from live config, not from any doc; re-run the cap census in the same RUNBOOK.
- **what it found on first use, which is the point:** 4 cap hits in the retained window (`content-feed-trigger` 3 of 4 runs at exactly 5; `internal-linker` 1 run at exactly 15) with two working negative arms (`model-directory-trigger` 0 of 5, max 4 against a cap of 12; and `content-feed-trigger` itself under its cap on one run). The same question asked of the logs returned zero, twice, on two different days.
- **the wider lesson, already stated elsewhere and worth obeying:** a log-only signal is not a durable control on this fleet. Before building one, ask what will read it in a week — and check whether the fact is *already* being persisted by something else, because on this platform it usually is.
- **relations:** the two entries above on chassis log retention (2026-08-08 at 0.4 s; 2026-08-14 at ~90 s with the liveness-control recipe) · `bugs_open/275` · `bugs_open/298` · register LCO-009 · MEMORY [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]] · [[detection-works-schedule-and-dispatch-do-not]]
- **added:** 2026-08-18, bugfix_275_silent_row_caps lane, while running the three verifications its own handoff owed

### A `cut`/`awk`/`sed` anywhere in a streaming watcher's pipeline holds the catch in a 4KB buffer — so the capture file stays EMPTY and reads exactly like "the event never fired"

- **footprint:** `kubectl logs -f`, `grep --line-buffered`, `cut -c`, any `… | grep --line-buffered … | <filter> | while read` watcher armed to catch a rare event, `pkill -f`
- **fires when:** you take the streaming recipe (the correct remedy for chassis log rotation) and add one formatting step — truncating enormous JSON lines to something readable is the obvious thing to do, and `cut -c1-900` is the obvious way. `grep --line-buffered` flushes per line; **`cut` then re-buffers at 4 KB**, and a rare, small WARN never reaches the file.
- **why the wrong answer looks right:** the watcher is running, the file exists, the pipeline has no error, and the event you armed for is *expected* to be rare — so an empty capture is exactly what a genuine negative looks like. If the deadline then kills the pipeline, the buffered lines are lost with it, and you record "armed for two hours, nothing fired."
- **the check:** **foreground-test the exact pipeline against a pattern that MUST match before arming it** — `… | grep --line-buffered -a -e '"level":"info"'` on a chassis pod produces lines within seconds. If your test prints nothing, the plumbing is broken, not the fleet quiet. (Measured 2026-08-18: 20 s with `cut` in the pipeline → **0 lines**; the same 20 s without it → 3 lines immediately.) Truncate inside the loop instead: `while IFS= read -r line; do printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "${line:0:900}" >> "$OUT"; done`.
- **the second half of the same trap, and it fires in the opposite direction:** once the pipeline flushes, an **unanchored** pattern over-collects. `grep -a "QueryDatabaseAction: Complete"` matches the literal *inside* the coordinator's 183 KB whole-state dumps — measured 2026-08-18, **121 of 184** captured lines were that, not the event — and if you truncate lines for readability (`${line:0:900}`) you delete the evidence of why they matched, so the capture reads as 184 genuine hits. **Anchor on the line's own message** (`'"msg":"QueryDatabaseAction: Complete"'`), keep matched lines WHOLE, and check the identity that must hold: **total lines == anchored hits**. An over-collecting watcher is worse than a silent one, because it produces a confident positive.
- **the adjacent trap that will eat your fix:** **never `pkill -f <name>` from a shell whose own command line contains that name** — including the heredoc that rewrites the very script you are killing. The shell matches its own pattern and kills itself mid-command (exit **144**, no error text), so the rewrite silently does not happen and you re-arm the OLD script believing it is the new one. The `[w]` bracket trick does **not** help when the command line genuinely contains the word. Write the PID to a file when you start it and kill by PID.
- **relations:** the chassis-log-retention entries above (streaming is their prescribed remedy — this is how the remedy fails quietly) · MEMORY [[foreground-test-a-watcher-before-arming-it]] · [[shell-tool-traps-committing]]
- **added:** 2026-08-18, bugfix_275_silent_row_caps lane, arming a capture for a 6-hourly cap event
