### You cannot measure a NEW producer on a deduped `item_type` by counting its own rows — the first filer keeps the attribution, so the new one reads ZERO while working perfectly

- **footprint:** `site_work_items.spec->>'refused_by'` / `source` / `created_by` / any producer-attribution key, `emitOwnedPageReviewItem`, `idx_swi_dedup`, `owned_page_review`, `capability_gap`, `needs_diagnosis`, and **any item type the 2026-08-02 ruling's "converge N producers onto ONE item_type" shape applies to**
- **fires when:** you add a second (or fourth) producer to an existing deduped item type — which this estate actively encourages — and then try to prove the new one is working. No symptom: you write the obvious query, get zero, and the zero looks like a dead code path.
- **the trap:** the emitters insert `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on `(site_id, item_key)`, and the key is derived from the SUBJECT (a page name), **not from the producer**. So if any earlier producer already filed an open row for that subject, the new producer's insert is silently discarded and **the surviving row still carries the FIRST filer's attribution**. Your new producer can fire correctly, repeatedly, for ever, and never appear in a count grouped by its own name.
- **⚠ it is worst exactly where the new producer matters most.** A second producer is usually added because the subject is being hit repeatedly — and a repeatedly-hit subject is precisely the one that already has an open row. ~~**On a mature estate the count can read zero permanently.**~~ **CORRECTED 2026-08-20 — that was too strong, by the entry author, one day later.** The count is suppressed **per subject**, not globally: `refused_by='load_page_record'` read **0** on 08-19 and reads **3** on 08-20, because the guard reached pages that had no open row yet. **So the right statement is: the new producer is invisible on exactly the subjects it was added for, and visible only on fresh ones — which is the more insidious version, because a non-zero count now "proves it works" while saying nothing about the repeat cases.** Measured 2026-08-19 on `bugs_open/301`: the new `load_page_record` guard refused three builds (quoted `OWNED_PAGE_GUARD` in `__step_error` at 13:37:08, 13:37:59, 13:38:35) and filed **0** rows, because both pages already carried `owned_page_review` rows filed by the *save* path two days earlier.
- **the second half, and it is the reason the dedup bites at all:** `idx_swi_dedup`'s partial predicate excludes only `complete, verified, rejected, wont_fix, failed, unresolved, cancelled`. **`needs_human_review` is NOT in that list**, so a HITL-terminal row — the shape auditors are told to use — stays **inside** the open set for ever and blocks re-filing indefinitely. A `failed` row does not; a `needs_human_review` one does. Check the status list before assuming a row is out of the way.
- **the check — measure the producer at its OWN evidence, never at the shared row:**
  - `orchestration_states.collected_data->'__step_error'` — `failed_step` plus a marker in the message (`OWNED_PAGE_GUARD`) names the producer that actually ran. ⚠ ~24h retention, so do it on a **fresh** burst.
  - the **absence** of downstream work is often the cleaner signal: for 301, "no `page-content-writer` orchestration within a minute of the build" proved the early refusal where no row count could.
  - if you need row-level attribution, the emitter must put the producer in the **`item_key`**, and that is a deliberate trade — it defeats the cross-producer dedup the ruling wanted. Decide which you are buying; you cannot have both.
- **relations:** LANDMINES "`count(*) = count(DISTINCT item_key)` is the WRONG dedup test" (the sibling arithmetic trap on the same index), `bugs_open/301` + `bugs_closed/295` (where this was measured), `bugs_open/204` (why an emission needs a bounded dedup key), CLAUDE.md 2026-08-02 ruling §1 (the practice that creates this shape)
- **added:** 2026-08-19, vigilant_designer_offer_analysis lane

### A `css_themes` row can be BORN EMPTY while git serves the real stylesheet — the site looks perfect for days, and the FIRST css-patch cycle then replaces the whole file with a fragment, through a door `bugs_open/198` named and only half-closed

- **footprint:** `css_themes.css_content` · `fork_theme_from_site_action.go` · `install_site_composition_action.go` · css-patch-agent's `deploy_css` (`git_commit` of `css_saved.css_content`) · `assets/css/styles.css` on any framework site · `style_collections.css_theme_id`
- **fires when:** a site's theme row is created with empty/tiny `css_content` (measured: `theme-noted-co-uk` born empty 2026-08-15, 67 seconds before webdesign-agent committed the real 17,475-byte file to git) and ANY `contrast_failure` later routes to css-patch-agent. The 198 fix (candidate 3, live 08-10) made the DB append shrink-proof — **and the deploy still commits the DB value wholesale over the file**, so a correct guarded append onto an empty baseline shipped 91 bytes over 17,475 (21 commits, 16 minutes, 2026-08-18). The auditor then files MORE contrast findings against the now-unstyled page: the loop amplifies its own damage, every run green.
- **the tell, before any symptom:** `SELECT s.domain, ct.version, length(ct.css_content) FROM sites s JOIN style_collections sc ON sc.id=s.style_collection_id JOIN css_themes ct ON ct.id=sc.css_theme_id;` — compare against the deployed file's size. A theme row **smaller than its served `styles.css`** is this trap armed; empty is the loaded form. After the fact, the tell is a run of `CSS fix: … (theme vN)` commits whose file sizes RISE from double digits.
- **the check after any css-patch activity:** never the work item (`complete`, honest, useless) — `git log` the FILE's sizes, and diff DB length vs served length in the same breath.
- **repair recipe (proven 2026-08-19, noted):** rebuild `css_content` = last-good git version + provenance comment + the accumulated patches (they are appended, so the current DB value IS the patch list); deploy via the git-adapter **with the site's real `repo_name`** (`vm-sites` for VM sites — the default `sites` is the OTHER landmine); verify DB==repo==box==live and that base selectors serve.
- **the doors that remain open** (fix candidates in 198's file, that lane's to close): git-writer shrink guard; fork/composition birth guard on empty `css_content`; a DB↔file drift check.

### `css_themes.css_content` is EMPTY on most sites while the served `styles.css` is 20KB+ — deploy the row wholesale and you WIPE the site's theme, with every guard green

- **footprint:** `css_themes` · `style_collections.css_theme_id` · `css-patch-agent` (`save_css_to_db` / `deploy_css`) · `assets/css/styles.css` · any workflow that loads `css_themes`, modifies, and commits to a site repo
- **fires when:** you build or run anything that treats `css_themes.css_content` as the source of truth for a site's deployed `/assets/css/styles.css`. No symptom beforehand: the append succeeds, the guard passes, the commit lands, the item completes.
- **the trap:** the deployed file is written ONLY by webdesign-agent design runs (`bugs_open/072`, quoted at `rerender_single_page_action.go:396`) and was never backfilled into `css_themes` — measured 2026-08-19, **11 of 21 linked themes hold 0 bytes** while their sites serve 13–25KB stylesheets carrying every `:root` variable definition. Appending to `''` is monotonic, so the 198 shrink guard passes by construction, and the deploy then replaces the real 20KB file with the patches-only row: every `--color-*` definition vanishes and most text on the site goes invisible (dark-fallback sections render black-on-black, heroes white-on-white). Six sites took exactly this 2026-08-17/18 (`bugs_open/198` round 2). The follow-on audit measures 1.00:1, files `contrast_failure`, and routes it BACK to the same agent — the loop re-deploys the broken file for ever, every item `complete`.
- **the check:** before shipping `css_content` to a site file, compare it with the file it replaces: `curl -s https://<domain>/assets/css/styles.css | wc -c` (or repo HEAD) vs `length(css_content)`. Row ≪ file means the row is NOT the source of truth — backfill it from the file first (the 198 relojistas/idea.uk restore recipe), never the reverse. A site whose served stylesheet has `grep -c ':root'` = 0 is already clobbered, whatever its work items say.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/198` (both rounds + restore recipe) · `bugs_open/072` (who writes the file) · `bugs_open/012` / 016b §9 (persisted-fragment class) · `a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact` · **sibling entry directly above (noted lane, written concurrently the same day): the BORN-EMPTY seed (`fork_theme_from_site`) and the pre-symptom one-query tell — read both**

### `visual-design-auditor` reads CSS **source**, not computed style — so it reports fallback literals as the site's palette, and four of five findings on a healthy page were FALSE

- **footprint:** `agent_definitions.type='visual-design-auditor'` (step `run_visual_llm_audit`) · `design-audit-agent` (its orchestrator) · `design_context.css_excerpt` / `component_samples` / `index_samples` · `site_work_items` types `needs_design_review`, `spacing_fix`, `responsive_fix`, `dark_section_audit` · handlers `webdesign-agent`, `css-patch-agent`, `component-template-fixer`
- **fires when:** you dispatch it to "have a look at the design". It returns exactly five findings with severities, `current_value` quotes and machine-checkable `acceptance_test` strings — a report that reads audited. Its inputs are **CSS text and HTML samples**, so anything whose value is decided at cascade time is invisible to it.
- **measured 2026-08-19**, leopardessconsulting.co.uk, graded against the rendered page with `getComputedStyle`: **1 of 5 confirmed, 3 false, 1 misdiagnosed.**
  - *"the palette is corporate blue, `--color-primary: #1e40af`, `--color-accent: #d97706`"* — **false.** Computed `:root` is `#0D0D0D` / `#836E32` / header `#0D0D0D`, i.e. the brand values the finding said were missing. It had read `var(--color-primary, #1e40af)` **fallbacks** inside component CSS. Severity high, handler `webdesign-agent`: acting on it repaints a correct palette.
  - *"body font is Merriweather serif, inconsistent with the brand"* — **false.** Computed body and h1 are `Inter, -apple-system, …, sans-serif`. Merriweather is applied nowhere.
  - *"`padding: var(--spacing-section, 4.5rem 2rem)` is malformed so the section has no padding"* — **false twice.** Computed `.stat-band` padding is **80px**, and a `var()` fallback is a token stream that may legally contain a shorthand.
  - *"the hero h1 has no responsive scaling and will overflow"* — **misdiagnosed.** 56px at 1280, 32px at 375, `scrollWidth == clientWidth == 375`, no hero overflow.
  - *"the hero carries an inline rgba overlay and `--hero-btn-ink`, so a theme change cannot cascade into it"* — **confirmed**, verbatim in the `style` attribute. The one that holds is the one about markup the auditor could actually see.
- **why it is worse than a noisy report:** every finding lands as `status='detected'`, and `detected-item-promoter` takes exactly that status to `triaged` on a ~2-minute tick, whence the build pipeline dispatches the named handler. So a false palette finding becomes a live repaint of a correct palette **without anyone reading it**. Hold them the moment they land: `UPDATE site_work_items SET status='needs_human_review' …` is enough, because the promoter's predicate is `WHERE wi.status='detected'`.
- **the check, and it is cheap:** before believing ANY of its colour, spacing or typography findings, ask the rendered page — `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--color-accent')` and friends. Working probe: `docs/leopardessconsulting/scripts/verify_audit.py`. The platform already owns a renderer-side witness (`render_audit`, VIZ-010/012) and this agent does not use it; until it does, its output is a hypothesis list, not an audit.
- **⚠ the same trap catches humans reading the page source.** In this lane's own notes the day before, `--color-accent` was quoted as `#d97706` from a `grep` of the served HTML; the computed `:root` value is `#836E32`. Corrected in place. A hex in the source is not a hex in effect.
- **source:** 2026-08-19, leopardess design-review dispatch — the owner asked for a design report *before* any change, which is the only reason the nine filed items were read rather than executed
- **relations:** MEMORY [[a-css-fallback-is-present-and-inoperative]] · [[a-subagent-report-is-another-doc]] · [[a-pass-from-a-blind-check-outlives-the-blindness]] · register VIZ-010 (the renderer-side witness this agent should be using)
- **added:** 2026-08-19, leopardess design-review lane

### Correcting a site brief with a PARTIAL write deletes the rest of it from the writer's view — the document still reads complete, and the write logs success

- **footprint:** `site_specs` (aspect `content_direction`) · `write_site_spec` / `WriteSiteSpecAction` (`platform/orchestration/actions/site_spec_actions.go:212` and `:247`) · `datahelpers.FormatContentDirection` (`format_content_direction.go`) · `apply_adoption_plan_action.go:280` · any migration, operator script or agent that writes a `content_direction` correction
- **fires when:** you fix one part of a site's brief — a tagline, a banned phrase, a CTA rule — and write just that part. This is the normal, careful way to edit a spec, and it is the trap. **No symptom follows**: the write succeeds, the stored document still contains all twenty keys, `git`-style review of the spec looks right, and the action logs a healthy `formatted_len` for what it wrote.
- **the trap:** the page writer does not read the document. It reads **`content_direction.formatted`** and four other named fields — that surface is the agent config, not folklore: `page-content-writer`'s prompt references exactly `content_direction.formatted`, `identity.key_differentiators`, `identity.target_audience`, `evidence_base.writer_block`, `design_intent.imagery_direction`. `formatted` is rebuilt on every write **from the incoming partial, before the deep merge** — so it becomes a rendering of your two keys, and the other eighteen stop reaching the writer while remaining in the document for ever after. Measured 2026-08-19: it fired on four sites on 2026-04-18 (`domain-research-classifier` → `build-site-planner`), and **three still serve a fragment four months on** — `ai-agent-orchestration.com` at 5 of 18 keys, `robot-hands.com` 14 keys dropped, `leopardessconsulting.co.uk` 12. One site's eight-item `things_to_avoid` has reached no page since April.
- **the check, before and after any spec write:** `docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/copy_quality_two_stage/audit_writer_brief.py <domain>` — section 2 lists document keys reaching no writer-visible field, and separates a genuinely empty key (`compliance_rules: []`, benign on 13 sites) from real content. In SQL, the same test in one line: a key is in the brief iff its humanised label (`things_to_avoid` → `Things to avoid:`) appears in `data->>'formatted'`. **Do not size a brief by `length(data::text)`** — on the worst site that is 4× the text the writer sees, and counting the document rather than the brief is what made this lane withdraw a published fleet census on 2026-08-19.
- **if you must write a partial today:** re-read the merged row afterwards and rewrite `formatted` from it, or write the whole document. ⚠ **A backfill is not a no-op on output** — restoring ~10,000 chars of brief changes what every subsequent page says, and on at least one site the restored `example_phrases` are themselves written in the mannerism the owner objected to. Read the diff; do not sweep.
- **source:** `bugs_open/327` (mechanism, per-site measurements, fix candidates) · `copy_quality_two_stage/NOTES_two_stage_copy.md` 2026-08-19
- **relations:** `bugs_open/305` (found while investigating it — and **explicitly not its cause**, §4 of 327) · MEMORY [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]] · [[a-config-key-that-nothing-reads.md]] · register CQ-025
- **added:** 2026-08-19, copy_quality_two_stage lane

### The 090 trigger prints `SAVE: CORRELATION_ID=…` and THEN fails the intake insert — a newline or a double quote in your symptom loses the run, and you walk away holding an id for something that does not exist

- **footprint:** `docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/fixloop_eg_dartsonline/090_TRIGGER_needs_diagnosis_v1.sh` (`INPUT_DATA` assembly at `:339`, the `$json$…$json$` intake insert) · `site_work_items` (`item_type='needs_diagnosis'`) · any trigger script that interpolates free text into a `$json$`-quoted psql literal
- **fires when:** you author a symptom the way every guideline in CLAUDE.md tells you to — several paragraphs, the mechanism first, symbol names quoted. Heredoc it to a file, `"$(cat …)"` it into the trigger, and the newlines and quotes travel with it. **No symptom beforehand**: the script's own banner block prints in full, including the item_key, the anchor site, the repo/ref and a correlation id under the words `SAVE: CORRELATION_ID=`.
- **the trap:** `INPUT_DATA` is built by shell string concatenation — `INPUT_DATA="{\"symptom\":\"$SYMPTOM\",…"` — with **no JSON escaping of `$SYMPTOM`**, and the banner is printed *before* the insert runs. So the order you experience is: id printed, then `ERROR: invalid input syntax for type json`. A raw newline fails with `Character with value 0x0a must be escaped`; a double quote fails with `Token "…" is invalid`. **Both leave no work item and no run**, while the id you were told to save is real-looking and joins to nothing. The usage comment at `:83` warns about `"` and `\` only — it says nothing about newlines, which is the one a multi-paragraph symptom hits first.
- **the check:** flatten and de-quote before dispatching, and **verify the intake landed rather than trusting the banner** —
  ```bash
  tr '\n' ' ' < sym.txt | tr -s ' ' | sed "s/\"/'/g" > sym_safe.txt
  ... 090_TRIGGER_needs_diagnosis_v1.sh "$(cat sym_safe.txt)"
  ```
  The positive signal is the script reaching `Waiting up to 180s for the loop to claim it …` and printing **`SAVE: RUN_CORRELATION_ID=`** (a *different*, later line from the `CORRELATION_ID=` one). If you only ever saw `SAVE: CORRELATION_ID=`, the insert failed. Settle it in SQL rather than by scrollback: `SELECT status, created_at FROM site_work_items WHERE item_key='needs_diagnosis:<your-slug>';` — no row means no run, however much output you got.
- **⚠ the two ids are not interchangeable, and this is where the trap compounds.** `CORRELATION_ID` is the intake correlation; `RUN_CORRELATION_ID` is minted by `diagnose-dispatch-loop` and is the key the artifacts are written under. Querying `orchestration_states` on the intake id returns nothing, which reads identically to "the dispatch was dropped" — the exact evidence CLAUDE.md warns not to retry on.
- **source:** 2026-08-19, `bugs_open/029` lane — two consecutive dispatches lost this way (newline first, then a quoted `"response"` marker name) while re-filing the wedge diagnosis; third attempt with the flattened, de-quoted text reached `RUN_CORRELATION_ID=be89750f`
- **relations:** `bugs_open/174` / the `SEED_SCOPE` comma-string entry above (same script, same class: free text crossing an unescaped boundary) · MEMORY [[shell-tool-traps-committing]] · [[kcat-publish-silently-drops]] (a publish that exits 0 having sent nothing — this is its intake-side twin) · [[escape-sequence-emission-trap]]
- **added:** 2026-08-19, `bugs_open/029` retry-kills-live-child lane

### `validate_content` protects the page-BUILD path and NOTHING ELSE — the section-editor and chrome paths render through the same seam and write straight to a live page

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/section_editor_actions.go` (`applyContentEdit` :886, `applyComponentSwap` :996, `updatePageComponentAfterEdit` :1233 and its `UPDATE page_components SET rendered_html` at :1251), `platform/orchestration/actions/component_library.go` (`RenderTemplate`, `RenderHeader` :1969, `RenderFooter` :2038, `RenderHead` :2311), `page_components.rendered_html`, `site_components.rendered_html`, `bugs_open/260` §4, work item types `content_rewrite` / `content_edit`
- **fires when:** you reason about what protects a render — sizing the blast radius of a rendering defect, deciding whether a bad render can reach a live page, or quoting `bugs_open/260` §4's *"the gate is why"* / *"Live damage: ZERO"*. **No symptom needed, and the wrong answer is the reassuring one.**
- **the tell:** there is none at the artefact — the tell is in what you are reading. 260 §4 establishes that no damaged section has ever been stored and attributes it to `validate_content` refusing first. That is measured and true, **and it is a fact about the page-BUILD path only.** The sentence does not say so and reads as a property of rendering in general. Grep `section_editor_actions.go` for `validate` or `unrendered` and you get **one comment about a review-queue sweep and nothing else**: an edit renders, and `updatePageComponentAfterEdit` writes `rendered_html` to an already-published page with no content validation in between. Chrome (`RenderHeader`/`RenderFooter`/`RenderHead`) is the same shape.
- **⚠ and the guard that looks like it covers this cannot.** Both editor sites already do `if rendered == "" { return …error }`. The failure mode it would need to catch does **not** produce empty output — the regex fallback returns well-formed HTML with `{{if}}`/`{{range}}`/`{{end}}` still in it. A guard written for roughly this class, blind to it, and reading as protection.
- **the check:** never generalise a "nothing was persisted" result past the path whose gate produced it. Name the gate, then grep the OTHER writers of the same column for it: `grep -n "validate\|unrendered" platform/orchestration/actions/section_editor_actions.go`. If a write path does not name the gate, it does not have it. And size the exposure rather than assuming it is idle — `[MEASURED 2026-08-19]` **271 `content_rewrite`/`content_edit` items, 117 complete, 2026-04-08 → 2026-08-19**, against **0 of 1,789** stored components carrying a leak. That zero is a real negative (the path runs) but it is a demand control, **not a guarantee about the next edit**: the correct statement is *"the ungated path has not yet been unlucky."*
- **related:** the entry on the regex render fallback (`RenderTemplateReportingMissing`) — same seam; that one tells you the render degrades silently, this one tells you which paths have nothing downstream to catch it. `bugs_open/260` §9c (the `copy_quality_two_stage` lane reached the editor hazard from the other direction and also had not measured the missing gate).
- **source:** 2026-08-19, `bugfix_260_render_fallback` lane, while sizing candidate 1 · `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_260_render_fallback/NOTES_260_render_fallback.md`
- **added:** 2026-08-19, bugfix_260_render_fallback lane

### A site brief's `formatted` text is regenerated in a RANDOM order every write — so diffing two briefs reports ~100% changed whether or not anything did

- **footprint:** `site_specs` (aspect `content_direction`) · `datahelpers.FormatContentDirection` (`format_content_direction.go`) · `write_site_spec` / `WriteSiteSpecAction` · `apply_adoption_plan_action.go` · any check, audit or handoff that compares two versions of a brief, or asserts that a brief correction landed
- **fires when:** you correct a site's brief and then verify the correction — by diffing the new `formatted` against the old, by eyeballing the top of it, or by asserting "the brief now reads X". Also when a **detector** keyed on brief text reports a change. **No symptom first:** both texts are real, both are current, and the diff is enormous and completely uninformative.
- **the trap:** `FormatContentDirection` renders the spec with `for key, val := range spec`, and **Go randomises map iteration order by design**. Nothing sorts. Two writes of an **identical** document therefore produce two briefs that share no line ordering at all. Measured 2026-08-19 on `loanzy.uk`: three writes on 2026-08-18 (13:36, 15:58, 20:19), same 14-key document, `formatted` at 9,802 / 10,115 / 10,108 chars, **all three carrying 13 of 13 labels**, opening on `Content depth:`, `Voice:` and `Compliance rules:` respectively. **A diagnosis-loop verdict read exactly those three opening lines as three different partial briefs** and cited it as live evidence of a different bug — so this misleads machines as well as people.
- **the check:** compare briefs by **label presence and per-key content**, never by diffing the rendered text. A key is in the brief iff its humanised label (`things_to_avoid` → `Things to avoid:`) appears in `data->>'formatted'`; `audit_writer_brief.py <domain>` does exactly that and is order-independent. To prove a correction landed, assert on the corrected key's own text (`position('<new phrase>' in data->>'formatted') > 0`) plus the label count, not on the document.
- **the fix, if someone is already in there:** one line — iterate a sorted key list. It is a **different defect from `bugs_open/327`** (which is about `formatted` being computed from the incoming partial before the merge) that happens to live in the same function; fixing one does not fix the other.
- **not a prompt-cache problem, checked:** the brief sits ~21% into a ~45,000-char rendered writer prompt, but the order is fixed once stored, so every call between two spec writes sees identical text. The arithmetic looks alarming until you do it.
- **source:** `bugs_open/327` (final `090` verdict section, 2026-08-19); `copy_quality_two_stage/NOTES_two_stage_copy.md`
- **relations:** the sibling entry above (the partial-write collapse — same function, same footprint, different failure) · register CQ-025 · MEMORY [[a-subagent-report-is-another-doc]] (a verdict's citation is another doc: check what it measured, not what it concluded)
- **added:** 2026-08-19, copy_quality_two_stage lane

### Every `banned_claims` pattern is compiled with a forced `(?i)` — so a pattern that leans on CAPITALISATION silently matches everything, and it fails by BLOCKING pages, which looks like a strict gate

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/claims.go` (`regexp.Compile("(?i)" + p)` at `:296`) · `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/claims_global.go` (`:223`, same) · `site_specs` aspect `evidence_base`, key `banned_claims` · `cmd/claimscan` · `validate_page_content` check 8 / `save_sections_claims_guard` / `save_page_meta_description_action`
- **fires when:** you write or review a `banned_claims` pattern whose discriminator is a capital letter — an attributed name (`[A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z]`), a proper noun, a brand, an initialism, a sentence start. **No symptom needed, and the failure is invisible from the live corpus.** Also fires when you read such a pattern's `reason` and believe it describes what the pattern does.
- **the trap:** the compile site prefixes `(?i)` to EVERY pattern, site-level and fleet-wide, and nothing in the register's schema, the `reason` field or the author's editor shows it. `[A-Z]` then matches any letter and `[a-z]+` any word. Worked case, webdesign.uk 2026-08-19: the testimonial ban `"[^"]{20,}" ?[—,-]? ?[A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z]` — whose reason says "a long quotation followed by an attributed name" — degraded to *"a quotation followed by more prose"*. It blocked a quoted example brief, a quoted anti-example and a quoted **question** exactly as readily as a real testimonial, and stopped a guide page whose whole subject is quoting example briefs.
- **⚠ why no census will find it: the damage is an ABSENCE.** A page blocked at save never becomes a stored component, so a scan of `page_components` before and after the fix returns the SAME findings in both directions (measured: 0 added, 0 removed over 27 components). The only evidence is a probe set you author yourself. And the direction of failure is the reassuring one — an over-broad ban reads as a strict gate, not a broken one, so it draws no suspicion and each blocked page looks like the writer's fault.
- **the check:** before trusting any pattern containing `[A-Z]`, assume it is case-insensitive and re-read it that way. Census the estate in one query —
  ```sql
  SELECT s.domain, b->>'pattern'
    FROM site_specs ss JOIN sites s ON s.id=ss.site_id,
         jsonb_array_elements(ss.data->'banned_claims') b
   WHERE ss.aspect='evidence_base' AND ss.is_current AND b->>'pattern' ~ '\[A-Z\]';
  ```
  (2026-08-19: exactly one row fleet-wide, now fixed; the Go fleet-wide set has none.) **Then prove it with `cmd/claimscan` on a probe set carrying BOTH halves** — the shapes that must still block *and* the innocent shapes that must pass. A probe set of only must-pass sentences cannot tell a narrowed ban from a disarmed one.
- **the fix, when you need case:** Go's RE2 honours inline flag groups, so `(?-i)` inside the pattern locally reverses the forced prefix — `"[^"]{20,}" ?[—,-]? ?(?-i)[A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z]`. No platform change needed.
- **relations:** the same file's negation guard is the sibling trap — it scans BACKWARDS only and excludes bare "no" by design, so a bare-token ban blocks the DENIAL of the thing it bans (three cases on webdesign.uk in two days: `\brefunds?\b`, `whenever you like`, `round of changes`). Both are "the pattern does not mean what its author read it as". MEMORY [[a-doc-comment-is-not-an-enforcement-mechanism]] · [[mutate-the-code-to-prove-the-guard]]
- **source:** 2026-08-19, `webdesign_uk_build_service` lane · `docs024_key_docs_latest/webdesign_uk_build_service/SQL_2026-08-19h_testimonial_ban_needs_case_sensitivity.sql` and the NOTES entry of the same date
- **added:** 2026-08-19, webdesign_uk_build_service lane

### `fix_component_template`'s `action: "needs_review"` is a REFUSAL flag that only the agent's own WORKFLOW reads — `complete_work_item` never did and still does not, and the file's own comment said otherwise for five months

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/fix_component_template_action.go` (every `return map[string]interface{}{"fixed": false, …}` in it; `fixTypesRefusedByDesign`) · `agent_definitions[component-template-fixer]` steps `check_needs_rerender` / `check_refused` / `park_refused` (migration 495) · `platform/orchestration/actions/write_audit_findings_action.go` (`categoryToFixType`, `noHandlerCategories`, `designRouting` entries that name the fixer) · `load_work_item_actions.go` `CompleteWorkItemAction`
- **fires when:** you add or edit a branch in the fixer that returns `fixed:false`; you route a new category or fix_type at `component-template-fixer`; or you read a fixer completion's payload to decide whether work happened.
- **the trap, in both directions.** The fixer's vocabulary is: a **refusal** (cannot do this fix_type; slot locked; subject unidentifiable) carries `action:"needs_review"`; an **idempotent no-op** ("already has flex CSS", "already deployed", "already patched") carries NO `action` key. Until 2026-08-19 NOTHING read that key — the workflow branched on `fixed` only, `handlerReportedFailure` reads `response.status` (which `complete_workflow` cannot set from config), gate 1b is opt-in and numeric — so every refusal closed `complete` (993 `cta_improvement`, 22 sites, 0 ever fixed). The comment at the top of `chromeFixLockSkip` asserted the flag "is what stops the dispatch loop recording the work item as done"; a grep for a reader would have shown it did not. Since migration 495 the agent's workflow branches on EXACTLY that key: **omit it from a refusal and the item completes green; add it to a no-op and legitimate completions park at `needs_human_review`.** Measured over the handler's whole history before the change: 470 refusals / 299 no-ops / zero overlap — keep it that way.
- **the check:** (1) before believing any "X stops the loop" comment in an action, `grep -rn '\["<key>"\]' --include=*.go platform/orchestration` AND census live workflow conditions (`… default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->k->'config'->>'condition' LIKE '%<key>%'`) — a key with no reader is a claim, not a control. (2) routing a category at the fixer: `go test ./platform/orchestration/actions/ -run TestAuditRoutingNeverTargetsAFixerRefusalArm` — it resolves the fix_type the HANDLER would see via its own fallback ladder, so omitting `spec.fix_type` hides nothing. (3) reading a completion: `result->'response'->'fix_result'->>'action'` separates refusal from no-op; `fixed` alone cannot, and 525 of the 993 historical rows carry a FOREIGN payload (spawn record / design-token blob / triage decision) in `result`, so filter on shape before you count.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/323` · `bugs_closed/302`/`213` D1 (the sibling class, where the handler had NO discriminator) · `bugs_closed/077` (router files `capability_gap` for work with no handler) · MEMORY [[a-doc-comment-is-not-an-enforcement-mechanism]] · [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]]
- **source:** 2026-08-19, `bugfix_323_cta_improvement_refusal` lane · `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_323_cta_improvement_refusal/NOTES_cta_improvement_refusal.md`, diagnosis run `b218f39d` (CONFIRMED), probe run `64f89f97`
- **added:** 2026-08-19, bugfix_323_cta_improvement_refusal lane

### Probing the live binary for YOUR commit returns ABSENT on a binary that certainly contains it — the artefact carries ONE stamp, not its ancestry, and the log line that holds it has already scrolled

- **footprint:** `pkg/buildinfo/buildinfo.go` (`GitCommit`) · every `cmd/*/main.go` "build provenance" log line · any `_HOLD`-suffixed file in `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/` · `kubectl … exec <pod> -- grep -a … /proc/1/exe` · CLAUDE.md §"Building & deploying images"
- **fires when:** you are discharging a deploy interlock — "apply this migration only after commit X is live" — which is the standing shape for 32 migrations in the corpus and all 16 `_HOLD` files. No symptom precedes it: you are doing the careful thing, in the documented way.
- **the trap, and it fails in the SAFE-LOOKING direction only by luck.** CLAUDE.md prescribes: read the service's `build provenance` line, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor <your-commit> <the stamp>`. Two things defeat it, and they compound:
  1. **The line is a STARTUP line, so it scrolls.** Measured 2026-08-19: `agent-chassis` pods up at 17:13Z, earliest retained log line 20:08Z — the stamp was unreachable **three hours** after the roll, on a full `kubectl logs` (not a `--tail`). CLAUDE.md already warns an empty result means "not in range", not "unstamped"; what it does not say is how routinely there is no answer at all.
  2. **`buildinfo.GitCommit` is ONE string, not a set.** So the obvious fallback — `grep -aq <my-commit> /proc/1/exe` — is a category error: it asks "was the binary built at exactly this commit", when the question is "does the binary contain this commit's code". Measured the same day: three commits proven by `git merge-base` to be ancestors of the previous stamp all probed **absent**. A session that stops there concludes its fix did not ship, and either re-ships it or, worse, leaves a correct interlock undischarged for ever.
  3. The third fallback is already banned in this file: a *discovery* grep for "some 40-hex string" matches Go's internal digit table and returns the same wrong answer on every service.
- **the check — probe for the CAPABILITY, never for the commit.** Ask the binary for the thing the interlock exists to guarantee: the check name you are about to put in a `checks` array, the config key you are about to set, the literal the code emits when it acts. On **every pod** (a partial roll makes replicas disagree, and the run that fails is the one that lands on the old one), always with a control that must come out absent:
  ```bash
  for POD in $(kubectl -n ai-persona-system get pods -l app=agent-chassis \
                 -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {end}'); do
    kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec $POD -- grep -aq "cta_nonpage_destination"        /proc/1/exe && echo "$POD present"
    kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec $POD -- grep -aq "cta_nonpage_destination_NOTREAL" /proc/1/exe && echo "$POD CONTROL FAILED"
  done
  ```
  Go function names survive in the pclntab for stack traces, so unexported helpers probe fine (`NormalizeTelHref`, `storedCTADestinationIsAuthored` — 2 hits each). This is **strictly stronger** than commit ancestry: it asserts the property rather than a proxy, it is immune to the same-tag-rebuild trap (MEMORY: *a FRESH BUILD CAN SHIP NO NEW CODE*), and unlike a log line or a git ref it **has no shelf life** — the symbol is in the artefact for as long as the artefact runs.
- **the second-order trap:** having improvised a substitute, sessions do not write it down, so the next one re-derives it under time pressure. That is why this entry exists, and why `RFC_040` proposes making it mechanical rather than remembered.
- **relations:** `RFC_040` (DRAFT — persist what the binaries already enumerate; a fail-closed `assert_live_capability()` for migrations) · this file's `logs deploy/X reads one pod of N` and the `strings`/discovery-grep entries · `bugs_open/312` (the interlock that motivated it) · MEMORY [[prove-a-deploy-at-the-artefact-index]] · [[a-fresh-deploy-can-ship-no-new-code]]
- **source:** 2026-08-19, `bugfix_299_cta_dials_phone` lane · `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_299_cta_dials_phone/NOTES_cta_dials_phone.md` (2026-08-19 entries) · migrations 475/476 headers, which record the discharge in full
- **added:** 2026-08-19, bugfix_299_cta_dials_phone lane

### A resolver-conflict class that has gone QUIET is usually waiting for traffic, not fixed — and the instrument cannot see the cases where the candidates happen to AGREE

- **footprint:** `agent_error_log` rows where `error_code='RESOLVER_CONFLICTING_CANDIDATES'` · `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/unified_extractor.go` (`findFieldRecursive`, `extractSingleField`, `collectFieldCandidates`) · `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/resolver_findings.go` · `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/unified_extractor_search_test.go` (the Phase 1 → Phase 2 flip sites) · RFC_029 §9 D2
- **fires when:** you read the conflict window to decide whether a field/caller pair is dealt with — which is the *stated precondition* for flipping the whole-tree search to refusal, and is also how anyone sizes "did my fix land?" on this instrument. No symptom precedes it: the query is short, the dates look decisive, and a class that stopped a day ago reads as closed.
- **the trap, in two independent directions.**
  1. **`max(occurred_at)` measures TRAFFIC, not repair.** These rows are emitted only when a run actually reaches the search with a conflicting tree. Measured 2026-08-19: `page-rerender` had **396 runs in 24 h** with its conflict class last seen ~31 h earlier, and `site-review-agent` had **zero runs at all** — the first is dormant-looking but armed and waiting on a data shape, the second cannot fire whatever you do, and **the two are indistinguishable in the conflict table alone**. Of 19 field/caller pairs logged since the instrument went live on 08-16, four were genuinely killed by shipped fixes and the rest had simply not been provoked. Read either as "handled" and the Phase 2 flip refuses a field in production that no window ever warned about.
  2. **A conflict row requires the candidates to DIFFER, so the instrument under-counts its own class.** `findFieldRecursive` compares by `reflect.DeepEqual` and only warns when the collected values disagree. A tree holding exactly ONE match — or several that agree — resolves silently, with no WARN and no row, and the value can still be wrong: it is simply the only wrong answer available. `bugs_open/330` is the worked case (a step declared `related_pages` via config, the declared path was empty, and the search substituted a different suggestion's list). **So "zero conflict WARNs over the window" can never establish that the search is safe — only that the conflicting subset is empty.** That is a permanent limit of the "or" branch of the flip's own precondition, not a gap to be closed by waiting longer.
- **the check — never read the conflict table without a demand control beside it**, and never treat the instrument's start date as a retention floor (`agent_error_log` holds back to 07-20; the conflict rows begin 08-16 because that is when the instrument shipped):
  ```sql
  WITH conflicted AS (SELECT DISTINCT agent_type FROM agent_error_log
                      WHERE error_code='RESOLVER_CONFLICTING_CANDIDATES')
  SELECT c.agent_type,
         count(o.orchestration_id) FILTER (WHERE o.created_at >= now() - interval '24 hours') AS runs_24h,
         max(o.created_at) AS last_run
  FROM conflicted c LEFT JOIN orchestration_states o ON o.owner_agent_type = c.agent_type
  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY runs_24h DESC;
  ```
  `runs_24h` high + class quiet = **armed, not fixed**. `runs_24h` zero = the class is unfalsifiable from this table; go and read the producer.
  > **⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-20 by the same lane — the join is narrower than this entry first implied.**
  > It answers **"is this agent running NOW?"** and nothing more. It CANNOT size a class
  > historically, because the two tables have wildly different retention: `agent_error_log` holds
  > rows back to **2026-07-20**, while `orchestration_states` keeps only ~**24 h** of `COMPLETED`
  > rows. Worked case: `site-review-agent` has **58 conflict-era rows in `agent_error_log`** and
  > **zero trace in `orchestration_states` by ANY column** — `owner_agent_type`, `workflow_plan`
  > and `execution_metadata` all return 0 — because its runs aged out. So `runs_24h = 0` licenses
  > *"cannot fire right now"* and **NOT** *"retired"*, *"never ran"*, or any claim about the period
  > when the class was actually firing. For that, use the error log's own history. A table read as
  > "agent idle" on this join is a **retention artefact suspect** until you check a second column.

  And group the population by candidate SET (`context->'candidate_paths'`), not by field — a per-field count hides which shape survives and turns a brand-new producer into a bump in an old number (2026-08-19: a `build-dispatch-loop`/`commit_sha` loop-echo class appeared this way, invisible in the per-field view).
- **relations:** `bugs_open/330` (the silent-substitution worked case) · `bugs_closed/306` (the tie-break this instrument exposed) · RFC_029 §10.13 step 5 · this file's `A component's input_schema fallback is NEVER consulted at render time` (same family: a fallback that looks live and is never reached) · MEMORY [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]] · [[zero-adoption-means-read-the-mechanism]] · [[a-pass-from-a-blind-check-outlives-the-blindness]]
- **source:** 2026-08-19, `staged_component_build` lane · `docs024_key_docs_latest/staged_component_build/NOTES_staged_component_build.md` (`## 2026-08-19 (night)`) · `HANDOFF_2026-08-18b_continue_here.md` §5.4(c)
- **added:** 2026-08-19, staged_component_build lane

### `query_database` STRINGIFIES a jsonb column, so `{{range}}` over it iterates nothing — and it looks perfect in psql, in the logs, and in `collected_data`

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/database_actions.go` · any `query_database` step whose SQL builds a column with `jsonb_agg` / `jsonb_build_object` / `to_jsonb` / `array_agg(...)::jsonb` · any `prompt_template` that `{{range}}`s over such a field · `agent_definitions` `default_config`
- **fires when:** you want a LIST inside one row — a set of rules, tags, sibling pages — and reach for `jsonb_agg` because it is the natural SQL, then iterate it in a Go template.
- **the mechanism, measured 2026-08-20:** pgx scans a `jsonb` column into `[]byte`, and the action's own scan loop converts every `[]byte` to a Go `string`. So the value that reaches `collected_data` is a **JSON string**, not a structure:
  ```
  voice_rules        -> object   (correct)
  voice_rules.rules  -> string   "[{\"reason\": \"banned_language: ...\", \"pattern\": \"\\\\bproduction[- ]grade\\\\b\"}, …"
  ```
  `{{range}}` over a string is not iteration, and the step **FAILED** (`current_step=write_descriptions, status=FAILED`).
- **why it is a landmine and not just a bug:** every surface you would check says it worked. The SQL is right in psql. The column is populated. `collected_data` shows the full, correct, human-readable JSON — you have to ask `jsonb_typeof` to see it is a string, and nobody asks that about a value they can read. **The tell is the TYPE, never the content.**
- **the check, before you write the template:**
  ```sql
  SELECT jsonb_typeof(collected_data->'<field>'),
         jsonb_typeof(collected_data#>'{<field>,<subfield>}')
  FROM orchestration_states WHERE correlation_id::text='<corr>';
  -- the inner one must NOT be "string"
  ```
- **the fix is the SHAPE, not the template.** Do not `jsonb_agg`. Return **one row per element** with plain text columns and iterate `output_format: "object"`'s own `rows` array, which the action builds as real structures (`{"rows": results, "count": …}`). `{{range .field.rows}}` then works and `{{.column}}` resolves — and you get `.count` for the `{{if}}` as a free side effect.
  ⚠ And note `output_format: "array"` is NOT the answer either: that returns a bare slice with no addressable keys, which is `bugs_open/313`'s trap in the other direction.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/313` (the sibling: `.count` against a bare array) · `bugs_open/320` migrations `499` (shipped it) and `500` (fixed it) · MEMORY [[a-print-statement-is-not-a-config-row]] (same family: the readable surface is not the operative one)
- **source:** 2026-08-20, `bugs_open/320` — cost one broken live agent on an hourly schedule, caught by reading the artefact rather than the orchestration status
- **added:** 2026-08-20, `meta_description_never_backfilled` lane

### The voice gate's DENSITY rules are statistics over a CORPUS — applied to one sentence they refuse good copy, and 7 of 9 gated sites have already switched them off by hand

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/voicetells.go` (`VoiceGate.ScanVoice`, `MeanSentenceWords`, `LongSentenceWords`, `LongSentenceShare`, `EmDashPer1000Words`, `TriadsPerPage`, `ExpectContractions`) · `site_specs` `aspect='voice'` → `voice_gate` · any caller applying the gate to a SHORT single-value field rather than to page prose
- **fires when:** you reuse the voice gate on something that is not a page — a meta description, a title, a nav label, an alt text — which is the right instinct, because the BANNED-PHRASE half genuinely belongs there.
- **the mechanism:** the gate carries two kinds of rule and only one of them travels. **Content rules** (banned phrases) are true of any string. **Density and distribution rules** are statistics computed across a page's blocks by `ScanVoiceTells`. Over a single sentence they degenerate: "mean sentence length" of one sentence is just its length, "long-sentence share" is 0 or 1, "expects contractions" over 25 words is noise. A 24-word meta description — good, ordinary copy, inside Google's display budget — is refused as `long_sentences: mean sentence length 24.0 words` against a default trip of 22 (`voicetells.go:179-180`).
- **⚠ THE PART THAT PROVES IT IS NOT JUST MY OPINION:** `[MEASURED 2026-08-20]` of the **9** sites with an enabled voice gate, **SEVEN** set `mean_sentence_words: 100000` and `long_sentence_words: 10000` — thresholds chosen to disable the length checks while keeping the banned-phrase list. Only `leopardessconsulting.co.uk` and `oufe.com` leave them unset and inherit the defaults. **The estate has already voted on this with its own config**, one site at a time, without anyone writing down why.
- **the check, before you wire the gate to a new field:** ask whether the field is a CORPUS. If it is one value, filter to the content findings (`check == "banned_phrase"`) and skip the distribution ones. And before believing a refusal, read `save_result.detail` — the finding names which `check` fired, so a density refusal is distinguishable from a real one at a glance.
- **do NOT fix it by raising the site's thresholds**: that is relaxing a checker to fit the content, and it disables the rule for the site's *pages* too, which is where it does work.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/320` (SEO-004's copy gates; migration `501` mitigates in the prompt and says so) · MEMORY [[fixing-a-checker-to-agree-with-a-broken-site]] · the sibling landmine that `check_voice_tells` cannot see `pages.meta_description` at all
- **source:** 2026-08-20, `bugs_open/320`, first scheduled run of the meta-description backfiller
- **added:** 2026-08-20, `meta_description_never_backfilled` lane

## A config key can be DECLARED on the wrong action's spec — and every instrument says it is fine: the literal is in the binary, `git log -S` names the shipping commit, and the arming precondition is met

- **footprint:** `datahelpers.RegisterActionInputSpec`, `ActionInputSpec`, `ConfigKeys`, `StrictConfig`, `datahelpers.UnknownConfigKeys`, `platform/validation/workflow.go` (`checkStepConfigKeys`), `platform/orchestration/actions/v3_site_actions.go`, any `*_HOLD.sql` that arms a new step config key, `WORKFLOW_INVALID`
- **fires when:** you arm a new opt-in config key on a live step — the standard "code first, config second" sequence — and the workflow that carries it dies at validation with `has unrecognised config keys [...] — this action declares its config contract as complete`, even though the key's reader demonstrably shipped. One file can register several specs in one `init()`; put the key in the wrong one and the reader's spec still refuses it. `[MEASURED 2026-08-20]` `deploy_result_field` sat in `RenderComponentInputSpec.ConfigKeys` while `UpdatePageStatusAction` read it and `UpdatePageStatusInputSpec` (`StrictConfig: true`) declared five keys without it — arming migration 494 at 06:49:49Z hard-failed **every workflow that stamps a page**: 8 items across 4 item types, 123 `page_rerender` queued fleet-wide and none draining, until the config was rolled back (`bugs_open/336`).
- **why the wrong result looks exactly right — three instruments, all confirming:** (1) **`grep -aq "<key>" /proc/1/exe` returns PRESENT**, because the literal is in the binary from the reader plus every `zap.String("<key>", …)` call, whichever spec declares it — presence of a literal is not membership of a list, and this is the one question the sanctioned binary probe cannot answer; (2) **`git log -S'"<key>",'` names the commit that shipped the reader** and reads exactly like the declaration's commit — the match is the `zap.String` call, comma and all; (3) **the arming precondition passes**: the owning lane's own rule ("do not arm until a build carrying X has rolled") is about the READER, so ancestry says go while the declaration is still misplaced.
- **the check:** read the LIST, at the commit, inside the spec named in the `RegisterActionInputSpec` call for the action the step actually uses — `git show <stamp>:<file> | awk '/<TheAction>InputSpec = /,/^}/' | grep '"<key>"'` must be non-empty, and the same grep against the OTHER spec in that file must be empty. Then check `StrictConfig` on the reader's spec: strict turns a misplacement from an inert key into a fleet-wide hard failure, so arming a key on a strict action is the case to verify before, not after. Cheapest end-to-end proof is one real item: arm on ONE definition, watch a single work item complete, then arm the rest.
- **and when you disarm:** prove the recovery with DEMAND — a completed item after the rollback, not an absence of failures (the hour before this incident also had zero completions, because nothing was queued). `WHERE error LIKE '%<key>%'` is NOT a failure census: the `error` column keeps its text after a row later succeeds, and it reported two fresh failures here that were both `complete`.
- **relations:** `bugs_closed/336` (this — closed 2026-08-20 14:40Z once a real page stamped a content_hash through the armed path; filed as `bugs_open/336`, so grep BOTH dirs) · `bugs_open/315` / `architecture_review/RFC_038` (the change being armed) · `bugs_open/234` and this action's three retired keys (why `StrictConfig` exists and must NOT be relaxed to paper over a misplacement) · MEMORY `cite-the-arm-not-the-function` (the citation was real and about something else) · MEMORY `a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control`
- **added:** 2026-08-20, webdesign_tool_rebuilds lane (found as a blocked served-page grade, not as a config review)

## A pointer that hardcodes `bugs_open/` rots at exactly the moment it starts to matter — and where it is stamped into a row ONCE, a later fix cannot repair the rows already stamped

- **footprint:** `scheduled_tasks` `name='held-pair-canary-escalation'` (its `pre_query`, and the `owners (item_type, owner) AS (VALUES …)` CTE inside it) · `site_work_items.result->'held_pair_escalation'->>'owner'` · `resolution_path='auto:held_pair_escalated'` · migrations `453`/`466`/`479`/`497` · **and generally: any config value, prompt, seed or map that names a bug as `bugs_open/NNN`**
- **fires when:** you write a pointer to an owning lane into config — an escalation owner, a routing hint, a "see also" in an agent prompt — and spell it with a directory prefix. Nothing is wrong at the time. It rots **when the lane you pointed at SUCCEEDS**, because `bugs_open/` → `bugs_closed/` is precisely what closing a bug *does*. So the pointer is guaranteed to be dead by the time somebody follows it, and it dies **silently**: no query fails, no row errors, the config still reads like a well-maintained map.
- **⚠ the half that makes it expensive: some of these maps are ONE-SHOT.** `owners` is read by the `escalated` UPDATE and stamped into `result.held_pair_escalation.owner` **at escalation time, then never revisited**. A migration that fixes the map does **not** retro-fix a row already escalated. So a wrong entry is not "stale config" — it is a wrong instruction handed to a person, once, permanently, at the only moment they were going to read it. Before you deprioritise fixing one of these, check whether it is stamped or re-read: the two have completely different urgency, and the stamped kind has a **deadline** (here, a daily 12:57Z tick).
- **it is measured, not prospective.** `[MEASURED 2026-08-20 06:49Z]` **all three** entries in that map were dead or wrong: `placeholder_contact` → `bugs_open/201` and `literal_markdown` → `bugs_open/184 + bugs_open/201`, **none of which exist** (checked at HEAD with `git ls-tree`, all three matching files under `bugs_closed/`); and `page_component_status_drift` → `(UNASSIGNED - claim this) … no lane doc claims it` while `bugs_open/300` owns it, open with its fix live. **The only escalation this family has EVER produced** (2026-08-17T12:57:43Z) carries that `(UNASSIGNED` string in its `result` — so at n=1 of 1 the map has already misled a human. Fixed by migration `497`.
- **the check, and it is two questions not one:** (1) `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD -- bugs_open/ bugs_closed/ | grep -E '/(NNN)_'` — **never `ls`**, because a `git mv` staged by another session makes the working tree disagree with HEAD. (2) Is the value **stamped or re-read**? Grep for the field in a `jsonb_build_object` inside an `UPDATE`: if it is written into a row, every past row is already wrong and only future ones are fixable.
- **write it so it cannot rot:** name a bug by **NUMBER and SLUG**, never by directory, and let the reader grep both — a bare number is ambiguous anyway (`184` alone names two unrelated cases; `016`, `017`, `083`, `112`, `131`, `146` likewise). Name the **lane directory**, which does not move when a bug closes. `497` writes this rule into the map itself, beside the values, because correcting the three strings alone would have re-armed the same trap for the next close.
- **⚠ AND WHEN YOU CORRECT ONE, TWO SECOND-ORDER TRAPS, both of which fired in `497`'s own authoring:**
  - **A "no `bugs_open/` remains" assertion is TRIPPED BY ITS OWN REMEDY.** The rule comment you insert says *"NEVER write a `bugs_open/` … PREFIX"* — so the remedy text contains the token the check counts, and the count comes out one too high. **Counting a token cannot distinguish a live pointer, a dead pointer, and a prohibition against writing one.** Assert the specific claims instead: dead pointer = 0, **and the live one = its exact count, as a POSITIVE control** that you did not eat the prose you must not touch.
  - **A surgical `pre_query` edit needs a REVERSE-REPLACEMENT control, and it must be driven from the same variables as the forward edit.** Presence/absence checks on your new strings are near-vacuous: they pass identically whether or not the `replace()` also mangled 10 KB of unrelated `what_to_do` prose, which is the only damage such a file can plausibly do. Put the new strings back and assert the md5 returns to the pre-image — that can fail, and **mutation-prove it** (damage one byte of unrelated prose; it must fail). Declare the old/new strings **once** and use them in both directions: `497`'s first draft wrote the undo out by hand, one anchor was a *prefix* of the line it meant to remove, and the control caught the asymmetry before the file was ever run. A control transcribed a second time tests the transcription, not the change.
  - **and the bytes being right does not prove the SQL still RUNS.** `pre_query` is text the scheduler executes; a broken literal fails every tick, silently, until someone reads the task. Execute it rolled back — `CREATE TEMP TABLE t AS <pre_query>` inside the open transaction — which both proves it parses and previews exactly what the next tick will write.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/083` (this task's parent mechanism) · `bugs_open/300` (the item type the map called unassigned) · `bugs_open/333` (why the `reason` field beside it also understates the case) · `bugs_open/314` (a migration under `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/` is refused by the council gate client-side, so this class of fix gets no review) · the existing `watching_detail` entry for the same task · MEMORY [[declaring-a-key-silences-your-own-detector]] (same family, opposite direction — here the remedy *tripped* the detector) · MEMORY [[a-handoff-outlives-the-work-it-asked-for]] · MEMORY [[mutate-the-code-to-prove-the-guard]]
- **⚠ ADDED 2026-08-22 by the 040 lane — THE SCALE, and this entry is itself an instance.** The entry above measures three values in one `scheduled_tasks` map, which reads as "a trap in one config row". It is not. `[MEASURED 2026-08-22]` across every `.go` and `.md` outside `bugs_closed/`, counting **occurrences** not files:

  | `bugs_open/NNN` pointers | this lane, at HEAD | `029` lane, independent, at HEAD |
  |---|---|---|
  | pointing at a bug that is now **CLOSED** — i.e. already dead | **9,242** in **2,120 files** | **9,243** |
  | pointing at a bug still open *(positive control)* | 3,711 | 3,715 |
  | ambiguous (that number exists in BOTH dirs) | 755 | 755 |
  | **dead share of resolvable pointers** | **71.4%** | **71.3%** |

  Worst single numbers, agreeing exactly across both runs: `083` (282 occurrences), `029` (229), `213` (191), `260` (174). **So the default state of a directory-prefixed bug pointer on this estate is DEAD**, and "check before you follow one" is not caution, it is the base rate.

  **INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED, which is why the headline is worth trusting and the exact count is not.** Two lanes wrote the counter from scratch, ~20 minutes apart, and landed within 0.1 points. The residual drift is commits arriving between runs — **the count is a rate, not a constant, and quoting it to four figures would be false precision.** Cite it as **~71%**; re-run if you need better, and expect a different number.

  ⚠ **THE FIGURE FIRST PUBLISHED HERE (9,293 / 3,707 / 751, 71.5%) WAS MEASURED THE WAY THIS VERY ENTRY SAYS NEVER TO MEASURE.** It walked the WORKING TREE, so it counted other sessions' uncommitted edits; "the check" three bullets above says `git ls-tree … HEAD` — *"never `ls`, because a `git mv` staged by another session makes the working tree disagree with HEAD"*. The `029` lane used HEAD, and the disagreement showed up exactly where you would predict: the worst-singles differed (`083` 281 vs 282, `029` 231 vs 229) while the headline barely moved. **Corrected to HEAD above.** The effect was small and the method was still wrong — recorded because appending a measurement to a landmine while breaking that landmine's own stated check is the most on-the-nose way possible to demonstrate that reading an entry is not the same as applying it.

  **This entry's own `relations:` line is one of them, and it rotted in under two days.** It cites `bugs_open/083` — closed `dc47eb082`, 2026-08-22, *"owner instruction"* — and `bugs_open/314`, also closed. Written 08-20 by an author warning about exactly this, correct at the time, dead by the time you are reading it. **Left in place deliberately rather than silently repaired**, because the entry is more useful carrying a live example of its own subject than it would be tidied. `300` and `333` are still open, so the line is *partly* live, which is the worst readable state: nothing about it looks broken.

  **What to do with this number, and what NOT to do.** Do **not** launch a sweep — 9,293 occurrences across 2,131 files span every lane, most are historical prose where the prefix was true when written, and a mass rewrite would be an unreviewable diff touching work nobody asked you to touch. The measurement's use is different: **when you follow a `bugs_open/NNN` pointer and it does not resolve, that is the normal case, not evidence of anything** — `ls bugs_closed/NNN_*` before concluding the reference was wrong or the bug imaginary. And when you WRITE one, use the number+slug+lane-dir form above, which is the only part of this that is cheap and compounding.

  ⚠ **Counting method, because two obvious ones are wrong — one by 3×, one silently.** (1) A first pass counted *files matching each closed number* and summed, giving **6,208** — inflated, because a file citing five closed bugs counts five times. Count OCCURRENCES, resolve each against **both** directories, and bucket the reused numbers separately instead of guessing. (2) Resolve against **HEAD**, not the working tree — see the correction above. The live count is a **positive control**: if it came back 0 the classifier would be broken, not the estate clean.

  ⚠ **AND THE SECOND-ORDER TRAP FIRES ON THIS ENTRY TOO, exactly as the bullet below predicts.** Any "no dead pointer remains" grep run over this file returns non-zero, because this entry *quotes* `bugs_open/083`, `bugs_open/314` and `bugs_open/NNN` as its subject matter — and one of those is a deliberately-preserved live instance. The `029` lane hit the identical thing verifying its own fix. **Assert the specific claims, never a token count:** live pointers = 0, **and** each surviving hit asserted to BE a quotation, as a positive control that you did not eat the prose you must not touch.

  **The runnable form for THIS entry, with its expected answer, so the next person does not re-derive it.** Scope the block by the next `##`/`###` **heading** — *not* the next `---`, which appears inside its own tables and rules; a first attempt scoped that way silently swallowed six later entries and returned a `False` that was an artefact of the extraction, not a finding. Correctly scoped, the dead pointers inside this entry are exactly:

  | pointer | why it is here and must NOT be "fixed" |
  |---|---|
  | `083`, `314` | the deliberately-preserved live instances of this entry's own subject (see above) |
  | `184`, `201` | the 08-20 author's **quoted evidence** — the entry's own sentence says *"none of which exist"*. Repairing a pointer that a measurement cites AS dead destroys the measurement |

  and the live ones are `040`, `300`, `333`. **If your run returns that set, the entry is intact; if it returns fewer, you have eaten someone's evidence.** ⚠ And when an assertion like this fails, check whether your EXPECTATION was wrong before concluding the file is — mine predicted `{083, 314}` and the two it missed were quoted evidence, which is the same class of thing it was written to protect.
- **source:** 2026-08-20, found during the `bugfix_277` lane's session-start checklist — not from a symptom, and not from anything that looked wrong; **scale measured 2026-08-22 by the `040` lane**, prompted by the `029` lane finding it had written its *second* dead pointer in two days into `wedge-evidence-capture/base/check.py` and correctly reading that as the pointer SHAPE failing rather than two unlucky addresses
