### `llm_call_log.agent_type` is NOT "which agent's workflow made this call" — an acceptance test keyed on it reads ZERO after a demonstrably successful run

- **footprint:** `llm_call_log.agent_type` · any "has agent X ever made an LLM call / is X dormant / did my fix make X run?" question · any bug file whose §How to verify names `llm_call_log WHERE agent_type='<handler>'` · `bugs_closed/313`, `bugs_closed/298`
- **fires when:** you are proving a workflow's LLM step now executes — the natural acceptance test, and a good one in shape, because `SELECT count(*) FROM llm_call_log WHERE agent_type='<agent>'` is often genuinely zero beforehand, so the "before" arm looks unfakeable.
- **the tell: there is none.** The query returns `0`, which is exactly what it returned before the fix, and `0` is a well-formed answer to a question you did have. Measured 2026-08-19: correlation `50ea3037` ran `internal-linker`'s `plan_links` step to success — 21,946 input / 446 output tokens, a 2-link plan returned, 2 `content_rewrite` rows filed with `created_by='internal-linker'` — and `WHERE agent_type='internal-linker'` **still counted zero**, because the row landed under **`agent_type='generic'`**. That column carries the DISPATCH context (the client/topic the orchestration arrived on), not the agent type of the workflow that owns the step.
- **why this direction is the expensive one:** it fails toward *"not proven yet"*, on a fix that works. A dormancy or not-yet-verified claim built on it is unfalsifiable-looking and self-reinforcing — the next reader quotes the zero as evidence the agent is still dead, and the bug stays open indefinitely. `bugs_open/298` originally drew the opposite (and equally wrong) conclusion from the same zero: "dormant, never dispatched", when the zero was a symptom of the routing bug two steps away.
- **the check — key on a column the MECHANISM must write, not one the dispatcher stamps:**
  ```sql
  -- the step name is written by the step itself; the correlation ties it to your run
  SELECT created_at, agent_type, step_name, success, input_tokens, output_tokens
  FROM llm_call_log WHERE step_name='<the step>' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5;
  ```
  Before adopting ANY label-keyed acceptance test, confirm the label is populated the way you assume: `SELECT agent_type, count(*) FROM llm_call_log WHERE created_at > now() - interval '3 days' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;` — `generic` carrying dozens of rows while no handler agent has a per-workflow label is the disclosure. **"Cannot be faked" is a claim about the BEFORE arm and says nothing about whether the AFTER arm is reachable — state both, or you have written an unsatisfiable test.**
- **scope, stated honestly:** [MEASURED] for a hand-fired inline-`config.workflow` dispatch on `system.agent.generic.requests`. Whether a loop-dispatched `spawn_agent` run labels `agent_type` with the handler is **UNMEASURED** — which is itself the point: if you cannot say which dispatch paths label it how, you cannot use it as an acceptance test. `step_name` is correct on every path.
- **relation:** the direct sibling of the `orchestration_states.owner_agent_type` entry above ("NOT which agent ran — reads ZERO for a demonstrably active agent"). Same failure, different table, and the `bugfix_313` lane cited that entry and then built its acceptance test on this column anyway — so knowing about one does not protect you from the other. If you are about to identify an agent by a column *other* than the config row you read it from, assume the column means something adjacent until you have proved otherwise.
- **source:** 2026-08-19, session `bugs_open/taken 313 and 298 and 314`, while supplying the artefact proof the `bugfix_313_internal_linker` lane had left as its sole remaining gate. Both bug files carried the broken test; both corrected in place. WRONG_CALLS 2026-08-19.
- **added:** 2026-08-19

### After a `cat >` over a shared file, git CANNOT tell you whether you destroyed uncommitted work — a destroyed-then-retyped paragraph and a written-once-late paragraph leave IDENTICAL traces. The only witness is the authoring session, so ASK IT

- **footprint:** any `cat >` / `>` / `tee` over a file in `docs/agent_docs/`, `bugs_open/`, `bugs_closed/`, `architecture_review/` or `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/`; `git show <sha>:<path> > <path>` restores; `scripts/memory-git-snapshot.py`; any claim of the form "nothing was lost" / "restored byte-identically"
- **⚠ `>>` IS DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE, and keeping that crisp is what preserves this entry's force.** Append cannot produce the two-histories ambiguity — it destroys nothing, so there is no lost-vs-retyped question to ask. An append-only file (`WRONG_CALLS.md`, `LANDMINES.md`, `NOTES_*`) written with `cat >>` is **outside this entry even though it is a shell redirect**. Cite it at a truncating write or not at all; cited at appends it becomes noise and stops being read where it matters. (The redirect-vs-Write rule in CLAUDE.md still applies to appends for other reasons — this entry is about *recoverability*, not about which tool to reach for.)
- **fires when:** you overwrite a shared-tree file you did not create, notice, and restore it from git — then try to establish that the restore was lossless. It reads as settled and it is not.
- **the mechanism:** the snapshot hook (and git generally) captures the state **before** the clobber, which is exactly what you need to restore — but it records **nothing** about uncommitted content that existed in the tree at the moment you wrote. So consider a paragraph that appears for the first time in a commit made *after* your restore. Two histories produce that identical trace: (a) the author wrote it after your restore — nothing was lost; (b) the author wrote it **before** your clobber, left it uncommitted, your write destroyed it, and they re-typed it from memory afterwards, possibly without noticing. **`git log -S` dates the first COMMIT, never the first KEYSTROKE**, so it cannot separate them. A re-authored paragraph is not a preserved one, and (b) also means your "nothing was lost" is false while looking verified.
- **worked case, 2026-08-19/20 (`bugs_open/029`):** I overwrote another session's cold-start handoff with `cat >` at 22:15 and restored from a 21:06 commit at 22:17. A `SUPERSEDED` banner of theirs first appears at **22:21:40**, four minutes after the restore. Its author had told me they wrote it "~21:1xZ" — which, if true, would have put it inside my clobber window. **Unresolvable from git by either of us.** Settled only by the authoring session checking its own transcript: two `Edit` calls running continuously into that commit, `+16/-2`, **one** `Edit` issued — authored once, after the restore. Nothing lost. Their "~21:1x" was an unchecked estimate they had used as evidence.
- **the check, and it is a QUESTION, not a query:** after any overwrite of a shared file, **ask the authoring session "did you type this once or twice?"** — routinely, not as a one-off. Then record the answer as **attested by that session and unverifiable from git**, never as measured. Corollaries: `git log -S '<distinctive phrase>' -- <path>` gives you the commit boundary and is the right *starting* point; a first-appearance strictly after your restore is the shape that **demands** the question rather than answering it; and never write "nothing was lost" on the strength of a diff alone.
- **relations:** CLAUDE.md, "Read before write on any file you did not create; prefer the Write tool, which refuses an unread file, over a shell redirect, which does not" — **the Write tool would have refused this file and is the actual prevention** · `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-19 (worked a lane another session owned, then overwrote their handoff) and its 2026-08-20 addendum · MEMORY [[a-subagent-report-is-another-doc]]
- **source:** 2026-08-19/20, `bugfix_029_retry_kills_live_child` and the peer `029` session, jointly — neither could settle it alone
- **added:** 2026-08-20, 029 lane

### After the `bugs_open/327` fix rolls, the FIRST trivial write to one of the three shrunken briefs silently RESTORES ~10,000 chars of instruction — and every page written afterwards changes character for a reason nobody logged

- **footprint:** `site_specs` (aspect `content_direction`) on `ai-agent-orchestration.com`, `robot-hands.com`, `leopardessconsulting.co.uk` · `write_site_spec` / `WriteSiteSpecAction` · `page-content-writer` · any migration, operator script, HITL edit or classifier re-run that writes `content_direction` on those three sites
- **fires when:** you make **any** `content_direction` write on one of those sites after the fix is live — a one-key tweak, a tagline correction, a classifier re-run. Nothing about your edit says "and also restore four months of missing brief".
- **the trap, and note it is the INVERSE of the two entries above:** the fix rebuilds `formatted` from the **merged** document, so the first write of any size re-renders **every key the document has accumulated since 2026-04-18**. On `ai-agent-orchestration.com` that is 3,558 → ~10,000 chars: twelve keys returning at once, including `writing_rules`, `things_to_avoid` and `example_phrases`. **The brief triples as a side effect of a one-line edit, and every page written afterwards is written against instructions that have not been in play since April.** The repair is correct and it is also a large, unannounced content change attributable to the wrong edit — a lane will see its copy change character and have nothing in its own diff to explain it.
- ⚠ **UPDATED 2026-08-24 — the transfer risk is HIGHER than the figure this entry originally leaned on.** The `apis_uk_bees_homepage` lane rewrote one site's `example_phrases` and measured the result: **a vivid, complete, on-topic exemplar is not imitated as style, it is LIFTED AS CONTENT** — one came back verbatim as the hero subheadline, another opened three separate sections. Their finding: *"the originals were partly metaphor (which did not transfer) and the replacements were all plain concrete statements (which did)"*. So exemplar transfer is a function of the exemplar's CHARACTER, not a flat rate, and this lane's fleet-wide 3-of-52 average under-reads the concrete, on-topic end. Judge the returning exemplars themselves; do not lean on the average (`WRONG_CALLS` 2026-08-24).
- ⚠ **and on at least one site part of what returns makes a known fault WORSE.** `ai-agent-orchestration.com`'s restored `example_phrases.characteristic` is itself written in the define-by-negation construction the owner objected to (`bugs_open/305`) — *"Agents fail in isolation — not in cascades"*, *"Speed comes from engineering discipline, not from skipping the hard parts"*. On this estate's measured principle that the example is the instruction, restoring that key unchanged pushes the writer **towards** the complaint.
- **the check, before you write to one of those three:** read what is about to come back, and decide about it deliberately —
  ```
  docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/copy_quality_two_stage/audit_writer_brief.py <domain>
  ```
  Section 2 lists exactly the keys that will reappear, largest first. Fix or delete the ones you do not want restored **in the same write**, because there is no second chance: once `formatted` is rebuilt, the next page render uses it. On the other two sites nobody has yet read the returning keys at all.
- **why it is a landmine rather than a line in the bug file:** the damage lands on whoever makes the next unrelated edit, not on whoever fixed the bug, and it looks like their change caused it. The three sites are all **other lanes'**.
- **source:** `bugs_open/327` (slug `a_partial_spec_write_silently_shrinks_the_brief_the_writer_reads` — the number is ambiguous); fix `c9a71388f`, inert until the next chassis roll
- **relations:** the two sibling entries above (the partial-write collapse this fixes, and the random-order rendering) · `bugs_open/305` · register CQ-025 / SPEC-002's 2026-08-20 correction
- **added:** 2026-08-20, copy_quality_two_stage lane

### `rerender_pages_actions.go`'s whole-page path is DEAD CODE — its head render, its contact-info block and `RenderTemplateWithMap` cannot be dispatched, and nothing in the file says so

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/rerender_pages_actions.go` · `RerenderSitePagesAction` · `rerenderSinglePage` · `rerenderInjectContactInfo` · `RenderTemplateWithMap` · `platform/orchestration/actions/registry.go` / `GlobalActionRegistry`
- **fires when:** you audit, fix, cite or size a render defect and this file's ~600 lines of page assembly are in scope. Everything about it reads live — it is committed, it compiles, it is referenced by the concept register and by two bug files, and `rerender_pages` even appears in live agent configs.
- **the trap:** `RenderTemplateWithMap` ← `rerenderInjectContactInfo` ← `rerenderSinglePage` ← `RerenderSitePagesAction`, and **`RerenderSitePagesAction` appears in NO entry of `GlobalActionRegistry`** (320 handlers, checked 2026-08-19). No workflow can reach it, and the linker eliminates the leaf — which is what the `idea_uk_vm_site` lane was seeing when it recorded `RenderTemplateWithMap` as **absent from the binary** and could not explain why. A fix here is defensive, for a path someone may revive; it stops nothing today. Size a defect off this file and you will overstate it.
- ⚠ **the near-miss that makes this worth an entry: `rerender_pages` IS in live agent configs, and it is not this action.** A count of live definitions naming it returns 3, which reads as "dispatched". It is a **step name** — what those rows carry is `rerender_pages.pages`, the output field of `get_pages_for_rerender` (see `create_rerender_items_action.go`'s `pages_field` default). The registered rerender actions are `rerender_single_page` (→ `RerenderSinglePageAction`, which uses `assemblePage` and never touches this file) and `rerender_page_sections`.
- **the check, one command, and it is the registry not the grep:**
  ```
  grep -n '"<action_name>"' platform/orchestration/actions/registry.go     # registered?
  grep -rn "<ExportedActionFunc>\b" --include=*.go . | grep -v "_actions\?\.go:"   # anyone else calling it?
  ```
  An exported `…Action` function with no registry entry and no non-test caller is **unreachable**, however live its file looks. Do this before writing "this path is live", "latent", or "one edit away" — and note that a DB query naming the string can only tell you a config mentions it, never that the binary can dispatch it.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/260` §13g (whose "latent, one ordinary edit away" claim this refutes, corrected 2026-08-20) · `bugs_open/238`'s council round, which enumerated this seam as one of eight unguarded call sites · register `STY-057` · `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-20 · the two seams' languages also diverge — see the next entry
- **added:** 2026-08-20, bugs_open/260 renderer-half lane

### An EMPTY STRING in an array-declared field is normal, gated and live — a declared-type check that calls it a violation refuses a healthy page, and exactly one row on the estate proves it

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/content_type_violations.go` (`ContentTypeViolations`, `IsEmptyContentValue`, `DeclaredTypeSatisfied`) · `platform/orchestration/actions/json_envelope.go` (`missingRequiredLLMFields`, `isEmptyContentValue`) · `refuse_mistyped_llm_fields` · `content_components.input_schema` fields declaring `type: array`/`list`
- **fires when:** you write, tighten or reuse any check comparing `page_components.content_data` against a component's declared field types — the obvious first version tests `jsonb_typeof(...) <> 'array'` or `_, ok := v.([]interface{})` and reports everything that is not a slice.
- **the trap:** a declared-array field holding `""` is **not** a type error, it is "not filled in", and templates on this estate gate on it (`{{if $s.branches}}` before `{{range $s.branches}}`). `fundamentallyai.com` `/production-backend-engineering` stores five `mechanism-flow` `steps[].branches` as the empty string, renders clean, 8,824 bytes, no braces, **deployed and serving since 2026-08-15**. The first version of `ContentTypeViolations` flagged all five — so an armed pre-render gate would have refused a rebuild of a live, correct page. It is the **only** row of that shape on the estate, so no hand-written unit test would have found it, and a test suite that passes here proves nothing.
- **the check, in two parts:**
  1. **Share the emptiness predicate, do not re-derive it.** `datahelpers.IsEmptyContentValue` (nil, blank/whitespace string, empty slice, empty map) is the definition the PRESENCE gate uses; a type check that disagrees with it makes two gates contradict each other about one field. Only a value that is actually THERE can contradict its declared type.
  2. **Census before arming, not after.** Run the population query in `sql_for_agents/502_bugfix_260_arm_mistyped_llm_fields_HOLD.sql`'s header — top-level AND the nested `items` case, over every stored row — and **read the rows, not just the count**. A non-zero result that is all empty strings means your predicate is wrong; a non-zero result that is not means those pages will stop rebuilding.
- **why prospective:** the wrong version passes every test you would write, refuses nothing in CI, and only bites the one live page shaped like the exception — after the gate is armed, on a rebuild nobody connects to the check.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/260` (the seam this diagnoses for) · register `STY-057` (coverage + absent-field landmines) · `RFC_041` §5 · `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-20 ("what would this refuse today" is the only estate-wide test) · MEMORY [[declaring-a-key-silences-your-own-detector]] — same family: your own check can be blind or over-eager, and only the live population tells you which
- ⚠ **the verifier's `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` on this entry (2026-08-20 09:17Z) is the INDEX being behind, not a fault in the entry.** It reports `content_type_violations.go` and its three functions as "0 rows", and says why in its own evidence line: it answers for indexed commit `c2ccc345`, **"the last pushed tip, not the present tree"** (2026-08-18 21:02Z), while this file and its functions are in local commits `80b9c6235`/`1763bc4e5` on an unpushed branch. It confirmed the half it *could* see (`missingRequiredLLMFields` L451-474, `isEmptyContentValue` L478-490). **The general form, worth more than this instance: a landmine-verifier verdict on a brand-new entry is a statement about the pushed tip.** Re-verify after a push; do not "fix" a footprint the index simply cannot see yet.
- ⚠ **THE OTHER HALF, 2026-08-24: `DeclaredTypeSatisfied` is DEFAULT-TRUE, so declaring a type name is NOT validated and a TYPO passes exactly like a correct type.** The entry above warns this check can be too STRICT; this is the same function being unable to be strict at all outside one case:
  ```go
  switch declared {
  case "array", "list": _, ok := v.([]interface{}); return ok
  default:              return true   // <- everything else
  }
  ```
  Only `array`/`list` are examined. `text`, `html`, `hmtl`, `HTML`, `""` and any string a component author invents all return true, and `declaredTypeOf` is a bare `def["type"].(string)` map read with no validation behind it either. **So "my new field type passes the type check" is NEVER evidence the type name is recognised — nothing recognises type names.**
  - **fires when:** you introduce or retype a field type in `content_components.input_schema`, or read a passing type check as confirmation that a schema edit landed correctly. Live case: a peer lane's migration retyping **5** pass-through prose slots from `type: text` to `type: html` on the strength of "DeclaredTypeSatisfied passes html untouched" — true, and true for a reason that grants no safety.
  - **the check, and it is the only one that discriminates:** after any such migration read the values back LITERALLY — `SELECT function, jsonb_path_query_array(input_schema, '$.**.type') FROM content_components WHERE ...` — and assert the string equals what you intended. The type checker cannot fail on a typo, so the assertion has to be on the STORED LITERAL. Corollary for reviewers: an author citing a passing type check as evidence their retype is correct has cited nothing.
  - **[UNMEASURED]** how many distinct `type:` strings exist fleet-wide, i.e. whether typo'd types are already live. One `jsonb_path_query` census would answer it; nobody has run one.
  - **added:** 2026-08-24, staged_component_build lane (surfaced answering a cross-session question from the `bugs_open/381` lane; I read the function, not their migration)
- **added:** 2026-08-20, bugs_open/260 renderer-half lane

### An ARRAY OF OBJECTS in a `content_direction` spec is discarded silently — the write succeeds, the document keeps it, and it reaches no prompt

- **footprint:** `site_specs` (aspect `content_direction`) · `datahelpers.FormatContentDirection` / `FormatSpecValue` / `InterfaceSliceToStrings` (`format_content_direction.go`) · `write_site_spec` · any agent, migration or operator script authoring a structured list in a brief
- **fires when:** you add a list of OBJECTS to a brief — the natural shape for something like `example_phrases: [{phrase: "...", when: "..."}]` or a list of `{do, dont}` pairs. The write succeeds and the document stores it exactly as given.
- **the trap:** the writer never sees it. `FormatSpecValue`'s array branch calls `InterfaceSliceToStrings`, which **keeps only elements that are strings** and silently skips the rest; an all-objects array therefore formats to the empty string and the whole key vanishes from `formatted` — the one field the page writer reads. It looks identical to the `bugs_open/327` partial-write drop, and to a key you simply forgot to write. Nested MAPS are fine (they recurse); it is arrays whose elements are not strings that go. `[MEASURED 2026-08-20]` **zero live instances across all 25 current specs** — so this is a trap waiting for the first author who reaches for the tidier shape, not a live defect.
- **the check:** after adding any list-valued key to a brief, confirm it arrived — `audit_writer_brief.py <domain>`, section 2, expect your key NOT to be listed as dropped. Or in one line: its humanised label must appear in `data->>'formatted'`. **Keep list elements as strings** (a sentence per element, which is what every current spec does) unless you are also changing the formatter.
- **why it is here rather than in a bug file:** there is nothing to fix yet and no failure to reproduce. The formatter's behaviour is reasonable for the data it was written for; the trap is that the data shape is unconstrained and the loss is silent. Found while measuring spec depth to answer a council objection, not by anything going wrong.
- **source:** `bugs_open/327`'s council round 1 (the editquality depth objection and the shape census that answered it), 2026-08-20
- **relations:** the three sibling entries above (partial-write collapse, random-order rendering, and the post-fix restoration) · register CQ-025
- **added:** 2026-08-20, copy_quality_two_stage lane

### A `page-rerender` dispatched without `spec.page_name` throws away everything it re-rendered, reports `success: true`, and then DEPLOYS the stale HTML — the orchestration reads COMPLETED throughout

- **footprint:** `page-rerender` agent (`agent_definitions`, steps `check_rerender_mode` / `rerender_sections` / `save_sections` / `render_page` / `deploy_page`) · `platform/orchestration/actions/save_page_sections_action.go:132-140` · any hand-built kcat envelope carrying `input_data.spec` · `scripts/initial_messages/001_assemble_all_pages_rerender/*`
- **fires when:** you fix a CTA/href/copy value in `page_components.content_data` and dispatch a rerender by hand to push it to the page — the normal way to close a bug whose defect lives in stored data.
- **the trap, in two independent layers, and BOTH report success:**
  1. **No `spec.reason` ⇒ the sections are never re-rendered at all.** `check_rerender_mode` is a `conditional` whose own description says it plainly: *"Re-render sections only for re-render reasons; else assemble stored HTML"*. The reason must be one of `image_landed`, `section_data_resolved`, `cta_links_stale`, `template_changed`, `literal_markdown`. Anything else (including nothing) routes to `render_page`, which **assembles the components' STORED `rendered_html`** — so a `content_data` fix cannot reach the page, and the deploy ships the old bytes.
  2. **No `spec.page_name` ⇒ the sections ARE re-rendered and then discarded.** The step reads `page_name_field: input_data.spec.page_name`; with it missing, `SavePageSectionsAction` returns `{"success": true, "sections_saved": 0, "skipped": true, "reason": "no page name"}` — **success true** — and the workflow proceeds to `render_page`/`deploy_page`, deploying the stale assembly. Observed 2026-08-20: `rerendered: 4, sections_saved: 0`, deploy `success`, orchestration `COMPLETED`, page unchanged.
- **why the wrong answer looks right:** every surface a session normally checks says it worked. The orchestration is `COMPLETED`; `deploy_result.success` is `true`; a real git commit exists with a real sha and a real `files_count`. The only thing that disagrees is the artefact. `sections_metadata` even lists four component ids **that exist nowhere** — they are minted for the render and never persisted, so joining them to `page_components` returns zero rows and tells you nothing unless you thought to look.
- **the check — assert on the SAVE and on the ARTEFACT, never on the status:**
  ```sql
  SELECT collected_data->'sections_saved'->>'sections_saved' AS saved,
         collected_data->'sections_saved'->>'reason'         AS skip_reason,
         collected_data->'rerender_sections'->>'rerendered'  AS rerendered
    FROM orchestration_states WHERE orchestration_id = '<yours>';
  -- saved must be NON-ZERO and equal rerendered; a `reason` of "no page name" means
  -- your envelope was wrong, not that the page was already correct.
  ```
  Then read the component row itself — `updated_at` must have MOVED, and `rendered_html` must contain the new value:
  ```sql
  SELECT pc.updated_at, (pc.rendered_html LIKE '%<new value>%') AS html_has_it
    FROM page_components pc JOIN pages p ON p.id=pc.page_id WHERE …;
  ```
  A row whose `updated_at` still equals the timestamp of *your own SQL fix* is the tell that the rerender never touched it.
- **the working envelope** (both keys present):
  `{"action":"orchestrate","config":{"agent_type":"page-rerender"},"input_data":{"site_id":"…","domain":"…","page_id":"…","spec":{"reason":"cta_links_stale","page_name":"index"}}}`
  ⚠ `cta_links_stale` is only safe on a binary carrying bug 299's KEEP #3 (chassis ≥ v1.0.1317) — on an older one that reason IS the clobber trigger (register LNK-034).
- **why production does not hit it:** real work items carry `spec.page_name`, so this is a hand-dispatch hazard. But the SHAPE is the estate's most-repeated failure: a skip that returns `success: true` is indistinguishable from work done, and here it is followed by a deploy that makes the staleness look freshly published.
- **relations:** this file's *"The save seam's identity paths resolve to NOTHING inside the page writer's own run"* (adjacent but different — that one is about an UNATTRIBUTABLE record; this one is about DISCARDED work shipped under a success status) · MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] · [[repro-regenerated-from-source-is-destroyed-by-the-render]] (the sibling direction: a rerender regenerates from `content_data`, so it cannot reproduce a defect living in `rendered_html` — and, as here, will not fix one either unless it actually saves) · `bugs_open/299`
- **source:** 2026-08-20, `bugfix_299_cta_dials_phone` lane · orchestrations `2ea0cbe4` (no reason → assembled stale), `0ed191f2` (reason, no page_name → `sections_saved: 0`), `aab8de08` (both → `sections_saved: 4`, artefact correct)
- **added:** 2026-08-20, bugfix_299_cta_dials_phone lane

## A component whose `content_data` CANNOT REPRODUCE its own `rendered_html` — the page looks perfect, and every repair route that regenerates from `content_data` is inapplicable to it BY CONSTRUCTION

- **footprint:** `page_components.content_data` vs `content_components.html_template` · the `Ported Page (webdesign.co.uk)` component (115 instances) and any `schema: *-page.v1` / ported / adopted-verbatim component · `datahelpers.StripLiteralMarkdownFromContentData` · `rerender_page_sections` / `rerender_single_page` · `apply_section_edit` (`content_edit`) · `RenderTemplate` -> `component_library.go:1062` -> `executeGoTemplate` (`call_agent.go:1171`, `Option("missingkey=zero")`) · `literalMarkdownFinding.Source` · migrations `473` / `474`
- **fires when:** you pick a repair route for a finding on a page, and reason about it the way everyone does — *is this route allowed here (ownership, guards, policy), and does it have a good record?* Both questions can answer YES while the route is **incapable** of touching the defect, because the content it would rewrite is not in `content_data` at all. The page renders fine, so nothing looks wrong; the component's stored `rendered_html` is complete and correct, and `content_data` is a stub.
- **[MEASURED 2026-08-20]** `Ported Page (webdesign.co.uk)`: **115 instances, 100 of which hold NONE of their template's fields.** `content_data` is `{schema, sha256, source, qa_tier, generator}` — 215 bytes of provenance metadata — while the template's only field is `{{.body}}` and `rendered_html` is 2.7–23.9 KB of ported prose. **The split is total and is the tell: all 100 missing-`body` instances are `rebuild_policy='owned'`; all 15 that carry `body` are `generic`.**
- **⚠ THIS IS WHY "OWNED PAGES CANNOT BE REPAIRED" IS THE WRONG DIAGNOSIS.** Ownership and un-regenerability *coincide* on this component, so the ownership guard gets the blame and every proposed fix is about routing around it. Route around it successfully and you still repair nothing — there is no source to regenerate from. **Ownership is the correlate; the operative property is whether the content is reachable from `content_data`.** Three separate routes were proposed and measured against the wrong property in two days (`bugs_open/277` §5).
- **the check, and it is two lines of SQL — do it BEFORE costing a route:**
  ```sql
  -- do the template's fields actually exist as content_data keys?
  WITH t AS (SELECT id, ARRAY(SELECT DISTINCT (regexp_matches(html_template,'\{\{\s*\.([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)','g'))[1]) f
             FROM content_components WHERE id = '<component_id>')
  SELECT pc.id, COALESCE(pc.content_data,'{}'::jsonb) ?| t.f AS can_regenerate
  FROM t JOIN page_components pc ON pc.component_id = t.id;
  ```
  And read the finding's own `source` first: `spec.findings[].source` is `content_data | rendered_html`, with `field` **empty for rendered_html**. **A `rendered_html`-source finding on a component that cannot regenerate is unreachable by every content_data route there is.**
- **prove it rather than infer it, in about five minutes:** render the real template against the real `content_data` with production's own engine and option — `text/template`, `Option("missingkey=zero")` — in a throwaway program. Measured here: **4,665 bytes out, 188 in the body region, ZERO non-whitespace visible characters, `err=<nil>`.** ⚠ **Use a payload that CAN fill the template as the control** (a generic instance rendered 11,035 bytes with 6,568 of prose) — same component, same template, opposite results, which is what makes it a measurement rather than a demonstration.
- **`missingkey=zero` is why there is no error to catch this.** A missing key renders as the zero value, so the blanking render **succeeds**: no error, no exception, nothing in the status. The only signal is the byte count, and on this component a 4.4 KB `<style>` block dominates it — total bytes fall only ~12% while the prose falls 100%.
- **what STOPS it, so you do not over-alarm:** on the `apply_section_edit` path, `enforceSingleSlotFloors` (`section_editor_actions.go:451` → `single_slot_floors.go:161`) measures **VISIBLE** text with style/script content excluded, engaging above 200 existing chars — thousands existing against zero incoming is refused, *"nothing was written and the existing component still stands."* So the realistic outcome is a **refusal**, not destruction. Say so: the alarming version of this entry would be wrong.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/277` §5 (the worked case and the render measurement) · `bugs_open/333` · `bugs_closed/301` / `295` (the ownership refusal that gets the blame) · this file's *"A `section_edit` on a per-site TOOL FORK whose template carries `{{.field}}` copy…"* — the SAME failure on a different component class, and I checked that entry against the tool forks while the risk was in the section component I was actually pointing at · `bugs_open/178` / `253` (the floors that hold) · MEMORY [[repro-regenerated-from-source-is-destroyed-by-the-render]] (the same property, met as a reproduction problem) · MEMORY [[a-client-side-absence-is-not-an-absence]]
