## ~~`missingkey=zero` does NOT protect a component template — an absent key renders the literal `<no value>` onto the live page~~ **RETRACTED THE SAME DAY — THE PLATFORM ALREADY STRIPS IT**

> **⚠ RETRACTED 2026-08-24, hours after filing, by the lane that filed it. The central claim was
> FALSE and this entry is kept — not deleted — because the next person who sees `<no value>` in a
> template render will come looking for exactly this and must find the correction rather than
> silence.**
>
> **What I claimed:** an unguarded `{{.field}}` in a component template publishes the literal
> `<no value>` onto a live page whenever the writer omits that key, with nothing to report it.
>
> **What is actually true:** `RenderTemplate` (`platform/orchestration/actions/component_library.go`
> :1258) does `strings.ReplaceAll(result, "<no value>", "")` on every render, and that is the
> function `RenderComponentAction` calls (`v3_site_actions.go:2459`) — i.e. the live path. It is
> stripped before anything is persisted. **The estate handles this, and at a better layer than a
> per-template guard:** immediately above the strip, `missingBareFields` reports the fields that
> rendered empty **at Error level with their names**, deliberately greppable, because a blanked
> `href=`/`src=` is a dead control shipped to a live page (`bugs_open/018`: 30 shipped silently on
> idea.uk under a count-only Warn that named nothing). Separately `missingRequiredLLMFields`
> gates an absent REQUIRED field (`bugs_open/342`), because a missing required field means the
> content did not arrive at all rather than arriving broken.
>
> **How I got it wrong, and it is the instructive part.** I measured correctly — 0 live
> `page_components` contain `<no value>`, control 1,907 contain `<section` — and then explained the
> zero with the wrong mechanism: I read it as *"writers reliably fill every key"* when it is
> *"the platform strips it."* **The number was right and the story was wrong**, which is the same
> error this lane logged twice already today. The check I skipped costs one command:
> `grep -rn '<no value>' --include=*.go platform internal` — which returns the strip, the
> reporting, and two tests that assert the behaviour
> (`render_seam_no_fallback_test.go:376,387`). **Before filing a FLEET-WIDE landmine, grep for
> whether the platform already handles the thing.** A landmine that warns about a solved problem
> is worse than no entry: it is the phantom-miss failure — a warning people learn to ignore.
>
> **What survives, much smaller and not landmine-grade:** `{{if}}`-guarding an interpolation is
> still marginally better hygiene than relying on a downstream string replace — it renders a
> deliberate empty element rather than a stripped artefact, and it keeps the intent visible in the
> template. Migrations 604/605/606 guard for that reason and their headers now say so. That is a
> style preference, **not** a defect being prevented.
>
> **Also corrected: the "49 exposed templates" figure.** Those 49 active section templates do use
> `{{range}}`, but they are not *exposed* to anything — they are rendering through the same strip.
> The number was real and the word "exposed" was not.
>
> — `bugs_open/381` lane, 2026-08-24. Full incident in `WRONG_CALLS.md`.


### A work item's ROUTE lives in one of THREE places depending on its producer — a single-shape read calls correctly-routed rows `(UNROUTED)`, and adding `status='needs_human_review'` makes the count unable to come out non-zero
- **footprint:** `site_work_items` (`result->>'route'`, `result->'response'->'triage'->>'route'`, `spec->>'route'`), `item_type='required_fields_missing'`, `bugs_closed/277` §10.5, the `required-fields-missing-handler` router
- **fires when:** you audit whether a router or triage classified everything it was given — verifying a "zero unrouted" claim, writing any census keyed on a work item's route, or judging whether a handler has coverage. No symptom is needed and none appears.
- **the tell:** none, and it misleads in **both** directions from the same column. Measured 2026-08-24 on 64 rows of one item_type: `result->>'route'` holds the route for **32** rows (the router's own writes on `discovery` findings); **29** more carry it at `result->'response'->'triage'->>'route'` (the awaited triage response nests it a level down); **2** carry it at `spec->>'route'`, **pre-declared by the producer** (`section_editor`) before any router saw them. Read only the top-level key and 29 correctly-routed rows report `(UNROUTED)` — a false alarm on a working router.
- **the deeper half, which is the one that costs you:** the obvious fix — filter to `status='needs_human_review'` so you are "looking at the parked ones" — produces a **structurally green** answer. **The router is what parks a row at `needs_human_review`**, so that filter selects exactly the rows it already handled. As measured, every row missing a top-level route is `complete` or `failed` and every `needs_human_review` row has one, so `(UNROUTED)` **cannot** be non-zero. `bugs_closed/277`'s own close shipped this query as its verification, and it was incapable of reporting the fault it existed to detect.
- **the check — read all three shapes, drop the status filter, and keep a positive control:**
  ```sql
  SELECT COALESCE(result->>'route',
                  result->'response'->'triage'->>'route',
                  spec->>'route', '(GENUINELY UNROUTED)') AS route, source, status, count(*)
  FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='<your item_type>'
  GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 4 DESC;
  ```
  Group by `source` as well as route: **a second producer is how the third shape arrives**, and the producer that pre-declares its own route is invisible in any query grouped on route alone. Before believing a zero, name the rows that would have shown up had it been non-zero — on `required_fields_missing` those are the two `section_editor`/`failed` rows, which no status filter of the parked set can ever reach.
- **relations:** owner ruling 2026-08-02 §1 (a shared `item_type` must name its producer set — this is the cost of not doing so: each producer invented its own route slot) · the "a post-fix ZERO needs a DEMAND control" family in MEMORY · `bugs_closed/277` §10.5, where the amended query lives · `site_work_items` is a rolling window, so union the archive if you are counting history
- **source:** 2026-08-24, a session asked to resume `bugs_closed/277`. Found by re-running the close's own verify block two days after the close: it printed a reassuring zero while 29 rows sat in the `(UNROUTED)` bucket of the same output — **the false alarm is what exposed the false clean.** The bug's central claim ("zero unrouted") turned out to be TRUE; it was the recipe that could not show it.
- **verifier:** `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` ×2 (2026-08-24 20:15Z) — **a scope limit, not a refutation.** The landmine-verifier indexes **Go symbols only**: it confirmed `site_work_items` and `required-fields-missing-handler` in current code, and reported the three JSONB route paths, the `required_fields_missing` literal and the `bugs_closed/277` path as outside its corpus — *"could not be verified or refuted"*. Those are the DB-measured half, and the census that establishes them (64 rows, 3 shapes, 2 producers) is in the bullets above and re-runnable from the SQL block. **Answered by the author on the day; do not read the verdict as an open objection.**
- **added:** 2026-08-24, resuming `bugs_closed/277`. ⚠ **Appended TWICE**: the first append (20:13Z) was lost when a concurrent session wrote the whole file back from a copy that predated it — the file went 17,010 → 17,028 (mine) → 17,030 (theirs, mine absent). Nothing of theirs was lost; the `doc_notes` rows from the first sync survived because delivery had already run.


### Registering a verifier protects a type only on the paths that ASK — the coverage guard goes green either way, and two of the three writers of `complete` never asked
- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/verifiers.go` `RegisterVerifier` / `RegisterVerifierWithPolicy` / `GetVerifier`, `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/verifier_coverage_test.go`, `platform/orchestration/actions/v3_site_actions.go` `UpdateWorkItemStatusAction`, action `update_work_item_status`, register `CQ-023`, `WII-030`
- **fires when:** you write a verifier off `verifier_coverage_test.go`'s **`catMechanical` backlog** — the list that says of itself *"These SHOULD get verifiers — this is the actionable backlog, not an excuse list."* You need no symptom: you register it, the coverage test goes green, and you are done. Also fires on any reasoning of the shape "this item_type is verified, so its completions were checked".
- **the tell:** none, in either direction. `verifier_coverage_test.go` asserts that every item type is verified **or** an acknowledged gap. It says nothing about **who stamps the row**, and there are **three** writers of `complete` on `site_work_items` that do not agree:
  1. `CompleteWorkItemAction` — consults the verifier (`complete_work_item_verification.go`).
  2. `UpdateWorkItemStatusAction` — consulted **nothing** until 2026-08-24 (`GetVerifier` had exactly ONE non-test caller in the entire tree), and now consults it only when that **step's** config sets `verify_before_complete: true`.
  3. the `claimed-item-timeout` sweep — consults **neither** gate; it writes the row directly, held off a type only by `livespec.ClaimedItemTimeoutExclusions` (`bugs_closed/317`).
- **the half that costs you most: the register told you the OPPOSITE, by name.** `CQ-023` warned whoever registered a `required_fields_missing` verifier that it *"would fail-closed the `converted` arm's completion"*. Measured 2026-08-24: all three of that router's `complete` arms (`close_converted`, `close_resolved`, `close_stale`) are `update_work_item_status` steps, so it would **not** fail-close — it would do **nothing at all, silently**. You are braced for one wrong outcome and handed a different one. (Corrected in place at `CQ-023`; the warning is now true **per arm**, once that arm is armed.)
- **the check — ask WHO COMPLETES the type before you write its verifier, and read the recursive shape:**
  ```sql
  -- which live agents complete via the writer that may not consult a verifier?
  WITH live AS (SELECT type, default_config FROM agent_definitions
                WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL)
  SELECT l.type,
         COALESCE(st->'config'->>'status','(default=complete)') AS sets_status,
         (st->'config'->>'verify_before_complete') AS armed
  FROM live l, LATERAL jsonb_path_query(l.default_config,
         'strict $.**{0 to last} ? (@.action == "update_work_item_status")') st
  ORDER BY 1,2;
  ```
  Then join your item_type to its `handler_agent` (`SELECT DISTINCT handler_agent FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='<yours>'`). If the handler appears above with a `complete` arm and `armed` NULL, **your verifier will never run** — arm the step, or move that completion to `complete_work_item`.
  **Three ways this query goes wrong if you shorten it, all measured 2026-08-24:**
  · `jsonb_each(default_config->'workflow'->'steps')` **misses nested loop-step configs** — it finds only 2 of the 4 live `complete_work_item` callers. Use the recursive form.
  · `WHERE config->>'status' = 'complete'` **cannot see a step that omits `status`**, and the action **defaults it to `complete`**. `COALESCE` it, or a seventh arm is invisible.
  · counting registrations with `grep -c 'RegisterVerifier('` **under-reports**: it does not match `RegisterVerifierWithPolicy(`, which is how `hardcoded_section_colors` and `needs_brand_head_assets` are registered. Use `'RegisterVerifier\(WithPolicy\)\?('`, and count **types**, not grep lines (18 lines, 13 types).
- **and once you HAVE registered one, the row will tell you:** an unarmed completion of a type that has a verifier now writes `result._verification.status = 'verifier_not_consulted'` with the remedy. `SELECT count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE result->'_verification'->>'status' = 'verifier_not_consulted'` — ⚠ a **zero** there while a verifier exists means the record is not firing, not that nothing was skipped, so control it against a completion you know took that path.
- **relations:** `WII-030` (the arming key and its measured consumer set) · `CQ-023` (the corrected warning, and why arming is per arm) · `bugs_closed/317` + `claim_timeout_exclusion_lockstep_test.go` (the third writer, and the declaration+lockstep shape this class was already solved with once) · `bugs_open/375` (the bug, with the census and its positive control) · `bugs_open/213` (`VerifierPolicy.Grades` — the *other* way a registered verifier grades the wrong thing) · `bugs_open/017` / `bugs_open/021` §INSTANCE 2 (the class)
- **verifier:** `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` (2026-08-24 20:52Z) — **a SCOPE LIMIT, not a refutation; answered by the author, do not read it as an open objection.** It confirmed the core footprint (`verifiers.go` with `RegisterVerifier`/`RegisterVerifierWithPolicy`/`GetVerifier`, `v3_site_actions.go` with `UpdateWorkItemStatusAction`, the action name) and reported three things out of scope: `verifier_coverage_test.go` returned **0 rows**, and `CQ-023`/`WII-030` are register prose, which a `.go`-only index cannot hold. ⚠ **The 0 rows are the index's own staleness, not a missing file** — its answers describe indexed commit `e347c5ad` of **2026-08-23 12:21Z**, which PREDATES both that file's header edit and this entry, and the index has not been recut since. So a verifier verdict on any entry written after 08-23 can only speak for symbols that already existed. The claims it could not reach — the arming key's behaviour and the three completion writers — are proven instead by the mutation-tested unit suite (`update_work_item_status_verification_test.go`, M1–M7) and by the live census in this entry's own SQL block.
- **status 2026-08-25:** the gate is LIVE at the artefact on chassis `v1.0.1337` (literal probed on both pods with present- and absent-controls). ⚠ **This changes nothing about the trap** — 0 steps arm the key and none of the 7 reachable types has a verifier, so the entry is exactly as load-bearing as it was on the day it was written. It stops being latent the moment somebody works that backlog. **That sentence is a state claim with a shelf life, so here is what re-establishes it (last true 2026-08-25 16:31Z):** `grep -rEho 'RegisterVerifier(WithPolicy)?\("[a-z_]+"' platform/ internal/ --include=*.go | grep -v _test | sed -E 's/.*"(.*)"/\1/' | sort -u` — if any of `needs_imagery`, `required_fields_missing`, `needs_hero_image`, `unfulfilled_hero_variant`, `needs_logo`, `image_url_404`, `image_source_unsatisfiable` appears, **the trap is no longer latent and this entry is now about a live bypass.**
- **added:** 2026-08-24, `bugfix_375_completion_verifier_gap` lane, on taking `bugs_open/375`. Found by reading `CQ-023` before choosing a fix candidate and noticing its warning could not be true given the census the handoff had just run — the entry exists because the *documentation* was the trap, not only the code.
- **⚠ AND WHEN YOU RUN THAT CENSUS, UNION THE ARCHIVE.** `site_work_items` is a ROLLING WINDOW — `work-item-archiver` moves terminal rows to `site_work_items_archive` (**25,281** rows as of 2026-08-24), which is where COMPLETED rows go, i.e. exactly the ones a completion census is about. Measured: over the live table alone this bug's own blast radius read **5 item types / 134 completions**; over the union it is **7 / 578**, and the two extra types (`unfulfilled_hero_variant`, `image_url_404`) had completed ENTIRELY into the archive. The conclusion held — all seven are unverified — but only by luck. Disconfirming question before writing any "all-history"/"ever"/"lifetime" figure on this table: *would a row that already completed and got archived appear in my result?* Named `site_work_items` only ⇒ no, and the figure means "recently" however it is worded.

### Probing `/proc/1/exe` for a Go STRUCT FIELD name reports "absent" while the feature is live — probe a string LITERAL the change introduces

- **footprint:** `kubectl exec … grep -aq "<symbol>" /proc/1/exe`, `TerminatedOnRepeat`, `terminated_on_repeat`, every "did my fix ship?" probe in `CLAUDE.md` § Building & deploying
- **fires when:** you verify a deploy the sanctioned way — grep the running binary for a symbol your change introduced, with a must-be-absent control — and the symbol you pick is a **struct field**, a local variable, or a type's method set member. Field names are not emitted into the binary (no reflection, no struct tag naming it → nothing to find); **function** names are (pclntab), and string **literals** are.
- **the trap:** the control passes (absent), your target reads **absent**, and the reading is "NOT in this build" — a confident, controlled, wrong answer, on a fleet where "did it ship?" decides whether you re-roll. [MEASURED 2026-08-24, both `v1.0.1334` replicas] `TerminatedOnRepeat` (a `failureLadderOutcome` field) → absent; `stop_on_repeat_failure` (a string literal in the same commit) → PRESENT; control absent. Same binary, same feature, opposite verdicts.
- **the check:** choose the probe from what the compiler must keep — a string literal the change added (`grep -n '"' <your diff>` and pick one), or an exported/unexported **function** name. Never a field, a constant that inlines, or a variable. And keep the two controls: one that must be present (a literal you know shipped earlier) and one that must be absent.
- **relations:** CLAUDE.md § "Ask the service what it is running" · MEMORY [[prove-a-deploy-at-the-artefact-index]] (probe the CAPABILITY, not the commit — this is the sub-case where the capability's NAME is the wrong probe) · WII-029's verify-later
- **source:** 2026-08-24, `bugs_open/345` close-condition probe; caught because the same breath probed a literal from the same commit and it disagreed.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/345` lane

### Fixing a detector does NOT dispose of the findings it already filed — the revalidator reports "the standard moved, not the copy" and keeps them open, correctly
- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/revalidate_unverified_claims.go` (`claimStillOnPage`, `unverifiedClaimsVerdict`, `armGateClaimsStillPresent`, `armScanStillTrips`), `site_work_items` `item_type='claims_unverified'` / `status='needs_human_review'`, `review-queue-revalidate-daily`, any change to `editorialPageTypes`, `businessClaimContextRe`, `isExcludedNumber` or a banned-claim pattern
- **fires when:** you fix a false positive in the claims layer and expect the queue to drain — the natural next thought after "my fix removes 20 findings" is "so the 20 items filed from them will close on the next revalidation". **They will not**, and the reasoning that gets you there is sound, which is what makes this worth an entry.
- **the tell:** none until you read the verdict ladder. The revalidator DOES re-scan (`armScanStillTrips`) and your fixed scan now returns nothing — so far so good — but the ladder then reaches the **claim-granular gate**, which compares the finding's **cited token** against the slot's CURRENT text. Your fix changed the standard, not the copy, so every token is still exactly where it was, and the verdict is `armGateClaimsStillPresent`: *"page X no longer trips the check, but N of the M texts this finding cited are STILL in the component they were cited from — so the standard moved, not the copy; a claim that stopped being flagged while its words are untouched has not been addressed."* The item stays `needs_human_review` for ever.
- **the check:** before predicting a queue will drain, read the verdict ladder rather than the scan. Ask **"does closure key on the SCAN's verdict, or on the TEXT being gone?"** Here it is the text. Then enumerate the items you expect to close and record their ids FIRST — closing archives the row out of `site_work_items`, so a later census cannot see what it succeeded at. Measured 2026-08-25 (`bugs_open/364`): two items open since 2026-08-09 (`4405fb38` adoption-tracker/8 findings, `2f8f67dd` protocol-tracker/3) are pure false positives of the fixed defect and will never self-close.
- **⚠ DO NOT "FIX" THIS.** It is a deliberate integrity control, added by council round 5 (`compliance`, HIGH, 2026-08-11) on the platform's highest-stakes and deliberately HITL-terminal item type: it is what stops a CSS tweak, a typo fix — **or a detector change** — silently disposing of a real fabrication. The seat's own first suggestion (compare the cited SNIPPET) was measured and REJECTED because it found the claim in only 18 of 41 still-holding cases and would have failed OPEN on half of them; the TOKEN is what discriminates. Disposing of a stale false positive is a **human ruling**, not an engineering one.
- **and the sibling trap:** the same run will correctly keep genuinely-unsupported findings open on the same page type. Do not read "some items stayed open" as the fix having failed — separate them by whether the page is the one your fix targeted, and read the recorded `arm`, which is the only field that tells the two refusals apart.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/364` lane, on the roll that shipped its interim (v1.0.1337). I had drafted the prediction that these items would auto-close before reading the ladder.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/364` lane

### `pages.nav_order` also ranks CTA destinations — so hiding a page from the nav makes it no less prominent, and a fossil `nav_order` silently owns the site's main button
- **footprint:** `pages.nav_order`, `pages.in_header`, `platform/orchestration/actions/resolve_internal_links_action.go` (`chooseCTATargets`, `loadInteractivePages`, `setCTAField`, `stampCTADestinationGuidance`), `render_site_components_action.go:182-190`, `bugs_open/391`
- **fires when:** you set, tidy or migrate `nav_order`; you remove a page from the navigation; you add a tool/game page; or you are asked why a site links something odd from its hero or call-to-action. No symptom is needed — the wrong outcome is a valid, existing, 200-returning page, and the button's copy is generated to name whatever it was handed, so it reads as a deliberate recommendation.
- **the tell:** none at the page. `chooseCTATargets` takes **every** `page_type IN ('tool','game')` page on the site, drops only excluded areas (contact/legal/about) and self-links, sorts by **`COALESCE(nav_order,100)` then `name`**, and returns `ordered[0]` as the primary CTA and `ordered[1]` as the secondary. **There is no topic, tag, semantic or LLM input in the selection at all.** So the most prominent link on every page of a site is decided by a column whose visible job is menu order.
- **the trap inside it — `in_header` is NOT read by the chooser.** Its linkability predicate (`datahelpers.PageMayBeLinkedPredicateFor`, `links.go:328`) is purely deployment-state. Measured 2026-08-25: a session had already hidden `password-entropy` from one site's nav with the comment *"a password tool doesn't belong in the primary nav"* (`docs/leopardessconsulting/scripts/L5_nav_and_ctas.sql:29`) and **it changed nothing** — the page kept `nav_order = 1` and went on winning the primary CTA on every page. **Removing a page from the nav does not remove it from CTA candidacy, and leaves intact the very number that makes it first choice.**
- **the check — simulate the ranking before and after you touch either column:**
  ```sql
  SELECT s.domain, p.name, COALESCE(p.nav_order,100) AS nav_order,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY s.id ORDER BY COALESCE(p.nav_order,100), p.name) AS rank
  FROM pages p JOIN sites s ON s.id=p.site_id
  WHERE p.page_type IN ('tool','game') AND p.status IN ('active','deployed')
  ORDER BY s.domain, rank;
  ```
  Mirror the code exactly — `COALESCE(...,100)`, tiebreak on **`name`** not `url` — or the simulation proves nothing. `rank` 1 and 2 are the buttons your change is about to move. ⚠ **A low `nav_order` on a tool page is usually a FOSSIL, not a decision**: the three sites bitten here carry `nav_order = 1` set at page creation in March, beating every relevant tool at 6–204.
- **and the base-rate check that stops the obvious wrong conclusion:** before reading `in_header=false` as *"a human judged this page inappropriate"*, count it — **143 of 228 tool/game pages fleet-wide are `in_header=false` (62.7%)**, the majority state. It is not evidence of intent. This refuted a 13-site claim of mine that was one edit from being filed; the leopardess case counts only because its SQL comment says so in words.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/391` (the bug — **renumbered from 389 on 2026-08-25**; 389 is a different CTA bug from the `bugfix_308` lane) · `bugs_closed/299` (`home_page_cta_names_the_brief_starter_tool` slug) and LNK-034 — the existing CTA detectors check **validity** (does it exist, is it a page, does the copy name it) and **none checks relevance**, which is why this class passes every gate · `bugs_closed/191` (header CTA validated by a looser predicate than the nav beside it — the same nav-vs-CTA divergence one layer up) · `bugs_open/248`/`bugs_closed/268` (what constrains a repair run) · `datahelpers/cta_provenance.go` LNK-035, the stamp that tells you whether a given CTA was minted or authored
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugfix_389_cta_relevance` lane, from an owner report. Confirmed at code, at the simulated ranking against live data, and at the served bytes on three domains.
- ⚠ **THE HALF THAT MAKES IT PERMANENT, added 2026-08-25 after adversarial review — a `nav_order` fix does NOT reach a button whose COPY already names the destination.** `setCTAField` (`:418-434`) tries **`BestLabelMatchForPage` on the existing label FIRST** and the positional pick LAST; and `stampCTADestinationGuidance` (`:362`) appends *"Destination (fixed): <title>"* to the **label** field's `llm_field_specs`, which pipes to the writer. So the sequence is: positional pick → `*_target_title` → guidance → **the writer produces a button that NAMES the wrongly-picked page** → the next resolve label-matches that copy back to the same page. **A ranking accident becomes a content fact, and the locked set grows with every mint.** Measured 2026-08-25 on one population: 17/17 resolver-minted fields carry a `*_target_title` naming the tool, 16/17 have copy naming it, and **20 of 80 fields are label-locked — including every button the owner actually complained about.** The tell that the positional path (not label-match) produced a row is copy that could not have matched it: *"Book a Technical Discovery Call"* → `/tools/password-entropy.html`, minted 2026-08-24.
- **so, before you claim any ranking fix reaches a population, run the lock query** — `count(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(content_data->>replace(key,'_url','_text'), content_data->>replace(key,'_url','_label'), content_data->>replace(key,'_url','')) ILIKE '%<destination word>%')` over the `%\_url` fields. Locked rows need the COPY rewritten; only the rest are reachable by ordering. ⚠ **And do not fix this at the loaders**: `render_site_components_action.go:182-190` (the site **header** CTA fallback) calls `loadContentHubs`/`loadInteractivePages` directly, takes `ordered[0]`, and its output is **never persisted** (`site_components` holds 0 `cta_url` keys), so a loader change moves every site's header button invisibly. **Change the ranking.** A flag on the ranking alone still does not bind `LoadCTALabelUniverse` — an opt-out that ignores the label match has a hole exactly the shape of the bug.
- **verifier:** `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` (2026-08-25 09:56Z) — **a scope limit, and it CORROBORATES the structure.** It confirmed `chooseCTATargets` and `loadInteractivePages` both exist in `resolve_internal_links_action.go`, and independently noted that `in_header` appears in **`classifyPagesForNav`** — i.e. on the NAV path, which is exactly this entry's point. What it could not check is the behaviour (the sort keys, the absence of `in_header` in the chooser), because its index holds Go **symbols** and not function bodies, and `pages.nav_order` / the bug file path are outside a .go-only corpus. Those halves were read by hand and are quoted verbatim above. ⚠ Its line numbers (L640-671, L878-887) differ from the ones cited here because it indexes commit `e347c5ad` (2026-08-23, the last pushed tip); **the citations in this entry are against the present tree.** Answered by the author on the day; not an open objection.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugfix_389_cta_relevance` lane

### `site_work_items.handler_agent` has TWO causes — a producer minting it and a human re-pointing it — and the column cannot tell you which, so it CANNOT prove a routing fix

- **footprint:** `site_work_items.handler_agent`, `site_work_items.created_by`, `spec->>'page_type'`, `updated_at`, `builderForPageType`, `reconcile_site_plan`, `WriteBuildItemsAction`, `needs_page:`, any closure/verification query of the shape "the producer minted this row at the right handler", `HandleRetryWorkItem`, the resolve endpoint, `bugs_open/206`, `bugs_open/220`
- **fires when:** you ship a change to *which handler a producer routes work to*, then verify it by querying for rows carrying the new handler. This is the obvious closure test and it is what two lanes independently wrote.
- **the trap:** `handler_agent` is a **mutable column**, and re-pointing a parked row at a handler that works is this estate's *documented operator escape hatch* — recipe in `reconcile_site_plan_action.go`'s own gap-arm comment, and used at least twice for real. So `created_by='<the producer>' AND handler_agent='<the new handler>'` matches **both** a row your fix minted and a row a human repaired months after a different producer minted it wrong. The two are indistinguishable in that column, and the hand-repaired one is *more* likely to exist, because a page somebody cared enough to fix is a page somebody was looking at.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** the row you find is a *correct* row — right handler, right producer, page probably building. Nothing about it looks repaired. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25, live UNION `site_work_items_archive`, all history]` on the `bugs_open/206` closure test: **exactly three rows fleet-wide matched the PASS predicate and ALL THREE were hand re-routes** — `created_at` 2026-07-17, months before the fix; `updated_at` 08-08 and 08-24, the two dates this estate re-routed pages by hand. Run without a domain filter, that query would have declared a fix **proven by rows the very hardcode it replaced had minted.** The fix is real; the instrument was not.
- **the check, before you believe any "the producer routed it correctly" row — TWO gates, and the first alone is not enough:**
  ```sql
  WHERE swi.created_by = '<producer>'
    AND swi.spec ? '<key only the new emit writes>'              -- GATE 1: the mint fingerprint
    AND swi.updated_at < swi.created_at + interval '1 second'    -- GATE 2: untouched since the mint
    AND swi.created_at > '<the roll>'
  ```
  **⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-25, hours after this entry was added, by an adversarial review of it.** As first written this check was gate 1 only, and called airtight on the argument *"a re-route only touches `handler_agent` and cannot add a spec key"*. That is true and **insufficient**, twice over — and the author had the second gate in hand (the measurement that produced this entry computes exactly `updated_at > created_at + interval '1 second'`) and left it out.
  - **the fingerprint dates the ROW, not the mutable VALUE.** The column stays mutable after a stamped mint, so if the fixed producer *mis*-routes — the failure the test exists to catch — and someone then repairs it, the row is stamped AND correct and reads PASS. Same false pass, one generation on.
  - **an operator recipe can forge gate 1 without ever touching a spec key**, if some *other* row the emit writes already carries the key. Exactly what happened here: reconcile's `capability_gap` spec also contains `page_type`, and the documented repair is *"promote this row in place — set `item_type`, `status` and `handler_agent`"*. A promoted gap row satisfies every PASS condition by hand. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` prospective, not live (0 stamped gap rows exist) — it arms itself the moment the fix files its first gap, i.e. when the test starts being used. **So enumerate every row shape the new emit stamps, not just the one you are asserting on.**
  - **gate 2 works because the `updated_at` trigger is `BEFORE UPDATE … FOR EACH ROW`** (verify it in `pg_trigger` for your table): *any* write bumps it, so `updated_at ≈ created_at` means nothing has touched the row since the emit. **Its cost is that it expires** — a legitimate claim or completion bumps it too, so read the mint promptly, while the row is still at its born status. If `updated_at` has moved, that row cannot serve as proof; find a fresher one rather than relaxing the gate.
  - Still confirm the fingerprint's population is **empty before your first run** (`[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` 508 reconcile-minted rows, all history, stamp FALSE on every one). That makes the first hit necessarily the fix — it does not make the hit *correctly routed*, which is what gate 2 is for.
  - **the durable fix is a code change, not a better query:** stamp the decision itself into the immutable payload (`spec->>'handler'`) and assert it *equals* the mutable column. Then the column carries its own provenance and no hand action can forge agreement.
- **generalises:** whenever a fix changes what a producer WRITES into a mutable column, that column stops being evidence about the producer the moment anything else can write it too — and an operator recipe, a retry endpoint and an admin resolve button all can. Ask *"what else could have put this value here?"* before *"is this value right?"*. The same shape governs `status`, `priority` and `spec` steering keys. Note the asymmetry that catches people: the mutable column is still fine for detecting **FAILURE** (a wrongly-routed row is exactly the one nobody repaired), which is why a check can look validated against a known-bad population and still be incapable of confirming success.
- **relations:** BLD-027 · `bugs_open/206` (§2 of the 2026-08-25 section carries the measurement and the corrected query) · MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] and [[your-action-moves-you-to-the-back-of-the-selector.md]] (same family: a column written by more than one actor) · [[mutate-the-code-to-prove-the-guard]] (the general remedy — make the check produce the disconfirming answer before trusting it)
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugfix_206_directory_build_handler` lane, found while preparing to RUN the closure test the previous session had already corrected once
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugfix_206_directory_build_handler` lane

## A `citation` fact with no `quote` FAILS ITS RE-VERIFICATION EVERY DAY, FOR EVER, AND NOTHING WILL EVER TELL YOU — the sweep reports `error`, the error means "unknown", and unknown files nothing

- **footprint:** `site_specs.aspect='evidence_base'` · `source.citation.quote` · `staleness_days` · `platform/orchestration/actions/evidence_citations.go` (`refreshCitationFact`, `citationDateStale`) · `refresh_evidence_base_action.go` · CLM-007 · CLM-008 · `bugs_open/288`
- **fires when:** you SEED or hand-author an evidence register — the commonest new-site task there is. You write a citation with `url`, `title`, `publisher`, `accessed`/`captured` and no verbatim `quote`, because every field you wrote is true and the object looks complete. No symptom follows. The daily sweep runs, reports the fact as *checked*, and the register reads healthy for ever.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly like the right one:** `refreshCitationFact` re-proves a fact by re-fetching its URL and matching the **stored verbatim quote**. With no `quote` it cannot run at all and returns `outcome: "error"`, detail `citation missing required field(s): quote`. That error is then handled **correctly and deliberately** by CLM-008 — *unknown is not loss* — so it files **nothing**: no work item, no doc_note, no raise. The one thing that could eventually escalate it is age, and `citationDateStale` returns false when `staleness_days <= 0` (`evidence_citations.go:113-115`, *"No staleness_days → never stale by age"*), which is the default. **So the two safety rules compose into permanent silence: the check cannot run, and the thing that would notice it never ran is switched off by default.** Neither rule is wrong on its own.
- **the scale, measured 2026-08-25:** **83 of 184 current citation facts fleet-wide (45%) carry no `quote`** — and **all 83 also have `staleness_days` unset**, so not one of them can ever escalate. Today concentrated on a single site (`agritec.uk`, 83 of its 104), i.e. **one lane's authoring habit rather than a platform defect** — which is exactly why it belongs here: the next lane to seed a register will do the same thing and get the same silence.
- **the check — read the OUTCOMES of a real sweep, never the register's shape:**
  ```sql
  -- 1. who cannot be re-proved at all, and would anything ever escalate them?
  SELECT si.domain,
         count(*) AS citation_facts,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT (fa->'source'->'citation' ? 'quote')) AS no_quote_UNPROVABLE,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE COALESCE(NULLIF(fa->>'staleness_days','')::numeric,0) <= 0) AS never_escalates
  FROM site_specs s JOIN sites si ON si.id = s.site_id,
       jsonb_array_elements(s.data->'facts') fa
  WHERE s.aspect='evidence_base' AND s.is_current AND fa->'source' ? 'citation'
  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC;

  -- 2. the confirming half: what did the LAST REAL sweep actually say?
  SELECT (r->>'domain') AS domain, f->>'outcome' AS outcome, left(f->>'detail',60) AS detail, count(*)
  FROM orchestration_states o,
       jsonb_array_elements(o.collected_data->'refresh_result'->'results') r,
       jsonb_array_elements(CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(r->'facts')='array' THEN r->'facts' ELSE '[]'::jsonb END) f
  WHERE o.created_at > now() - interval '2 days' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 4 DESC;
  ```
  **Query 2 is the one that bites**, and query 1 alone will mislead you: a register can look complete field-by-field and still be 100% inert. ⚠ And run query 2 against a **non-dry** pass — a dry run writes nothing and is not evidence about production.
- **the fix, and it is the author's not the platform's:** store the verbatim sentence from the source that carries the figure, in `quote`; and set `staleness_days` so a citation that *cannot* be re-proved eventually becomes a human's problem instead of a permanent quiet error. A fact with a `quote` and no `staleness_days` is merely un-aged; a fact with **neither** is unverifiable and unescalatable, which is the state to hunt for.
- **relations:** CLM-008 (unknown-is-not-loss — correct, and half of why this is silent) · CLM-007 (the daily sweep) · `bugs_open/288` §5c (found while reviewing another lane's fence; the same session's `artifact_check`-at-the-top-level entry is the same class one key over — a declaration that is live, well-formed and read by nothing) · RFC_025 (`artifact_check`, the *other* verification mechanism, which is unaffected by a missing quote and is the only live check on such a fact)
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `register_guards_code_phase_b` lane (`bugs_open/288`), from reviewing the `agritec_uk` lane's fence. Confirmed at the code, at the live register shape, and at the outcomes of the real 09:06Z sweep. The owning lane was told the same day.
- **⚠ THE FIX HAS ITS OWN TRAP, AND IT IS SHARPER THAN THE ORIGINAL: A COMPOSED QUOTE IS A HYPOTHESIS ABOUT THE EXTRACTOR'S WHITESPACE, NOT ABOUT THE SOURCE.** Same day, same site: the owning lane added all 83 missing quotes and set staleness. The register's SHAPE then read **104 citation facts, 0 without quote, 0 without staleness** — perfect. **The sweep said 102 fresh and 2 `citation_lost`.** This is the two-query rule earning its place on the very fix for the thing that motivated it, so run query 2 after the repair as well as before it.
  The two survivors were `UPL5`/`UPL6`, whose stored quote is `… on moorland (minimum 70% GLU ) £18 per hectare` — a space before the closing paren, taken from how the page *renders* rather than from what the extractor *emits*. The matcher (`NormalizeForQuoteMatch`, `datahelpers/citations.go:116`) unescapes entities, normalises punctuation and thousands separators, lowercases, and collapses whitespace **RUNS** to one space (`quoteWSRe`) — **it does not delete a single space.** So `glu )` will never match text that extracts as `glu)`, and no amount of re-fetching helps.
  **The remedy is structural, not clerical: build the quote FROM the extractor's output** (`VisibleTextFromHTML` = `strings.Join(ExtractAssertionText(html), " ")`), never from the page source, the rendered page, or a reconstruction of a table row. And because `QuoteFoundInText` is a **`Contains`**, prefer the **shortest distinctive fragment** that carries the claim and spans no ambiguous boundary — `UPL5 Supplement: Keep cattle and ponies on moorland` re-proves reliably where the full row with its parenthetical does not. A longer quote is not stronger evidence; it is more surface on which to disagree with the extractor.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `register_guards_code_phase_b`; extended the same day with the composed-quote trap after the owning lane's repair left 2 of 83 still failing

## Go's HTTP client FOLLOWS REDIRECTS by default, so any probe that reasons about status codes is reading the END of a chain — and a "only 2xx qualifies" rule written beside it is inert

- **footprint:** `http.Client{}` built without `CheckRedirect` · `platform/orchestration/actions/render_sitemap_action.go` (`probeOK`) · `check_endpoint_health_action.go` · any Go action that fetches a URL to decide whether it is live, canonical, deployed or reachable · any `probe_dropped` / `url_count` / health figure derived from one
- **fires when:** you write or trust a URL probe whose decision is a status code. `net/http` follows up to **10** redirects transparently and hands you the FINAL response, so `resp.StatusCode` can never be 3xx unless you asked for that. The probe then reports 200 for a URL that redirects — possibly to a different domain entirely.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly right:** the probe is usually the only validation in the pipeline, and it returns the success value. Nothing logs a redirect, no counter increments, and the derived figure reads perfect. **[MEASURED 2026-08-25]** `webdesign.uk` 302s **every** path to `webdesign.co.uk`; its sitemap sweep reported `url_count: 7, probe_dropped: 0` and committed a `sitemap.xml` advertising seven URLs that redirect away. Re-probed without following: **7 of 7 are 302**; followed: **7 of 7 are 200**. `probe_dropped: 0` — the field that exists to report exactly this — was the most convincing part of the wrong answer.
- **⚠ the doc comment made it worse, not better.** `probeOK` carried *"Only a 2xx qualifies. A redirect is deliberately NOT listed — a sitemap should carry the canonical URL"* from the day it was written. A reader checking whether redirects were handled found the rule, stated clearly and correctly, **beside code that did not implement it** — so the comment converted "unhandled" into "handled" for every reviewer who read it. Related: MEMORY [[a-doc-comment-is-not-an-enforcement-mechanism]].
- **the check — probe both ways and compare; one number alone cannot show you this:**
  ```bash
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'  "$url"   # no-follow: what your probe SHOULD see
  curl -sL -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "$url"   # follow:    what it ACTUALLY sees
  ```
  A disagreement means every status-derived figure downstream is about the wrong URL. In Go, make the rule true:
  ```go
  client := &http.Client{
      CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error { return http.ErrUseLastResponse },
  }
  ```
  Then **measure the blast radius before switching it on** — sites that legitimately 301 to a canonical form will start being dropped. Sampled across 27 domains on 2026-08-25 it was 1, and that one was already excluded; do not assume yours is.
- **source:** portfolio_positioning lane, 2026-08-25, found because `webdesign.uk` was the one swept site still serving no sitemap of ours. Fixed in `54ba65b25`, pinned by `TestProbeDoesNotFollowRedirects` (mutation-proven: the bare client yields *"reported status 200, want 302"*, verbatim the live reading). Council `25157bab-4b6d-40c5-a218-98148b60daf6`
- **added:** 2026-08-25, portfolio_positioning lane

## CANONICALISING your output makes it stop matching the SOURCE it came from — so your own verification query scores your own fix as a regression

- **footprint:** any census that joins generated artefacts back to `pages.url` (sitemap `<loc>`, nav hrefs, link graphs, JSON-LD `@id`, `llms.txt`) · `datahelpers.NormalizePagePath` · any "N of M match" verification written BEFORE a canonicalisation change and re-run after it
- **fires when:** you write a matching check to prove an artefact is genuinely yours, then change the emitter to canonicalise. The stored value and the emitted value now differ **on purpose**, and the check — which predates the change — counts every canonicalised item as a MISS.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly right:** a match test failing looks like the artefact being wrong, which is the thing it was built to detect. **[MEASURED 2026-08-25]** after `/index.html` → `/` shipped, a fleet census scored 26 domains at exactly **n−1** matches, and `apis.uk` — whose only deployed page IS the homepage — scored **0 of 1** and was reported **NOT OURS**. Its sitemap was perfect. Correcting the check (canonicalise the `pages` side the same way the emitter does) moved the fleet figure **25 → 26 of 28** and every per-site score to a clean n/n.
- **the tell, and it is the only one:** the misses are **too uniform**. One unmatched entry on 26 different domains is not 26 independent faults — it is one systematic difference. A real coverage problem is ragged. **If every site is wrong in the same place, suspect the instrument.**
- **the check:** before re-running any match census across a change to the emitter, ask *"does this change alter the very string the join keys on?"* If yes, apply the same transform to both sides. And when a site's whole population is the affected shape (a single-page site, where the only URL is the homepage), the systematic error becomes a **total** one and the site reads as entirely broken.
- **relations:** MEMORY [[declaring-a-key-silences-your-own-detector]] and [[your-action-moves-you-to-the-back-of-the-selector]] — same family: **your own action changes what your own detector measures.** The distinguishing feature here is that the detector was RIGHT before the change and RIGHT after, about two different questions.
- **source:** portfolio_positioning lane, 2026-08-25, verifying the `590` fleet sweep
- **added:** 2026-08-25, portfolio_positioning lane

### Registering a verifier is NOT a one-line change — the `init()` fails five guards, and the load-bearing one is a LIVE MIGRATION without which a sweep completes items straight past the guard you just added
- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/verifiers.go` `RegisterVerifier` / `RegisterVerifierWithPolicy`, `platform/livespec/livespec.go` `ClaimedItemTimeoutExclusions`, `scheduled_tasks` (`claimed-item-timeout`), `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/verifier_coverage_test.go`, `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/page_lifecycle_posture_test.go`, `platform/orchestration/actions/write_audit_findings_verifier_join_test.go`, register `WII-031`/`WII-032`
- **fires when:** you take an item type off `verifier_coverage_test.go`'s `catMechanical` backlog — the list that says of itself *"These SHOULD get verifiers — this is the actionable backlog, not an excuse list"* — and write the obvious one-line `init()`. No symptom is needed; the build tells you, which is the good case. **The bad case is that you satisfy the guards in the wrong ORDER.**
- **the tell:** the one line fails **five** guards. Four are bookkeeping and one is not. **Measured 2026-08-25 by doing it** for `required_fields_missing`:
  1. `TestClaimTimeoutExclusionCoversBothCompletionGates` — **THE LOAD-BEARING ONE.** Add the type to `livespec.ClaimedItemTimeoutExclusions` **AND ship a migration amending the LIVE `scheduled_tasks.pre_query`.** ⚠ **ORDER CORRECTED 2026-08-25: do NOT add the exclusions entry first.** The lockstep fails in BOTH directions — `excluded ⇔ (verifier) OR (noChangeGates) OR (a REFUSING acceptancePredicateGates entry)` — so a type added to the exclusions slice before anything can grade it trips the REVERSE arm ("declared excluded but NO gate can grade it", the `bugs_open/006` §C churn). **Apply the MIGRATION first** (it is about the live object, and its window merely makes `--live-declaration-drift` noisy while the sweep skips the type), **then land the exclusions entry and the `RegisterVerifier` call in ONE commit** — either alone breaks the build. ⚠ **And if a second lane is adding a type to the same clause, two migrations written against the same starting clause will NOT compose**: `livespec.Declarations` pins the live `pre_query` to `ClaimedItemTimeoutExclusionClause()`'s rendering with a FragmentMatch Min:1/Max:1, so whichever applies second must render the MERGED slice or the drift auditor fires on a correct-looking change (raised by `bugs_open/395`, which owes `content_rewrite` on this same clause).
 The `claimed-item-timeout` sweep auto-completes a timed-out claim **by writing `site_work_items` directly**, so neither completion gate runs — until the live clause excludes your type, that sweep completes items **straight past the verifier you just added**. That is `bugs_closed/317` reintroduced *by the act of adding a guard*, and the test says it plainly: *"the declaration alone changes nothing in production"*.
  2. `TestOnlyTheOptedInVerifierCarriesAScopeTest` — if you declared `VerifierPolicy.Grades`, license it in `optedIn` **with an archive-inclusive producer-shape measurement**. Its own failure text names the trap: the live table is a ~7-day window, and the discriminator is the **spec shape**, never `item_type`, never `created_by`.
  3. `TestEveryItemTypeIsVerifiedOrAnAcknowledgedGap` — remove the type from `itemTypesWithoutVerifiers`, or the gap list is lying.
  4. `TestEveryPagesQueryingCheckDeclaresItsLifecyclePosture` — if your verifier queries `pages`, declare its posture. ⚠ **The reasoning INVERTS for a verifier:** arming the lifecycle filter is the UNSAFE direction, because an archived page can still be serving, so a retired page whose component still renders the defect must be **graded** rather than have its `ErrNoRows` read as "page gone, resolved".
  5. `TestUnarmedCompletersOfVerifiedTypesAreAcknowledged` (`WII-031`) — every arm that completes your type through an unarmed `update_work_item_status` must be armed or carry a recorded reason.
- **the check — do step 1 FIRST, and prove it at the live object, not at the Go declaration:**
  ```sql
  -- is the live clause actually excluding your type yet?
  SELECT pre_query LIKE '%<your_item_type>%' AS live_clause_has_it
  FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE name = 'claimed-item-timeout';
  ```
  Then `go run ./cmd/config-key-audit --live-declaration-drift` — it probes that exact column against `livespec.Declarations` key `scheduled_task.claimed-item-timeout.exclusions`, and `compareAllDeclarations` iterates **every** declaration with no `Phase` filter. ⚠ **`PhaseGoSide` is the CHECKED state and `PhaseLiveAudit` is the INERT one** — the opposite of what the names suggest, and reading them backwards is how a council seat concluded phase 2 was unbuilt when it had shipped.
- **and the ordering trap inside the ordering trap:** satisfying guard 5 by ARMING an arm can break a live route. `CQ-023` records that a `required_fields_missing` verifier fail-closes the `converted` arm of its router. Arm `close_stale` and `close_resolved` before `close_converted`, and read that router's close paths first — or take the acknowledgement arm, which is why `WII-031` demands a reason rather than a switch.
- **relations:** `WII-032` (the worked case, and a verifier written and deliberately left unregistered at exactly this point) · `WII-031` (guard 5) · `WII-030` (why the consult is opt-in at all) · `bugs_closed/317` (guard 1's reason) · `bugs_open/213` (guard 2's reason) · `bugs_closed/367` + migration 574 (which axis a verifier must resolve on — mirroring the detector's `deployed` filter rebuilds that bug one layer up) · `bugs_open/375`
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugfix_375_completion_verifier_gap` lane. Found by writing the `init()` and reading what broke, rather than by reasoning about it — the five-guard sequence is not documented anywhere else, and four of the five would have been invisible until the build ran.

### A bare number regex over an `evidence-chart`'s `rendered_html` returns SVG COORDINATES — and some of them equal real former fact values, so the wrong surface can confirm your hypothesis

- **footprint:** `cmd/claimscan`, `page_components.rendered_html`, `page_components.content_data`,
  the `evidence-chart` component function, `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/claims.go`
  (`numberSupported`, `ScanUnregisteredNumbers`), any dry run counting "which published numbers are
  registered"
- **fires when:** you need the published numbers on a page and reach for SQL — `regexp_matches(pc.rendered_html, '[0-9]{3,}')`
  or a `content_data::text LIKE '%<n>%'` — instead of the exporter + `cmd/claimscan`. Both feel like
  reading the page. Neither is the surface the scanners read, which is **extracted text blocks**
- **the tell, and it is easy to miss:** the same numbers appear on *every* page you scan. Measured
  2026-08-25 on fundamentallyai.com, three components returned an identical 13-value list — 127,
  320, 555, 600, 620, 625, 666, 700, 766, 875, 1200, 9375, 8125 — because `evidence-chart` draws
  SVG and those are viewBox bounds and plot coordinates. Real findings do not agree that precisely
  across different copy. `cmd/claimscan` over the same 91 components reported **5** findings, on one
  page, and none of the 13
- **why it is a landmine rather than an ordinary slip:** **two of the coordinates, `8125` and
  `9375`, are genuine former values of `F10-feed-items-scored`.** So a hand-rolled scan can
  *confirm* a hypothesis about former values using chart geometry, and the agreement reads as
  evidence. A wrong surface that disagrees with the truth gets caught; one that accidentally agrees
  does not
- **and the second half:** `content_data` is a STAGING field holding the whole register snapshot,
  including each fact's claim text *and its writer guidance* (`"… always say so"` — present in
  `content_data` on all 3 components, in `rendered_html` on none, so not published). Presence of a
  value there does **not** mean the page renders it: two `landing` pages stored `11646` and drew it
  nowhere, so they are not convicted. `page_type=landing` is NOT on `editorialPageTypes`
  (guide, blog-post, news-index, tool, game) — do not reach for the skip list to explain a silence
  it does not cause
- **the check:** use the exporter recipe in `cmd/claimscan/main.go:27-40` — **all four columns**,
  because without `page_type` every page reads UNKNOWN and the tool disagrees with the gate it
  exists to predict — assert `wc -l` against the same predicate's `count(*)` before trusting it (the
  export truncates at exit 0 with only a stderr line), then run the binary. And check engine parity
  before quoting any result as "what the fleet does":
  `git diff <rolled provenance>..HEAD -- platform/orchestration/datahelpers/` must be empty; on
  2026-08-25 it was 122 lines, so a HEAD run predicted the post-roll gate, not the live one
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/386` lane, testing whether every stale rendered value was once
  a register value (it was — 5 of 5, once measured on the right surface). Full account:
  `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_386_counting_fact_drift/NOTES_counting_fact_drift.md`, and
  `WRONG_CALLS.md` same date
- **added:** 2026-08-25, bugfix_386 lane

### The customer submit script has an UNFIXED TWIN at the repo root — `scripts/…/082_submit_domain_unified.sh` was fixed, `./082_submit_domain_unified.sh` was not, and `check_untouched_twin` is `.go`-only so nothing fires

- **footprint:** `082_submit_domain_unified.sh` (both copies), `scripts/initial_messages/020_build_pipeline/082_submit_domain_unified.sh`, `run_improvement_sweep_once.sh`, `084_TRIGGER_diagnose_v1.sh`, `scripts/pattern-check.py` `check_untouched_twin`, `bugs_closed/327b`, any repo-wide census of `.sh` files that filters by directory prefix
- **fires when:** you fix, audit or census a shell script that exists in more than one place, or you follow a runbook's `./082_submit_domain_unified.sh …` shorthand. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` **eight** documents give that shorthand. From the repo root it resolves to a copy last touched **2026-07-30** that still publishes on `kubectl run -i` stdin — the drop this very bug is named for — while the documented `scripts/…` path was fixed 2026-08-23 (`ab8ec8fbf`)
- **why nothing catches it:** `check_untouched_twin` opens with `if not path.endswith(".go")`, so a shell twin is invisible to the one detector written for exactly this shape. The two files share history to `95639d4f6` and diverge only by the fix, which is the hardest kind of twin to notice: identical name, identical purpose, one silently stale
- **the second half, and it is the more general trap:** **a census that partitions by directory prefix has a hole wherever a file has no directory.** `bugs_closed/327b`'s scope table sliced the class into `docs/` (out of scope) and `scripts/` + touched-in-30d (the queue). The repo root is in neither, so a racing publisher there is *absent* rather than counted — which reads as nothing to report. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` of 42 racing publishers touched within 30 days, exactly **2** were outside `docs/` and **both** were at the repo root; one (`run_improvement_sweep_once.sh`) was live work nobody had queued
- **the check:** census from the root with **no prefix filter**, then exclude — `grep -rl "kcat -P" --include="*.sh" . | while read f; do sed 's/#.*//' "$f" | grep -q "run -i" && bash -n "$f" && echo "$f"; done | grep -v '^docs/'`. ⚠ **and give any anchored path filter a control that must match**: `grep '^\./scripts/'` returns **0** here because `grep -rl` on this machine emits paths *without* the `./` prefix, and that false zero agrees with whatever you expected. Before trusting a fix on one copy, `find . -name "$(basename <file>)" -not -path './.git/*'`
- **source:** 2026-08-25, a session picking up `bugfix_327_silent_publish_drop/HANDOFF_2026-08-25_open_decisions.md` while another closed the bug. Full account: `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_327_silent_publish_drop/CONTRIB_2026-08-25_root_level_racing_publishers.md`, and `WRONG_CALLS.md` same date
- **added:** 2026-08-25, bugfix_327 lane (contrib)
- **UPDATED 2026-08-25, same day, by owner decision — the specific instance is closed, the class is not.** The root copy is now `DEPRECATED_082_submit_domain_unified.sh.txt` (renamed, banner added, `exit 64` if anyone `bash`es it). Renamed rather than deleted so the eight documents' shorthand resolves to an explanation instead of to nothing; the `.txt` is what makes it non-runnable AND uncountable by any `*.sh` census. **What still stands, and is why this entry stays:** `check_untouched_twin` remains `.go`-only, so the NEXT shell twin will diverge just as silently — and the directory-sliced-census half below has nothing to do with this file at all

## `pages.rendered_header`/`rendered_footer` are NULL on whole sites — a nav-membership check against them reads "never shipped" while the served site carries the link

- **footprint:** `pages.rendered_header`, `pages.rendered_footer`, `site_nav_items`, nav-updater verification, `nav_drift`
- **fires when:** you verify that a nav change (new page in the menu, relabel, reorder) actually
  shipped, and reach for the obvious query — `SELECT count(*) FROM pages WHERE site_id=… AND
  rendered_header LIKE '%<slug>%'`. No symptom needed; this is the natural first check after a
  `nav_drift` item completes.
- **the trap:** on finetuning.uk ALL 52 pages have `rendered_header IS NULL` and no
  `rendered_footer` carries the footer's actual link list `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` — the deployer
  assembles chrome from `site_nav_items` (+ global templates) at deploy time, and these columns
  are not that store. The count is 0 for every slug, forever, on such a site.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** 0 is precisely what "the wave
  completed but shipped nothing" would look like, and it composes with the true observation that
  52 `page_rerender` items read `complete` into a confident false conclusion. It was reported to
  the owner as "the nav link did not ship" within minutes of the wave completing — while the
  served /index.html already carried the link (footer group, `site_nav_items` position 4).
- **the check:** verify nav at the SERVED page (`curl -s https://<domain>/index.html | grep -c
  '<slug>'` and read the match's context — header vs footer group matters), plus the intent at
  `site_nav_items` (which GROUP the item landed in). Before trusting any `rendered_*` column as
  a store, ask whether it is populated at all: `count(*) FILTER (WHERE rendered_header IS NULL)`
  = all rows means the column cannot answer your question on this site, whatever it does
  elsewhere.
- **relations:** MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] · [[prove-a-deploy-at-the-artefact-index]] · the 016b "trust the rendered artefact, not the status" invariant — this is its inverse twin: trust the SERVED artefact, not a stored render column either
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `finetuning_uk_service` lane, verifying the nav wave for
  `/your-own-model.html`. Full account: `finetuning_uk_service/NOTES_finetuning_uk_service.md` 08-25b.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, finetuning_uk_service lane

## `--fidelity locked` on an adoption SKIPS the entire build cascade — the run succeeds, the site goes live, and nothing the framework builds is ever exercised

- **footprint:** `scripts/initial_messages/020_build_pipeline/082_submit_domain_unified.sh`, `platform/orchestration/actions/apply_adoption_plan_action.go`, `platform/orchestration/actions/adopt_verbatim.go`, `site-adoption-agent`, `site-adoption-orchestrator`, `needs_tool_recreation`, `fidelity`
- **fires when:** you adopt a site in order to EXERCISE something — a new save-path behaviour, a builder change, a check you have armed — and reach for `--fidelity locked` because the flag reads as "adopt it faithfully". No symptom needed; this is the natural first choice, and the script's own header recommends `locked` for "a hand-built site you intend to KEEP".
- **the trap:** `apply_adoption_plan_action.go:486` returns early on `fidelityLocked` into the byte-preserving path. The tool-recreation and content-page routing that queues every downstream build lives at `:708` — **two hundred lines below the return**. A locked adoption therefore queues no `needs_tool_recreation`, no `needs_content_page`, no classifier handoff, and no design cascade. It writes each crawled document through as one `ported-page` component with `rebuild_policy='owned'` and stops.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** the run COMPLETES, a real site row appears, pages appear, the site serves — and every counter you were watching reads exactly what it read before you started, because the code under test was never reached. There is no error, no refusal, and no log line saying "cascade skipped". `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` this lane needed one page through `save_page_sections`'s no-`<section>` fallback; `locked` cannot produce one at all, and would have left `adopted=0` looking like a broken mechanism rather than an untested one.
- **the check:** if you are adopting in order to TEST something, omit `--fidelity` entirely (adopt mode defaults to `high`, the recreate path) and then **assert the queue, not the run**: `SELECT item_type, handler_agent, spec->>'page_name' FROM site_work_items wi JOIN sites s ON s.id=wi.site_id WHERE s.domain='<domain>'` must show the handler you intend to exercise. Zero build items after a COMPLETED adoption is the signature. And read it back from the spawned agent, not the trigger — `call_agent`'s `input_mapping` is an allow-list and dropped `fidelity` at the spawn boundary until migration 274: `SELECT collected_data->'input_data'->>'fidelity' FROM orchestration_states WHERE owner_agent_type='site-adoption-agent' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;`
- **relations:** MEMORY [[zero-adoption-means-read-the-mechanism]] (a silent mechanism is usually UNDRIVEN, not missing — this is the trap that keeps it undriven while you believe you have driven it) · [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]]
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/357` lane, dispatching two adoptions to give phase 2 its first firing. Full account: `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_357_component_identity/NOTES_component_identity.md` 08-25 afternoon
- **added:** 2026-08-25, bugfix_357 lane

## An adopted page's INTERACTIVE classification does not track its HTML — a real calculator routed to the static builder while a script-free page routed to tool recreation

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/apply_adoption_plan_action.go`, `needs_tool_recreation`, `needs_content_page`, `tool-recreation-handler`, `page-build-handler`, `page.Features`, `interactive_features`
- **fires when:** you predict which builder an adopted page will go to — choosing a candidate site to exercise the tool path, sizing an adoption, or explaining after the fact why a page was rebuilt as prose. The obvious method is to fetch the source page and look for `<script>`, `<input>`, `<button>`. No symptom needed.
- **the trap:** the routing at `apply_adoption_plan_action.go:719` keys on `len(page.Features) > 0`, and `Features` comes from the crawl-and-analyse LLM step, **not** from a markup scan. The two disagree, and `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` they disagreed in BOTH directions in one afternoon: `lampenkap.com/index` carries a working lux calculator (1 `<script>`, 6 numeric/select inputs, a `runSim()` button doing real arithmetic) and was routed `needs_content_page` → `page-build-handler`; `cv1.co.uk/index` carries **zero** `<script>` tags and **zero** form controls and was routed `needs_tool_recreation` → `tool-recreation-handler`.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** the markup reading is genuinely correct about the markup — it is just not the instrument that decides. A prediction built on it is specific, checkable and confidently wrong, and nothing downstream contradicts it: the page builds, the site serves, and the only trace of the routing decision is a work-item row you did not look at. I picked `lampenkap.com` as "the surest single shot at the tool path" on exactly this reasoning and it was the one site that produced no tool item at all.
- **the check:** never predict it — **read it**, after the adoption plan lands and before you reason about anything downstream: `SELECT wi.item_type, wi.handler_agent, wi.spec->>'page_name', wi.spec->'interactive_features' FROM site_work_items wi JOIN sites s ON s.id=wi.site_id WHERE s.domain='<domain>' ORDER BY wi.priority;`. If you must choose a candidate site in advance, choose MORE THAN ONE — the classification is a judgement on crawled content and one site is a sample of one.
- **relations:** MEMORY [[a-subagent-report-is-another-doc]] (a naming convention is not a measurement — nor is a markup marker) · [[measurement-discipline-index]] — your measurement answers the question you ENCODED: `grep -c '<script'` encodes "does this file contain a script tag", never "will the platform call this a tool"
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/357` lane, adopting `cv1.co.uk` and `lampenkap.com`. Full account: `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_357_component_identity/NOTES_component_identity.md` 08-25 afternoon, and `WRONG_CALLS.md` same date
- **added:** 2026-08-25, bugfix_357 lane

### A `gte` evidence fact can be a ROLLING WINDOW, not a total — so it FALLS, and the honest floor claim it vouches for becomes a build-refusing finding on a day nothing changed
- **footprint:** `site_specs` `aspect='evidence_base'` `facts[]` with `tolerance:"gte"` and an `sql` source · `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/claims.go` `numberSupported` · `validate_page_content` check 8 (`unregistered_number`, severity **error**) · any published "over N" / "more than N" copy · `bugs_open/386`, `bugs_open/364`
- **fires when:** you satisfy a claims finding by registering a `gte` fact, or you read "0 findings" from `cmd/claimscan` and conclude a page's figures are safe. It fires hardest on exactly the copy this platform likes to write — *"we run over 1,600 X a day"* — because a floor claim looks permanently safe once a `gte` fact exceeds it.
- **the tell: none, and the page that breaks is the one nobody touched.** The copy is frozen, the register moves underneath it, and the verdict flips. Measured 2026-08-25 on `aao-orchestrations` (ai-agent-orchestration.com): **35 snapshots ranging 1,494–7,281, 17 FALLS across 34 transitions, below 1,600 on 3 of 35.** Replaying the site's own historic low through the scan: the identical CTA scores **0 findings at 7,281 and 1 finding at 1,494**, at `error` severity — the page refuses to build. Fleet-shaped on that site: **4 findings appear at the low that are absent today.**
- **why the obvious mental model is wrong:** a `count(*)` fact is assumed to accumulate. Many do not. `aao-orchestrations`, `C4-orchestration-state-records` and `aao-work-items` are **rolling windows or reaping ledgers** — `aao-work-items` fell 1,267 → 1,051 when its ledger reaped, and that was written down on 2026-07-24 in `sql_for_agents/218_evidence_facts_for_043_sites.sql:48` and read by nobody since. **8 of 29 sql-sourced number facts have fallen at least once** (`bugs_open/386` census, 2026-08-25).
- **the check, before you register a `gte` fact or trust one:** ask the register's own HISTORY, not its current row — the refresh supersedes rather than overwrites, so it is all there:
  ```sql
  SELECT ss.created_at::date, f->>'value'
  FROM site_specs ss, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(ss.data->'facts') f
  WHERE ss.site_id=$1 AND ss.aspect='evidence_base' AND f->>'id'=$2
  ORDER BY ss.created_at DESC;
  ```
  If `min(value)` is below the floor your copy publishes, the page is one refresh away from refusing.

  > **CORRECTED 2026-08-25 by the `bugs_open/386` lane, twice — read the correction, the original text was wrong in both halves.**
  >
  > **(a) THE REMEDY. This entry first said 386's history-retention fix resolves it. IT DOES NOT.** `historySupports` is **EXACT-match only**: with the fact at 1,494 and the page saying "1,600", the `gte` arm fails (1600 ≤ 1494 is false) and the history arm then asks whether 1,600 exactly equals a retained reading — it does not, the register held 7,281. The page stays convicted. I had reasoned "1,600 ≤ 7,281 and 7,281 IS a value the register held", which is **`gte` applied to history** — a semantics nobody built, and one that **should not** be built: it means "supported if val ≤ the all-time MAXIMUM", so one busy day would vouch for "over 7,000 a day" for ever on every quiet day after. That is the accidental-support gradient with time as the amplifier, strictly worse than tracking the current value. Exact-only is what makes history safe.
  >
  > **(b) THE ACTUAL REMEDY, and it needs no code at all: the register already specifies a safe floor and the copy ignores it.** `aao-orchestrations`' `writer_line` reads *"over a thousand orchestrations a day ({value} in the 24 hours to 2026-07-26)"*. **A floor of 1,000 sits BELOW the historic low of 1,494, so that instruction is safe on every day in the record.** The convicted copy says 1,600 / 1,699 / 1,834 — all **above** the low, so all three deviate from the register's own instruction or predate it. So this is not an evidence-layer defect: it is the owner's "state a floor" ruling applied with **the floor set too high**, and the fix is to bring the copy back to the floor the register already gives. **The rule that generalises: the floor must sit below `lowest`, not below today's value** (`bugs_open/386` RUNBOOK §7).
  >
  > **(c) And the floor attribution below was mis-assigned.** Corrected, all three read live 2026-08-25 with 39 snapshots each:
  > - `C4-agent-definitions-catalogue` — *"more than 150"*, historic low **157**. **Seven to spare: this is the "inside its floor only by luck" case.**
  > - `C1-records-verified` — *"more than 2,000"*, historic low **2,291**. Holds.
  > - `C1-records-enriched` — **carries NO floor at all**; its `writer_line` is a bare *"{value} of those enriched with filed accounts data"*. Range **937–9,370**, a tenfold swing, and an exact-value line over it. That is a different and worse shape than a floor set too high, and it is the one to look at first.
- **and the direction that makes it worse than an ordinary false positive:** a finding raised this way is at `error`, so it **blocks the rebuild** — the page cannot be corrected through the normal path until the counter recovers or a human intervenes. The claim itself was never false; only the evidence for it moved.
- **do not "fix" it by widening the floor blindly:** a broad `gte` with a loose `context_terms` silently vouches for every smaller number near that term, which is the accidental-support hole `bugs_open/364` §2 records. `aao-orchestrations` is `gte` on the single broad term `["orchestration"]` today — it is both halves of this trap at once.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/364` lane, found while checking a "no measured cost" claim of its own that turned out to be true only of the day it was measured; census and the reaping counter-example from the `bugs_open/386` lane
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/364` lane

## A locked instance that gets NO delivery attempt files NO refusal — so a coverage count built on refusals reads it as "fine"

- **footprint:** `site_work_items` `item_type='lock_blocked_change'` · `page_components.locked_by` / `lock_type` · `section_edit` delivery (`section_editor_actions.go`) · `fix_component_template_action.go` fan-out · any "how many placements took the change?" census over a template rewrite (RFC_032 / RFC_034 instance-scope conversions, `content_components.html_template`)
- **fires when:** you rewrite a shared template and then measure adoption. The natural instrument is the refusal trail — locked rows that blocked the write file `lock_blocked_change`, so you count those, subtract, and report the rest as delivered. It is wrong in the direction that makes you stop looking.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly right:** the refusal trail records **attempts**, not **placements**. A locked instance the fan-out never reached files nothing, and *"no refusal"* is the same reading as *"nothing to do"*. **[MEASURED 2026-08-25]** `evidence-timeseries` has three placements, all locked. Two were attempted, refused, and filed `lock_blocked_change` — so they are visible. The third (oufe.com `/cases/thames-water.html`, locked by `oufe-workstream`) received a whole-page `page_rerender` at **12:32:25Z**, i.e. **68 seconds BEFORE** the template conversion at 12:33:33Z, and nothing afterwards. No attempt, no gate, no row, and its owning lane was never told. A refusal-keyed count reports **2 blocked / 1 fine**; the truth is **3 of 3 unconverted**, and the page still serves `id="evidence-timeseries-leakage"` two days later.
- **and the same census, re-derived honestly, moved a lot more than one row:** counting placements whose stored `rendered_html` carries no `c-` token, against templates that DO spell `{{.InstanceID}}` — **48 of 437 unconverted, 26 of them locked (2026-08-25)**. The architecture record had `evidence-timeseries` as *"(3/3/3)"*, which counted the TEMPLATE being converted and reads to any later reader as the placements.
- **⚠ AND DO NOT CARRY THAT 48 ANYWHERE WITHOUT THIS NEXT LINE — it is not damage.** A literal element id only collides where the same component appears **twice on one page**. Narrowed the same day: **48 unconverted → 8 on a multi-instance (page, function) pair → 1 page with an actually duplicated element id → 0 reaching a visitor.** The one page is `webdesign.uk/index.html` (two `generic-text-block` rows both carrying a **UUID** id — the retired `{{.ComponentID}}` binding frozen in bytes that never re-rendered), and `webdesign.uk` **302-redirects** to `webdesign.co.uk`, a *separate* `sites` row; controls: an invented path on that domain also 302s, and the followed target has **0** occurrences of the UUID against four unrelated ids. So it is a **consistency debt**, and the standing risk is **the redirect, not the count** — if that domain ever serves its own content the page becomes damage with no other change. **This bullet exists because the bare number travelled one hop in under an hour** and landed in another lane's cold-start doc as live breakage; a corrected figure does not stop moving, so the narrowing must sit with the number wherever the number goes.
- **the check — census the ARTEFACT, never the refusals:**
  ```sql
  WITH conv AS (SELECT id, function FROM content_components
                 WHERE is_active AND html_template LIKE '%.InstanceID%')
  SELECT c.function, count(*) AS placements,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE pc.rendered_html NOT LIKE '%id="c-%') AS unconverted,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE pc.rendered_html NOT LIKE '%id="c-%'
                            AND pc.locked_by IS NOT NULL) AS unconverted_locked
  FROM page_components pc JOIN conv c ON c.id = pc.component_id
  WHERE pc.build_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'removed'
  GROUP BY c.function HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE pc.rendered_html NOT LIKE '%id="c-%') > 0;
  ```
  Then **check the ORDER of events per row**, because that is what hid this one: a `page_rerender` that completed *before* the template write did not carry the change and is not evidence of delivery. Compare `page_components.updated_at` against `content_components.updated_at`, not against the batch's start time.
- **the transferable shape:** a signal emitted only by ATTEMPTS cannot measure COVERAGE. Every guard that files a row on refusal has this property — the refusals tell you about the population you reached, and say nothing about the population you missed. If your denominator comes from the same machinery as your numerator, you are measuring the machinery.
- **source:** found and reported by the `news_editorial_features` lane, 2026-08-25, against the `bugfix_283_component_instance_scope` lane's 2026-08-23 conversion batch; RFC_032 §9a corrected the same day
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugfix_283_component_instance_scope` lane
