### Cloudflare analytics and GA4 have OPPOSITE blind spots — the gap between them is the design, and it reads exactly like a bug you can find

- **footprint:** Cloudflare GraphQL `httpRequests1dGroups` (`sum{pageViews}`, `browserMap`) · GA4 / `GTM-PQ3WCTBD` · any fleet traffic dashboard, weekly report or affiliate-application figure · `dartsonline_traffic` and `apis.uk` lane notes
- **fires when:** you have both sources and do the obvious thing — compare them, find Cloudflare's "human" page views far above GA4's users, and go hunting for the fault. **There is no fault.** They cannot agree, because each is blind to a different population:

  | | Cloudflare | GA4 |
  |---|---|---|
  | our own `curl` (28.5% of one site's page views) | **counted** | invisible — curl runs no JS, so it never fires GTM |
  | our own headless Chrome | counted | **counted** — it does run JS |
  | bots and search crawlers | counted, and this is the useful part | invisible |
  | ad-blocked / JS-disabled humans | counted | lost |
  | referrers, events, behaviour | none | the whole point |

- **why the wrong result looks exactly right:** both numbers are real, both are correctly collected, both are labelled "traffic", and the discrepancy is large and stable — which is precisely the signature of a genuine defect. Someone will reconcile them, fail, and file it.
- **the check:** never treat one as a cross-check on the other. **State which population you mean before quoting any figure.** For "is a human reading this site", GA4 is closer *and* undercounts. For "is Google crawling this site" only Cloudflare can answer (GoogleBot never executes GTM). For an affiliate application, say which source and which population, because the two differ by multiples.
- **⚠ and GA4 has NO HISTORY on this estate.** Measured 2026-08-25 by the `apis.uk` lane: `GTM-PQ3WCTBD` was live on **24 sites** carrying **0 tags and 0 triggers** — loading everywhere and firing nothing, for months. A GA4 tag was added the evening of 2026-08-25 (container Version 2). **There is no backfill**, so GA4 begins at that publication and **Cloudflare remains the only source with a past.** Any before/after comparison spanning that date is comparing a source to its own absence.

### `git log -N -- <path>` answers "what LAST TOUCHED this file", never "what INTRODUCED this code" — and on a shared tree those are different commits, so the sha you write down sends the next reader to a commit containing none of it
- **footprint:** any `git log -1/-3 -- <path>` used to attribute a change · a sha written into `WRONG_CALLS.md`, `NOTES_*`, a `bugs_open/` file, a concept-register entry or a council trailer · `docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/WRONG_CALLS.md`, `LANDMINES.md` and any other file many lanes append to · `platform/orchestration/datahelpers/claims.go` and other hot shared files
- **fires when:** you are tracing a same-file passenger — "who swept my work in?" — which on this tree is the commonest reason anyone needs a sha at all. It fires hardest on the files most lanes touch, because those are exactly the ones where "last touched" and "introduced" diverge within minutes.
- **the tell: NONE, and this is the whole entry.** A path-filtered log always returns a commit, that commit always really did touch the file, and it is always recent — so it looks like an answer no matter how wrong it is. There is no error, no empty result, nothing to notice.
- **MEASURED 2026-08-25 — the same mistake, by two different lanes, in one day, both landing on the same innocent sha:**
  - the `bugs_open/386` lane reported its fact-history mechanism swept into `001211abf`. Pickaxe: `git log -S 'FactHistoryEntry' -- claims.go` → **`6548e8d79`**. `001211abf` added **only comment lines** to that file (25/6, zero non-comment additions); it surfaced in a `-S historySupports` search only because its prose *names* the function while describing it.
  - the `site_ai_agent_orchestration` lane reported its `WRONG_CALLS` entry swept into `001211abf`. Pickaxe on that entry's own heading → **`3d31b86a9`**, the `bugs_open/381` lane's commit. `001211abf`'s `WRONG_CALLS` diff contains only its author's two entries.
  - **and a THIRD way in, which is the one to watch for, because it is not making a wrong attribution but ENDORSING one.** One message after diagnosing this trap and running `git log -S` to fix its own case, the `bugs_open/386` lane adjudicated the second lane's identical error by **reading the two documents and running nothing**, then reported "a legitimate separate use, not my error propagating" in the confident register of a check. **Knowing a check and applying it to your own claim does not generalise to someone else's** — and it is most dangerous exactly there: immediately after being corrected, when the correction has made you feel careful without making you run anything. The second claim did not feel like a claim; it felt like reading. (Their own entry, recorded against themselves.)
  All three shas were written into lane NOTES *specifically so a `098` coverage flag could be hand-traced* — which is the one use where a wrong sha costs the next reader a real search. **One is an anecdote; three modes in one day is the pattern**: make it, inherit it, endorse it.
- **the check:** use the **pickaxe**, and search for the SYMBOL or the sentence, not the path:
  ```bash
  git log --oneline -S '<distinctive symbol or verbatim phrase>' -- <path>   # what INTRODUCED it
  git log --oneline -1 -- <path>                                            # what LAST TOUCHED it — a different question
  ```
  Then **confirm by reading the diff, because `-S` has its own trap**: it matches any change in the number of occurrences, including a commit that merely *mentions* the symbol in a comment or a commit message body. Both mis-attributions above are that trap. `git show <sha> -- <path> | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+\s*//'` is empty for a comment-only commit and is the two-second discriminator.
- **and the asymmetry that makes this worth an entry rather than a note:** the SWEEPER is the only party who can still prevent a same-file passenger (`git diff --numstat <file>` before committing — see the sibling entry); the SWEPT party can only ever attribute it afterwards, from the log, with the wrong tool close to hand. So the party doing the forensics is the one who cannot fix it, and the mis-attribution then points at an innocent commit — twice, on one day, at the same one.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/364` lane, after being named as the sweeper by two lanes and being the sweeper in neither case (it was the sweeper in a third, `6548e8d79`); the command-vs-question diagnosis is the `bugs_open/386` lane's own, recorded in its NOTES
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/364` lane
- **HAND-VERIFIED 2026-08-25 (the landmine-verifier returned UNVERIFIABLE — "cannot check", not "doubtful": its code index is Go-only and every footprint here is `.sh`/`.py`/`.txt`).** Checked by hand, each claim: `check_untouched_twin`'s guard is `if not path.endswith(".go") or path.endswith("_test.go"): continue` — confirmed verbatim; the two copies shared history to `95639d4f6` — confirmed; `grep -rl … .` emits paths with no `./` prefix, so `^\./scripts/` matches **0** while `scripts/` matches **133** — confirmed, and that is the control this entry asks for. **ONE CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE: it is SEVEN documents that give the `./` shorthand, not eight** — my original pattern carried a `^082…` alternative that also matched a document naming the script in prose. 94 name the file in some form. **And the re-count returned NINE, because two matches were files I had written that same day** (this entry and the CONTRIB) — the lane's own "your writing about the trap contaminates your grep for it", fourth occurrence, landing on the verification of my own claim. **Exclude your own files by name before counting, exactly as you strip comments**

### `status_override` on a refusal step is an UNVALIDATED free string written straight into `site_work_items.status` — pick a status the dispatcher does not know and the row becomes undispatchable, un-promotable and un-re-filable, with every field looking healthy

- **footprint:** `platform/orchestration/actions/load_work_item_actions.go` (`FailWorkItemAction`, the `status_override` branch ~:1250-1265) · `site_work_items.status` · `idx_swi_dedup` · `platform/orchestration/actions/claim_work_item_action.go:102` · `platform/orchestration/actions/triage_detect_items_action.go` · any `agent_definitions` step config carrying `status_override` · any new agent refusal/park step
- **fires when:** you add or edit an agent's refusal step and choose what the parked row should say. The key takes a bare string — `statusOverride, _ := params.StepConfig.Config["status_override"].(string)` — and writes it into `status` with no allow-list, no enum, no CHECK constraint and no validation against the three predicates that actually decide a row's fate. `"deferred"` is the natural word for "park this" and is precisely the wrong one.
- **the tell: none, and every field argues the other way.** The UPDATE sets `error`, `status` and `handled_by` and **leaves `handler_agent` untouched**, so the row keeps a real handler name, a real priority and a real `item_key`, and carries an `error` explaining the refusal. It reads as a queued job that hit a snag. `attempt_count` is the only hint and it says `0`, which reads as "not started yet" rather than "will never start". Nothing logs a warning, nothing fails, and no status query treats the value as a problem.
- **why the wrong value is fatal, in three predicates nobody reads together:** (1) dispatch claims `status IN ('triaged','approved')`; (2) the promoter selects `status='detected'`; (3) `idx_swi_dedup`'s exclusion list is `complete, verified, rejected, wont_fix, failed, unresolved, cancelled` — read it from `pg_indexes`, not from the Go list. A value outside (1) and (2) but inside (3)'s *kept* set is undispatchable, un-promotable **and** still holding the `(site_id, item_key)` slot, so the detector that filed it cannot re-file and **any other session dispatching that page hits 23505**, a failure that reads as *"already queued"* and means *"queued and abandoned"*.
- **the check, before you set it:** read what the live fleet already uses, and match it — do not invent a value.
  ```sql
  WITH RECURSIVE walk(type, path, node) AS (
    SELECT ad.type, ARRAY[s.key], s.value
    FROM agent_definitions ad, LATERAL jsonb_each(ad.default_config->'workflow'->'steps') s
    WHERE ad.is_active AND COALESCE(ad.is_snapshot,false)=false AND ad.deleted_at IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT w.type, w.path||s2.key, s2.value
    FROM walk w, LATERAL jsonb_each(COALESCE(w.node->'config'->'sub_workflow'->'steps', w.node->'sub_workflow'->'steps','{}'::jsonb)) s2)
  SELECT type, array_to_string(path,'>'), node->'config'->>'status_override'
  FROM walk WHERE node->'config' ? 'status_override' ORDER BY 1,2;
  ```
  ⚠ **The walk must be RECURSIVE** — a flat `jsonb_each` over `default_config->'workflow'->'steps'` misses every step nested in a `sub_workflow` and will tell you a key is unused when it is not. [MEASURED 2026-08-25] all four live values are **`needs_human_review`**: `component-template-fixer>judged_refusal`, `component-template-fixer>park_refused`, `page-build-handler>mark_needs_review`, `tool-improver>refuse_mangled_write`. **That uniformity is CONVENTION, NOT CONSTRAINT** — nothing prevents the fifth from differing, and `needs_human_review` is safe here only because it is a decision queue with a surface, not because the key protects you.
- **kin:** the two `deferred` entries in this file (a parked row is undispatchable AND holds its dedup slot) — this is the mechanism by which a *new* one could be minted at production rate rather than by hand; `bugs_open/296` (a park that cannot drain); the `idx_swi_dedup` ↔ `workItemTerminalStatuses` lockstep, which migration 157 broke once fleet-wide with SQLSTATE 42P10.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `deferred_work_item_park` lane (out of `bugs_open/328`), while ruling `FailWorkItemAction` IN and then OUT as the producer of 118 untraceably-parked rows. It is not the producer — it stamps `handled_by` and those rows have none, and no live config names `deferred` — but establishing that is what exposed the key's shape. **Found by re-running a grep I had already run**: the first pattern (`SET status ... deferred`) cannot see a parameterised UPDATE, and the claim "no Go path can write this" was resting on it.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, deferred_work_item_park lane

## A lane's fence installer REBUILDS the `doc_plans` body from its source files, so any key added to the live row by hand is DELETED on the next `--apply` — clean exit, no error, and the fence silently declares nothing again

- **footprint:** `doc_plans.body` · ```` ```criteria ```` fences · `install_fences.py` (every lane fork: `loanandmortgagecalculator_couk/`, `mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption/acceptance/`) · `agritec_uk/install_fence_facts.py` · `staged_component_build/scripts/gen_probe_plan_sql.py`, `gen_component_plan_sql.py` · `brochure_component_library/.../travelling_docs.py` · `gauntlet_dead_cta/round_record/build_record_page_sql.py` · `acceptance/criteria/*.criteria.json` · the fence-level `facts` key · `doc_notes` category `fact_binding_suggested` · CLM-022 · `bugs_open/288`
- **fires when:** you act on a `fact_binding_suggested` note — or on any advice of the form *"paste this into the tool's PLAN"* — by editing the `doc_plans` row, whether by hand, by migration, or with a small injector script that reads the live body and writes it back.
- **the trap:** several lanes install their criteria fence with a script that **regenerates the whole body from `acceptance/criteria/<slug>.criteria.json`** and then does an unconditional `UPDATE … SET is_current=false` + `INSERT`. The generated fence contains exactly the keys that script knows how to emit. A key it does not know about — `facts` being the live example — is not merged, not warned about and not preserved: it is simply absent from the next body. The row still reads `is_current`, still carries a valid fence, still passes every shape check. **The declaration is gone and the tool is back to being watched by nothing.**
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** every observable is green at both ends. Your paste succeeded (`has_facts = t`). Their re-install succeeded (`0 skipped`, no error, fence parses). Nobody ran a command that says "delete"; the key was never deleted, it was *not regenerated*, and no diff is printed because the script has no idea a previous body existed to compare against. The victim has no symptom to search on — and the mechanism this key feeds is a **silence** detector, so its failure mode is more silence.
- **the check, and it is one query:** before writing anything into a `doc_plans` row, ask **who wrote the one that is there**, and whether that writer would put your key back.
  ```sql
  SELECT subject_key, created_by, source, source_agent, created_at
  FROM doc_plans WHERE subject_type='tool' AND subject_key='<key>' AND is_current;
  ```
  Then `grep -rn "$(psql … created_by)" docs/agent_docs/` — `created_by` is very often the **installer's own hardcoded literal**, which names the script that will overwrite you. On the worked case the row read `operator:bugfix224-session`, that exact string is a constant in `loanandmortgagecalculator_couk/install_fences.py`, and the script had a `stamp-duty.criteria.json` resolving to that very subject. **If the writer is a generator, fix the generator's INPUT — never the artefact.**
- **⚠ the forks differ, so `grep` the one you are actually about to run — do not reason from the filename.** `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` across all **7** `doc_plans`-writing lane scripts: **1** reads the live body and injects (agritec's `install_fence_facts.py` — safe, and the reason agritec's own declaration survives), **1** rebuilds but carries `facts` through from its criteria JSON (mcalc — safe), **1** rebuilds and drops it (LMC — the only exposed population, now fixed), **4** write unrelated PLAN kinds. Two files named `install_fences.py` behaved **oppositely**; the 288 lane wrote a warning about the wrong one on exactly that assumption (`WRONG_CALLS.md` 15).
- **the durable fix, once you find one that drops your key:** add the carry to the generator (~3 lines) and declare from its source file, so the key is reproduced on every future run instead of surviving until the next one. Then prove it with a **body diff, not a summary line** — regenerate to a file, `diff` against the live `doc_plans.body`, and require that the *only* difference is your key before you trust `--apply`. These bodies are deterministic (hardcoded dates, no `now()`), so a clean diff is achievable and a dirty one is telling you the fence you are about to overwrite is not the fence the script would build.
- **generalises:** any artefact that is *generated* but *stored* has two sources of truth, and the stored one loses without announcement. Same shape as a committed build output, a scaffolded config, or a `kustomize`-rendered manifest edited in place. **Ask "what regenerates this, and does it know about my edit?" before "did my edit land?"** — the second question has a satisfying yes and the first is the one that decides.
- **⚠ EXTENDED 2026-08-25, same day, and this form is WORSE because no lane can patch it: the writer may be a PLATFORM AGENT, not a lane script.** `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` the three gamesdesign.co.uk tool PLANs carrying a `fact_binding_suggested` note read `created_by='tool-generator'` — the tool-generator agent writes the whole PLAN, and `tool-spawn-rate-balancer`'s body was **fully rewritten between 2026-07-29 and 2026-08-21 (28 of 41 lines changed)**, so regeneration is observed behaviour and not a hypothetical. CLM-021 already records that `tool-generator`/`tool-improver` name neither `writer_block` nor `evidence_base`, i.e. they cannot carry a `facts` key they do not know about.
  **So the LMC case was fixable and this one is not**, and the difference is worth knowing before you start: when the writer is a lane script you own, the durable fix is three lines in that script; when the writer is a platform agent, declaring by hand is knowingly writing something the next regeneration deletes, and the real fix is council-gated Go in the generator. **Check `created_by` FIRST — it tells you which of those two jobs you are actually taking on.** Until the generator carries it, a declaration on a generator-owned PLAN should be treated as expiring at the next rebuild, not as adopted.
- **relations:** CLM-022 (the `facts` mechanism this bit) · `WRONG_CALLS.md` 15 (describing the wrong fork of the same filename) · `bugs_open/288` §5c · MEMORY [[live-and-committed-are-independent-facts]] and [[a-one-off-deletion-is-not-a-class-fix]] (fix the producer, not the instance) · the sibling entry below, which is how you end up pasting the wrong CONTENT into the row this entry is about
- **verifier:** `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` (2026-08-25 12:38Z) — **a scope limit, and it asked for exactly the check the author had already run.** It confirmed the Go-side ```` ```criteria ```` fence construct in `check_tool_acceptance.go` / `load_doc_context_action.go` and found the entry internally consistent, but **all 7 Python scripts in the footprint are outside a `.go`-only index**, so it could answer none of them and said so. *Answered by the author the same day, first-hand:* the 7 scripts were enumerated by `grep -rln "INSERT INTO doc_plans" --include=*.py docs/agent_docs/`; LMC's rebuild-and-drop behaviour was read in its own source and then **demonstrated** — regenerated body diffed against the live `doc_plans.body`, identical apart from the key; and `created_by='operator:bugfix224-session'` on the live row was matched to that script's own literal. ⚠ Note its index is pinned to commit `e347c5ad` (2026-08-23), **two days behind this branch's tip**, so its zero rows carry no weight in either direction. Not an open objection.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `register_guards_code_phase_b` lane, found while acting on the first `fact_binding_suggested` note the mechanism ever filed — the advice in our own CONTRIB ("install through the lane's own fence installer; never hand-edit the doc_plans row") was right, and its one failure mode was that the installer would undo it.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `register_guards_code_phase_b` lane

## A `fact_binding_suggested` note proposes only the figures a value probe can MATCH — so adopting it verbatim declares a fence that LOOKS complete and watches half the tool

- **footprint:** `doc_notes` category `fact_binding_suggested` · fence-level `facts` · `platform/orchestration/actions/refresh_evidence_fact_suggest.go` · `refresh_evidence_fact_probe.go` (`factProbeMinValue = 1000`, `factProbeNotProbed`) · `site_specs.aspect='evidence_base'` · CLM-022 · `bugs_open/288`
- **fires when:** you adopt a machine-proposed binding by pasting its paste-ready `"facts": [...]` fragment, and take the length of that list as the size of the job.
- **the trap:** the suggester finds a registered value by looking for it **as a literal in the tool's script text**, and refuses anything below a measured distinctiveness floor of **1000**. So a fact is invisible to it whenever the register and the code **represent the same quantity differently** — and the commonest case in this estate is a rate: the register stores `5` (per cent), the code stores `0.05` (a fraction). Neither `5` nor `0.05` can match the other, and `5` would be refused by the floor even if it did. **The tool encodes the fact; the machine cannot say so; and nothing in the note tells you a category of fact was structurally unexaminable.**
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** the note is *correct* — every id it proposes is genuinely encoded, so every check you can run on it passes. The list is plausibly sized, the fragment is well-formed, and adoption produces a green fence naming real facts. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25, loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk `mortgages-stamp-duty`]` the note proposed **7**; the tool encodes **13**. The six it could not see were `2`, `5`, `5`, `5`, `10`, `12` — held in code as `0.02`, `0.05`, `0.10`, `0.12` plus one bare inline literal `(price - FTB_NIL_BAND) * 0.05` — i.e. **every rate in a stamp-duty calculator, which is precisely what a Budget moves.** Declaring the seven would have left them drifting behind a fence that reads complete.
- **the check, before adopting any binding suggestion:** open the tool's script and reconcile **both directions** — every id you declare exists in the register, *and* every constant the tool encodes is declared. Extract the script rather than eyeballing the page:
  ```sql
  SELECT rendered_html FROM page_components pc JOIN pages p ON p.id=pc.page_id
  WHERE p.site_id='<site>' AND p.name='<page>' ORDER BY pc.position;
  ```
  then pull `<script>…</script>` and read the constants. ⚠ **Per component — never `string_agg` the page's `rendered_html` and tokenise that** (a separate entry: one unbalanced `<script>` leaks the next component's prose into your "script text"). Compare the register's units against the code's: **percent-vs-fraction, pounds-vs-pence, annual-vs-monthly, and per-unit qualifiers carried in the register's `unit` field** are all shapes where the same fact has two spellings and only one is greppable.
- **do not "fix" this by lowering the floor.** It is measured, not chosen: 32.75% / 3.79% / 0.06% / 0.03% / 0.00% false positives at 1/2/3/4/5+ digits over 161 real tool pages. A two-digit rate is genuinely unmatchable by value alone. The honest instrument for a small figure is a human-authored `artifact_check` with surrounding context (`rate:0\.05` anchored on its neighbouring band), which is a different mechanism answering a different question — **broad one broad, sharp one sharp.**
- **generalises:** a suggestion engine's output is bounded by what it can OBSERVE, and that bound is invisible in the output. Treat any machine-proposed list as a **lower bound on the work**, never as its size — and ask what class of item the detector was constitutionally unable to nominate before you take its count as a scope. Same family as the probe reading `not_probed` on a whole rate-table site: the mechanism working correctly and telling you nothing.
- **relations:** CLM-022 · `bugs_open/288` §5c/§5d (agritec's 24 declarations, 24 × `not_probed` — the same blindness at the whole-site scale) · the entry above (where the paste then gets deleted) · MEMORY [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]] and [[your-measurement-answers-the-question-you-encoded]]
- **verifier:** `UNVERIFIABLE` (2026-08-25 12:41Z) — **and its own report says why that is not evidence:** *"NOTHING in this round was confirmed against indexed code, so absence claims here carry no weight in EITHER direction."* The index holds `.go` symbols only, at commit `e347c5ad` (2026-08-23) — and **`refresh_evidence_fact_suggest.go` / `refresh_evidence_fact_probe.go` did not exist at that commit**, having landed 2026-08-24, so the symbols it was asked to find were necessarily absent. *Answered by the author the same day, first-hand:* the skip-if-declaring arm is at `refresh_evidence_fact_suggest.go:167`, `Ambiguous` is written to the note body at `:284` and to no result field, the 30-day cooldown is at `:246`, and `factProbeMinValue = 1000` / `factProbeNotProbed` at `refresh_evidence_fact_probe.go:96`. The 7-vs-13 measurement was taken from the live register and the tool's own extracted script text, not from the index. Not an open objection.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `register_guards_code_phase_b` lane, found while adopting the mechanism's own first production suggestion — the lane had told another lane the same rule the day before ("declare what the tool ENCODES, not the subset that happens to be fenced") and then nearly sized its own adoption by the machine's list.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `register_guards_code_phase_b` lane

### A council APPROVAL never validates a MEASURED number — the seats cannot run anything, and two of the tables our evidence usually lives in are not in their schema at all
- **footprint:** any `Council-Reviewed:` / `Council-Submitted:` trailer cited as evidence · `bugs_open/*` and `architecture_review/RFC_*` sections that lead with "APPROVED round 1" · `grounded_in` figures in a `097` submission · the `load_schema_hint` step of `agent_definitions` where `type='council-gate'`
- **fires when:** you cite your own approval later — in a handoff, a register entry, a bug file, or to an owner — and the sentence reads as though the council confirmed the numbers the plan rests on. It fires hardest on a GOOD submission, because the more measurements you put in `grounded_in` the more the approval looks like it covered them.
- **the tell: none, and the verdict's own wording encourages it.** "APPROVED — all reviewers approve" says nothing about which claims were checkable, and a seat that could not verify something usually raises it as an ordinary advisory objection among others, so it reads as one more nit rather than as a stated limit of the review.
- **what a seat CAN see, measured live 2026-08-25** (re-read it rather than trusting this list — `SELECT default_config #>> '{workflow,steps,load_schema_hint,config,query}' FROM agent_definitions WHERE type='council-gate' AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL`): `agent_definitions, agent_error_log, content_components, diagnosis_artifacts, doc_notes, landmine, page_components, pages, site_plan_pages, site_plans, site_work_items, sites`.
  **NOT visible: `site_specs` and `orchestration_states`** — i.e. the evidence register and everything in `collected_data`, which between them carry most of what a claims-layer or workflow submission grounds itself on.
- **⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-25 by the `bugs_open/386` lane, and the correction is the whole entry — the bullet above is about what a seat is SHOWN, not what it can READ.** This first said "a seat can read a row; it cannot RUN anything". **A review seat executes NOTHING AT ALL — not even read-only SQL.** Measured live: every `review_*` step's config carries exactly seven keys — `ai_service, error_step, input_fields, output_format, prompt_template, temperature, tolerate_truncation` — with **no sql / query / tool / db key on any of them** (`… AND s.value->'config' ?| array['sql','query','tools','tool','db','database','queries']` returns **0**). The only `query_database` steps in the whole workflow are `load_schema_hint`, which runs BEFORE the reviews and injects a schema **description as text** into the prompt, and `compose_verdict` / `compose_verdict_checked`, which run AFTER them to assemble the result. **Nothing fetches data for a seat.** So the allowlist is the list of tables whose SCHEMA TEXT the reviewers are shown; it is not a query capability, and it is not what limits them. That is why `editquality` phrases objections as *"SQL checks against the given schema can't reach…"* — it is reasoning about what a query WOULD show, never reporting one it ran.
- **the consequence, which holds for EVERY table, allowlisted or not:** a figure that comes from executing anything — a corpus scan, a block-equivalence diff, a fleet dry run, a mutation test, `go test`, a `curl` — is unverifiable by the council, full stop. `page_components` is fully visible in the schema hint and that did not let any seat reproduce "775 pages / 2,042 components, zero differences", because no seat could run `cmd/claimscan` or read a row. Nor could any seat confirm "14 tests green, 7 mutations killed" in `bugs_open/386`'s round. **The allowlist is a red herring for this purpose; the seven-key config is the reason.**
- **the check:** when you cite an approval, say what it approved. It approved the PLAN and the REASONING; it did not re-derive your numbers. Put the re-derivation command next to the figure so a human can, and if a seat explicitly said it could not see a table — `prior_art_librarian` does this — **carry that sentence into your own notes rather than leaving it in the verdict**, because nobody re-reads a verdict body once the trailer exists. Worked case: `bugs_open/386` (approved r1, `18dba069`) rests on `site_specs` figures no seat could see; `bugs_open/364` Phase 2 (approved r1, `3ed2b792`) drew four schema-visibility objections from three seats, of which the `orchestration_states` one was genuinely unverifiable and the `content_components` one was merely un-shown — **a distinction worth keeping, but with the first half weakened as the `386` lane corrected on 2026-08-25: including the query makes your INFERENCE auditable — a reader can judge whether that query would answer that question — it does NOT make the number verified, because the seat still runs nothing.** The form to remember:
  > **A submission can make its reasoning checkable. Nothing a submission can do makes its evidence checked. Only someone re-running it does that.**
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/364` and `bugs_open/386` lanes, from `18dba069`'s `prior_art_librarian` objection asking that a human re-run the queries before arming; allowlist re-measured live rather than taken from the 2026-08-10 RUNBOOK entry it sits beside
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/364` lane

### `POST /c/<token>` must live on the SAME path as the GET — a suffix route compiles, passes every test, and 404s at the box with nothing in the service's logs

- **footprint:** `internal/core-manager/api/server.go` · `internal/core-manager/handlers/delivery.go` · `HandleConfirmPage` · `HandleConfirmTransfer` · `docs024_key_docs_latest/webdesign_uk_build_service/box/links.webdesign.uk.nginx` · `location ~` · `limit_except` · `links.webdesign.uk`
- **fires when:** you add, move or "tidy" any route under `/c/` — the obvious shapes being `/c/:token/confirm`, `/c/confirm/:token` or a versioned `/c/v2/:token`. Also fires when you narrow the box vhost, which looks like a pure hardening change.
- **the trap:** the customer-facing origin is not a catch-all. `links.webdesign.uk.nginx` proxies **one anchored regex** — `location ~ "^/c/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,128}$"` — so **anything with a suffix, a prefix segment or a differently-shaped token never crosses WireGuard at all.** The box answers 404 locally. Your handler is never reached, so **there is no log line, no metric and no error anywhere in the cluster**; `go test` passes, gin's route dump looks right, and a `curl` from inside the cluster (or against the pod) works perfectly. The failure exists only on the path a real customer takes, and only from outside.
- **the second half:** the same block carries `limit_except GET POST { deny all; }`. That is what makes the two-verb design legal today — but it is an enumeration, so a future `PUT`/`DELETE`/`PATCH` on `/c/` dies at the box the same silent way, and so would a preflight `OPTIONS`.
- **the check, and it must be run from OUTSIDE — inside the cluster proves nothing about the box:**
  ```bash
  T=$(python3 -c "import secrets,base64;print(base64.urlsafe_b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(32)).decode().rstrip('='))")
  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'GET  same-path  -> %{http_code}\n' "https://links.webdesign.uk/c/$T"
  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'POST same-path  -> %{http_code}\n' -X POST "https://links.webdesign.uk/c/$T"
  # CONTROL - the shape that MUST die at the box. If this is not 404, the regex is not doing what you think.
  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'POST suffix     -> %{http_code} (want 404)\n' -X POST "https://links.webdesign.uk/c/$T/confirm"
  ```
  A token-shaped path reaches core-manager and returns 200 on both verbs (an unknown token still renders a page, by design). **The suffix control returning anything other than 404 means the vhost has been widened**; the suffix control returning 404 while your new route "works" in tests means your route is unreachable in production.
- **why it is a landmine and not a bug:** every signal available to the session making the change says success. The estate's usual proof - build it, test it, ship it, grep the pod - is blind here, because the thing that refuses is upstream of everything the cluster can see.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `web_admin_console` lane, building the second-click confirmation page to `webdesign_uk_build_service`'s DECISION_2026-08-24 (which pinned same-path for exactly this reason, measured against the vhost rather than assumed)
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `web_admin_console` lane

### A STORED `acceptance_predicate` cannot be fed back to `EvaluateAcceptancePredicate` — it returns `inapplicable` on 100% of live predicates, and the reason reads like a fault in the model's output

- **footprint:** `spec.acceptance_predicate` · `EvaluateAcceptancePredicate` · `acceptancePredicateFields` · `verdict_at_emission` · `evidence_at_emission` · `predicateForEvaluation` · `storedPredicate` · `platform/orchestration/actions/verify_acceptance_predicates_action.go` · `complete_work_item_acceptance_predicate.go` · CLM-024
- **fires when:** you write ANY consumer of `site_work_items.spec->'acceptance_predicate'` — a completion gate, a sweep, a report, a one-off census — and pass the decoded object to the platform's own exported evaluator, which is exactly what the evaluator's doc comment invites you to do ("the evaluator it needs is one call, not a rewrite").
- **the trap:** `EvaluateAcceptancePredicate` enforces a **closed key set per predicate type** — a key it does not read REJECTS the predicate, deliberately, because "a key no checker reads is an assertion the artefact appears to make and does not". The emit-side gate STAMPS `verdict_at_emission` and `evidence_at_emission` onto the predicate **after** evaluating it. So the shape that lands in the database carries two keys the evaluator refuses, and **every stored predicate evaluates to `inapplicable`**. Strip them (`predicateForEvaluation`) and the same predicate over the same string returns `refutes`.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** `inapplicable` is a legitimate, expected verdict — it is what a predicate naming a page that has left the surface returns, and what a vocabulary change returns. So a consumer reading 100% `inapplicable` sees a plausible outcome, and the rejection message names a KEY, which reads as a fault in the model's output rather than in the reader. A gate built this way grades nothing and reports nothing wrong.
- **and NOTHING in the test suite catches it:** `TestTheFirstLiveEmittedPredicatesStillRefuteAfterTheFix` is the only test over real live predicates, and it hand-writes them WITHOUT the provenance keys — so the estate's most-cited evidence about this feature exercises a shape the database does not contain. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` all 3 live predicates carry both keys; `SELECT jsonb_object_keys(spec->'acceptance_predicate') FROM site_work_items WHERE spec ? 'acceptance_predicate'` shows them.
- **the check, before you evaluate anything you read out of a spec:** compare the key set you have against the closed set for its type, and assert BOTH directions in one test — the stored form must be `inapplicable`, the stripped form must be `refutes`. Either assertion alone passes for the wrong reason. In Go: `EvaluateAcceptancePredicate(predicateForEvaluation(stored), subject)` — **never** the stored map.
- **do NOT "fix" this by widening `acceptancePredicateFields` to admit the provenance keys.** That would let the MODEL write its own `verdict_at_emission` and have the gate accept it — a predicate asserting its own checkability, which is `bugs_closed/335`'s self-attribution failure exactly. The stamp and the strip are single-sourced in the file that owns them and pinned to each other by `TestStampAndStripAreInverses`, which fails when a THIRD provenance key is added to one and not the other.
- **generalises:** whenever a validator ENRICHES what it validated before storing it, the stored artefact is no longer a valid input to that validator. Ask "does the thing I am reading still satisfy the contract of the thing that wrote it?" — provenance stamping, envelope wrapping and audit fields all break round-tripping the same silent way.
- **relations:** CLM-024 · `bugs_open/395` §2 · `bugs_closed/335` (self-attributing artefacts) · MEMORY [[a-print-statement-is-not-a-config-row]] and [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]]
- **verifier:** `UNVERIFIABLE` (2026-08-25) — **and its own report says why that carries no weight in either direction:** *"NOTHING in this round was confirmed against indexed code."* All 10 footprint checks returned 0 rows against an index pinned to commit `e347c5ad` (2026-08-23), and **every symbol in the footprint was created 2026-08-24/25**, so the zeros are index staleness, not absence. *Answered by the author the same day, first-hand and re-runnable:* the closed-key-set loop is `verify_acceptance_predicates_action.go` `EvaluateAcceptancePredicate` (the `for k := range pred` guard immediately after the type lookup); `acceptancePredicateFields["text_order"]` admits `field/page/before/after` only; the stamping is `storedPredicate`; and the round trip is asserted BOTH ways by `TestTheLiveStoredPredicateIsUnevaluableUntilStripped`, which feeds the LIVE stored JSON (read from `site_work_items.spec` for item `b4c82ec3`) and requires `inapplicable` stored / `refutes` stripped. Not an open objection.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `vigilant_designer_offer_analysis` lane, found while building the completion-time consumer `bugs_open/395` asks for — the first consumer this design ever had, and it would have shipped permanently blind
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `vigilant_designer_offer_analysis` lane

### `pattern-check.py`'s `logged-model-output` rule reads STRING LITERALS AND COMMENTS — an ordinary English word in your prose fires it exactly like a payload being logged, and the comment explaining that re-fires it

- **footprint:** `scripts/pattern-check.py` · `PAYLOAD_NAME` · `LOG_SINK` · `SAFE_WRAPPERS` · `check_logged_model_output` · the `logged-model-output` finding · any `logger.Warn`/`Info`/`Error` in a package whose directory contains a file calling `GenerateText`
- **fires when:** you write a log call, anywhere in an LLM-adjacent package, whose format string, field values **or inline comments** contain any of `text`, `body`, `completion`, `response`, `raw`, `content`, `output`, `prompt`, `partial` — as a word, in prose. Nine ordinary English words; `response` and `content` in particular are nearly unavoidable in a remedy sentence.
- **the trap:** the rule accumulates **six raw lines from the log sink**, drops only the text up to the FIRST COMMA, and runs `PAYLOAD_NAME` over what is left. It never strips string literals and never strips comments, so it cannot distinguish a payload being LOGGED from a word being TYPED. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` a `zap.Warn` carrying an item id, an item type, a gate-authored detail and a fixed remedy — **no model data whatsoever** — fired it because its remedy ended *"NOT the model's output"*. ⚠ **And the first comma is inside most format strings**, so the "skip the format string" step usually skips half a sentence, not the string.
- **the sting in the tail, and it cost a second commit:** the natural fix is a comment beside the line saying why the wording is odd. **That comment is inside the six-line window and re-triggers the rule at the same line number**, because it necessarily names the very words it is telling you to avoid. Put the note in the function's doc comment, above the log sink, or it fires for ever.
- **the check:** treat a `logged-model-output` finding as a QUESTION, not a verdict — read the flagged line and ask whether a payload VALUE reaches the sink, or only a word. Reproduce and disconfirm rather than reword-and-hope: `python3 scripts/pattern-check.py --commit <sha>` must fire before your change and be silent after, with **nothing else altered**.
- **⚠ AND THE SILENT RUN IS THE WORSE HALF: `python3 scripts/pattern-check.py` with no arguments reads `git diff --cached`.** An unstaged fix means it scans **ZERO files** and prints exactly what a passing run prints. Always confirm the denominator — `git diff --cached --name-only | wc -l` — before believing a clean result. This is `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-07-27b, written by this rule's own author about this rule, and it is just as easy to walk into from the consumer side.
- **do NOT silence it with an allow-list** — the rule catches a real class (`bugs_open/362` §6 counts 25 standing findings). Reword the prose, record the false-positive mode, and leave narrowing the rule to whoever owns it; the honest narrowing is to strip Go string literals and `//` comments before matching, which needs a council round because `scripts/pattern-check.py` is in scope (CLAUDE.md, 2026-08-24 widening).
- **generalises:** any source-scanning detector that matches raw text makes your COMMENTS AND PROSE load-bearing, and the first thing an author writes when one misfires is a comment containing the trigger. Same family as a prompt scoring as the behaviour it describes.
- **relations:** `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-07-27b (the same rule, scanning nothing) · `bugs_open/362` §6 · MEMORY [[prompt-text-poisons-its-own-detector]], [[a-source-scanning-test-makes-comments-load-bearing]] and [[declaring-a-key-silences-your-own-detector]]
- **⚠ INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, and it had already cost another lane the SAME two commits.** The landmine verifier surfaced `platform/orchestration/actions/palette_specialised_slots.go:676-683`, where a different lane's `zap.Warn` carries this comment: *"Worded to keep pattern-check's logged-model-output rule quiet — it matches a certain three-letter word for unprocessed data anywhere inside a log call, **INCLUDING in a comment explaining its own absence, which is how the first version of this comment re-tripped the very check it was documenting**."* Two lanes, independently, hit both halves — the prose match AND the explanatory comment re-firing it. Note that author could not name the word in their own comment. **That is two lanes paying the same tax for a rule nobody has narrowed, which is the case for narrowing it.**
- **verifier:** `NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW` (2026-08-25) — **a scope limit, and it found the corroboration above while stating it.** The index holds `.go` symbols only, so `scripts/pattern-check.py` and its constants are unreachable by it and the mechanism claims (six-line window, first-comma skip, no literal/comment stripping) could not be checked. *Answered by the author the same day, first-hand:* `LOG_SINK`/`PAYLOAD_NAME`/`SAFE_WRAPPERS` at `pattern-check.py:1354-1362`, the six-line accumulation and `probe.split(",", 1)[-1]` in `check_logged_model_output` — and the behaviour was **demonstrated, not read**: the rule fires on `--commit 2fde4def9` and is silent on the fix, with the file staged so the run has a non-zero denominator. Not an open objection.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `vigilant_designer_offer_analysis` lane, on commits `69479bcf6` → `2fde4def9` → `b96529372` — three commits to remove one false positive, because the second reproduced it and the third caught that the clean result proving the second had scanned nothing
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `vigilant_designer_offer_analysis` lane

### `snapshot_agent()` RETURNS THE SOURCE ROW'S ID, NOT THE SNAPSHOT'S — so the obvious "compare against the pre-image" verify compares the live row with itself and reports a clean apply

- **footprint:** `snapshot_agent` · `agent_definitions_backup` · `agent_definitions` · `snapshot_taken_at` · `snapshot_reason` · `is_snapshot` · any `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/NNN_*.sql` that edits an agent's `default_config`
- **fires when:** you apply a migration that changes a live agent (the estate's standard shape: `SELECT snapshot_agent('<type>', '<reason>');` then `UPDATE agent_definitions …`), and then verify it INDEPENDENTLY of the migration's own `DO`/`RAISE` block — which is exactly what this estate's discipline tells you to do, and exactly when this bites.
- **the trap:** `snapshot_agent()` prints one uuid and a `NOTICE` naming it `source_id=…`. It is the id of the row you asked it to snapshot — the LIVE row. The snapshot itself is a separate row in **`agent_definitions_backup`**, keyed by `type` + `snapshot_taken_at`, carrying `snapshot_reason`. Join the printed id back to `agent_definitions` believing it is the pre-image and you have joined the live row to itself.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** every field of that self-join is what a perfect apply looks like — `before_n = after_n`, `every_pre_apply_name_survives = true`, `names_lost = none`. Measured 2026-08-25 on migration `603`: it reported 45 → 45 with nothing added and nothing lost, while the real answer was 44 → 45 with exactly one name appended. **A self-comparison cannot fail, so it certifies a total no-op and a correct apply identically.**
- **the check, in one line:** put both sides' identity in the result before you read the numbers — `SELECT snap.snapshot_taken_at, live.updated_at, …` or the two row ids side by side. If they are the same row, or the snapshot side is NULL, the diff is theatre. The correct pre-image is:
  ```sql
  SELECT default_config -> … FROM agent_definitions_backup
   WHERE type = '<agent>' AND snapshot_reason LIKE '<NNN>_%'
   ORDER BY snapshot_taken_at DESC LIMIT 1;
  ```
- **the tell that saved it:** `agent_definitions` has NO `snapshot_reason` and NO `agent_type` column, so a query written against the wrong table errors on the column name. Chasing that error is what revealed the snapshot lived elsewhere. If your verify does not reference a snapshot-only column, nothing will stop you.
- **generalises:** a before/after comparison whose two sides are not PROVABLY DISTINCT is not a comparison. Before trusting one, name what the disconfirming result would look like and check the query could produce it — same rule as a mutation test, applied to SQL.
- **relations:** `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-25 (this incident) · MEMORY [[mutate-the-code-to-prove-the-guard]], [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]] · CLAUDE.md "Migration runner practice"
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/384` lane, applying `603_enable_page_list_stale_HOLD.sql`
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/384` lane

### A template edited by SQL ships NOTHING — the `template_changed` fan-out lives in `component-template-fixer`, an LLM repair agent you are not going to invoke, and its query has no page-status filter

- **footprint:** `content_components.html_template` · `component-template-fixer` · `create_rerender` · `template_changed` · `check_rerender_mode` · `page_rerender` · migration `460` · `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/` component-template migrations
- **fires when:** you change a library component's `html_template` (or its `input_schema`) by migration — a colour fix, a new field, an accessibility repair — and expect the pages carrying it to show the change.
- **the trap:** every page keeps serving its STORED `rendered_html`. Nothing re-renders on a `content_components` write: the only producer of `spec.reason='template_changed'` re-renders is the `create_rerender` step INSIDE `component-template-fixer`, keyed on the component id that agent just fixed. So a migration applies cleanly, verifies cleanly, and changes nothing anyone can see — indefinitely, with a green status and no error anywhere (`bugs_open/283` §13 found this end-to-end: 111 items completed, page DEPLOYED, served bytes unchanged).
- **so you must fan out by hand** — one `page_rerender` / `spec.reason='template_changed'` per page carrying the component. `template_changed` is in `page-rerender.check_rerender_mode`'s reason list (migration `460`), so ONE re-render both re-resolves the `query.*` arrays and renders the new template, with no LLM.
- **⚠ AND DO NOT COPY THE FIXER'S QUERY AS-IS.** Read it from `agent_definitions` (not from `460`'s text — the live row has since gained `p.rebuild_policy IS DISTINCT FROM 'owned'`), and note what it STILL lacks: **any page-status filter**. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` of 60 live `tool-cta` instances, **16 sit on ARCHIVED pages** — the fixer would re-render and re-publish all 16, which is `bugs_open/098` exactly (archiving sets `status`, leaves `build_status` alone, and a retraction becomes self-undoing). It also omits `page_id`: only **4 of 272** live `template_changed` items carry one, against ~100% for every other reason class, and without it you cannot join an item back to its page to ask whether it landed somewhere it should not have.
- **the check:** after applying, assert at the ARTEFACT, not the migration — `SELECT rendered_html LIKE '%<your new class>%'` on a page carrying the component. Before the fan-out that is FALSE on every page, which is the honest baseline; after it, count the pages where it turned true and confirm none sits on an archived or `owned` page.
- **generalises:** DB config is live the moment it applies, but STORED RENDER OUTPUT is not config — anything already materialised into `rendered_html` needs a producer to regenerate it, and "the migration verified" says nothing about the bytes being served.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/283` §13 · `bugs_open/098` · migrations `460`, `614`, `615` · REB-002 · MEMORY [[a-stale-page-holds-every-improvement-since-it-rendered]], [[live-and-committed-are-independent-facts]]
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/384` lane, shipping `tool-cta`'s image (migration `614`) and having to write its own fan-out (`615`)
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/384` lane

### Censusing "work items with no handler" by `handler_agent IS NULL` finds NOTHING, and the owned-page door keeps the PRODUCER's name on every row it parks — so parked work reads as live, named work

- **footprint:** `site_work_items.handler_agent` · `site_work_items.created_by` · `status='deferred'` · the owned-page door (`writeWorkItem`, `platform/orchestration/actions/load_work_item_actions.go`) · `OWNED_PAGE_GUARD` · `bugs_open/396` · any "who owns this queue / what is unhandled" census
- **fires when:** you count, group or triage work items by whether they carry a handler — a backlog census, a provenance hunt, an "is this population growing" re-measure.
- **the trap, in two halves that compound.** (1) `handler_agent` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''::text`, so a cleared handler is the **empty string**: `IS NULL` finds nothing and `IS NOT NULL` is TRUE for every parked row. (2) **The door clears the handler but PRESERVES `created_by`.** So a parked row still carries the name of whatever filed it, and a `GROUP BY created_by` shows it sitting under an active producer — indistinguishable from live, named, dispatchable work. Measured 2026-08-25: `content_rewrite` at `deferred` splits **11 genuinely named** (`voiceh-rollout` 9, `apis-uk-bees-lane` 2) against **41 door-parked** (`required-fields-missing-handler` 28, `tool-generator` 13); an `IS NOT NULL` census returns **52** and reads as a population that has quintupled in a day.
- **the check:** group by the ways the field can be GONE, and print the discriminator instead of trusting a filter —
  ```sql
  SELECT coalesce(created_by,'(null)') AS parker, (handler_agent IS NULL) AS is_null,
         (handler_agent = '') AS is_empty, (COALESCE(handler_agent,'')<>'') AS truly_named, count(*)
  FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='<type>' AND status='deferred'
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 5 DESC;
  ```
  Genuinely named = `COALESCE(handler_agent,'')<>''`. Door-parked = handler cleared **AND** `error LIKE 'OWNED_PAGE_GUARD%'`. **A population defined by an ABSENCE cannot be censused by a field that is still present.**
- **⚠ the column fact is ALREADY in this file** — see the `mistyped_deployed_page` entry, whose fourth bullet states `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''::text` and whose footprint was widened **2026-08-02** precisely because it had bitten a second lane on an unrelated no-handler refusal. **This is the third occurrence.** The entry did not protect me because I grepped the *situation* (parked deferred rows) and not the *symbol*, which is exactly what MEMORY [[grep-landmines-for-your-symbols]] exists to stop: the SessionStart hook matches DIRTY PATHS, and a table-and-column footprint can never match one. Grep `handler_agent` before you count it.
- **generalises:** a sentinel that is a legal value of the column (`''`, `0`, `'unknown'`) is invisible to the nullity test people reach for, and a mechanism that clears one field while preserving another leaves rows wearing their old identity. Ask what the clearing code actually WROTE, not what "cleared" suggests.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/396` (the parked-with-a-named-handler population — its census is clean, and this is why that distinction is load-bearing) · `bugs_open/333` (the door) · WII-028 · `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-25 · MEMORY [[grep-landmines-for-your-symbols]]
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/392` lane — I asserted "all 40 have `handler_agent` null" to another lane from a query whose own output printed BLANK rather than my `'(cleared)'` coalesce default, then re-derived the filter from memory and reported 11 as 52. Caught by the `bugs_open/333` lane before it reached a third lane's census.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `bugs_open/392` lane

### A `tool_crosslink` finding you filed with `related_pages` is PARKED, not delivered — and both ways of checking it pass anyway: the row count cannot fail, and the target article already links your tool

- **footprint:** `related_pages` (the `add_tool` spec key) · `site_work_items.item_key LIKE 'tool_crosslink:%'` · `status='deferred'` · `OWNED_PAGE_GUARD` · `pages.rebuild_policy='owned'` · `tool-generator` · `bugs_open/330` · migration `516` · `docs/agent_docs/docs024_key_docs_latest/webdesign_tool_rebuilds/RUNBOOK_native_rebuild_of_ported_tools.md`
- **fires when:** you file an `add_tool` carrying `related_pages` and then check whether the cross-mention — the one-sentence, in-context reference woven into a related article — actually appeared.
- **the trap, in two halves, and you need BOTH checks to be wrong at once, which is what happens.**
  **(1) The row census cannot fail.** The recipe every lane copied says "verify at the artefact rather than the item status" and then hands you `SELECT status, spec->>'page_name' … expect one row per page you named`. The rows are always there — the resolver reads your key and files correctly. What the query never makes you look at is the STATUS. On an `owned` page the row is parked by `bugs_open/333`'s door the same second it is created (`created_at` == `updated_at`, `handler_agent` cleared, `spec.not_dispatchable` set), and nothing further will ever happen to it. **`deferred` is a terminus, not a gate** — a phrase in one lane's notes called it "their normal gate", which reads as a queue, and that reading survived eight filings.
  **(2) So you grep the target article for the tool's name — and it is there.** On webdesign.co.uk all three articles checked already carried a styled CTA linking their tool (`learn-data-unicode-gremlins`: *"Use our Regex-powered cleaner… Launch Text Sanitizer →"*). It is hand-authored copy that came across with the original port. **That slot was last written 2026-08-15, ten days before the filing it appeared to vindicate.**
- **the check:** read the status value, and date the slot. `status='complete'` is delivered; `deferred` + `error LIKE 'OWNED_PAGE_GUARD%'` is parked. Then, before crediting any name-match on the article:
  ```sql
  SELECT pc.updated_at   -- must be LATER than your add_tool's completed_at, or the copy predates you
  FROM pages p JOIN page_components pc ON pc.page_id=p.id
  WHERE p.site_id='<site>' AND p.name='<the page you named>';
  ```
  **And census it live UNION archive.** `site_work_items` is a rolling window; a closed row is
  archived out of the table you queried. My first published figure read 13 `failed` because I asked
  the live table alone — 9 more sat in `site_work_items_archive`. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` on site `6b49db8e` (webdesign.co.uk), all history: **41 `wont_fix` · 15 `deferred` · **22** `failed` · 2 `unresolved` · ZERO `complete` across **80** rows since 2026-08-05, live table UNION `site_work_items_archive`** — no cross-mention has ever been written on that site, through two distinct failure regimes (before the door these burned a dispatch and died at `load_page_record`/`save_sections`; after it they park cheaply with advice attached).
- **⚠ and there is NO "just pick a writable page" lever — do not go looking for one.** `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` the 37 active non-tool pages on that site split **34 `owned` / 3 `generic`**, and the three writable ones are `domains`, `index` and `news` — the shopfront. **Every `/learn/` article is owned, so every topically-CORRECT pick parks by construction, and the only picks that would land are ones a correct pick would never name.** That is why the figure is zero-of-80 rather than some-of-80, and it is also why steering picks toward writable pages is the wrong repair: the runbook's rule is pick by topic, and an unrelated page produces a worse sentence, not a neutral one.
- **⚠ still carry the key.** The omission class is real and separate (`bugs_open/330`: **0 of 58** hand-filed `add_tool`s carried `related_pages` before 2026-08-24, and since migration `516` removed the resolver's substitution an omission means no finding at all, recorded only as `agent_error_log.error_code='tool_crosslink_not_emitted:no_related_pages'`). A parked finding aimed at the right page is the raw material for the owned-page route; an absent one is nothing. **File it, and describe it accurately.**
- **generalises:** when a mechanism's last mile is refused by a policy guard, the artefacts of its EARLIER stages are all still produced — so every check aimed at the stages you can see passes. Ask what the final writer wrote, and date it against your own action. **A pre-existing artefact is the most convincing false positive there is, because it is real.**
- **relations:** `bugs_open/333` (the door — correct and proven; this is not a fault in it) · `bugs_open/330` · `bugs_open/277` (closed 08-22) · the parked row's own `what_to_do`, which names the route that DOES work on an owned page (`section_edit` → `section-editor`, 44 complete / 1 failed as of 2026-08-24) · LANDMINES "Censusing work items with no handler…" (same door, opposite end) · MEMORY [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]], [[a-receipt-nobody-asserts-on-is-a-log-line]], [[a-pass-from-a-blind-check-outlives-the-blindness]]
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `webdesign_tool_rebuilds` lane — filing rebuild #41 I checked my own crosslinks for the first time and found eight tools' worth of mentions I had been counting as delivered had never been written, then nearly un-found it again on the pre-existing CTAs.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `webdesign_tool_rebuilds` lane

### An env-only config key on `platform/config.Load` is SILENTLY IGNORED unless it is `BindEnv`'d — the overlay reads perfectly, the value arrives empty, and "unset" and "set to empty" are indistinguishable

- **footprint:** `platform/config/loader.go` (`Load`, `v.AutomaticEnv()`, `v.Unmarshal`, `v.SetDefault`, `v.BindEnv`) · `ServiceConfig` / `ServerConfig` and every `mapstructure` struct it fills · any `SERVICE_*` environment variable set in a kustomize overlay (`deployments/kustomize/services/*/overlays/*/patch-env.yaml`) · `configs/*.yaml`
- **fires when:** you add a config field that is set ONLY by an environment variable — typically a production-overlay `SERVICE_FOO_BAR` — and do not also name it in the service's `configs/*.yaml` or give it a `SetDefault`.
- **the trap.** `Load` calls `SetEnvPrefix("SERVICE")` + `SetEnvKeyReplacer` + `AutomaticEnv()` and then `v.Unmarshal(&cfg)`. **`AutomaticEnv` only resolves keys viper already KNOWS about**, and viper's key set comes from the config file, explicit `SetDefault`s and explicit binds — not from your Go struct's `mapstructure` tags. A key present in none of those is never queried, so `Unmarshal` leaves the field at its zero value **however the environment is set**. Nothing errors. The variable is right there in `printenv` on the pod, the overlay diff reviews perfectly, and the struct field is `""`.
  **What makes it worse than a normal typo: the failure is indistinguishable from the feature being switched off.** For any opt-in field — which is the shape CLAUDE.md 2026-08-02 §2 *prescribes* for new authority on a shared seam — "empty" is the legitimate OFF value. So the code does exactly what it should do with an empty value, quietly, and the only symptom is downstream and far away.
- **the check — and it must be able to come out the other way.** Do not inspect the overlay, the pod env or the struct tag; none of them can fail. Load the config in a test with the env var set and assert the FIELD:
  ```go
  func TestFooIsReadFromTheEnvironment(t *testing.T) {
      t.Setenv("SERVICE_SERVER_DELIVERY_PORT", "8090")
      cfg, err := Load(writeMinimalConfigWithoutTheKey(t))   // mirrors configs/<svc>.yaml
      if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
      if cfg.Server.DeliveryPort != "8090" { t.Fatalf("got %q", cfg.Server.DeliveryPort) }
  }
  ```
  **Run it BEFORE the fix.** It fails, and that failure is the whole evidence; written afterwards it merely agrees with you. Then bind the key explicitly next to the other env wiring:
  `if err := v.BindEnv("server.delivery_port"); err != nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf(...) }`
  (a `SetDefault("server.delivery_port", "")` also registers it; `BindEnv` says the intent out loud, and a default that is also the OFF value reads as if it were doing nothing).
- **⚠ the blast radius of the miss is not the config layer.** `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` the worked case was the delivery-only listener (SYS-095): `SERVICE_SERVER_DELIVERY_PORT` unbound would have meant no second listener, so `links.webdesign.uk/c/<token>` — every customer's confirmation link — would have 404'd **at the box**, where the anchored `location` regex means there is no log line, no metric and no error anywhere in the cluster. Two invisible failures in series, and the config half is the one nothing can see.
- **generalises:** a value that arrives by a path your tests do not travel is unverified however carefully it was written. Env vars, ConfigMaps and secrets all have this shape — the artefact that carries them is reviewable and the DELIVERY of them is not, so assert at the reader. And when the legitimate value of a field includes the zero value, no runtime check can distinguish "not wired" from "wired off"; the test is the only place that distinction exists.
- **relations:** SYS-095 (the listener this nearly shipped broken) · SYS-094 · LANDMINES "the customer-facing origin is not a catch-all" (the second invisible failure in the series) · MEMORY [[a-config-key-that-nothing-reads]], [[grep-the-config-key-before-calling-it-a-win]], [[a-print-statement-is-not-a-config-row]]
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `site_delivery_and_editor` lane, building RFC_054 Q2. Found by writing `TestDeliveryPortIsReadFromTheEnvironment` before trusting the wiring; it failed with `Server.DeliveryPort = "", want "8090"`. Fixed in commit `d30917150`.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `site_delivery_and_editor` lane

### A value backfilled into `site_components.rendered_html` is NOT a value the site HAS — the template gate reads `site_specs`, the next chrome render regenerates the slot, and the divergence detector overwrites your edit and files it as human review

- **footprint:** `site_components.rendered_html` (any `UPDATE … SET rendered_html = replace(…)` fleet sweep), `site_specs` aspect `site_config` (`analytics.gtm_container_id`, `locale`, `chrome`), `{{if .gtm_container_id}}` and every `{{if .<config_key>}}` gate in a chrome template, `datahelpers.ChromeRenderInputsSQL`, `StaleSiteComponentsCheck` (`check_integrity.go:375`), `chrome_divergence_overwritten`, `nav_rebuild`, any "backfill existing sites" instruction
- **fires when:** you are asked to put something on every site — a tag, a meta line, a banner — and the fastest correct-looking move is to edit the stored chrome artefact in SQL. It serves instantly (pages copy the stored head in), the curl check passes on every domain, the count is 27/27, and it is exactly right for as long as no chrome renders.
- **the trap:** the stored artefact is a **cache of a template's output**. The template does not contain your value; it contains a gate (`{{if .gtm_container_id}}…{{end}}`) whose input is looked up per site in `site_specs.site_config` — declared in the component's `input_schema` as `source: config.analytics.gtm_container_id`. Chrome is regenerated from template + inputs on any `nav_rebuild`, any `stale_chrome` item, any site rebuild; with no key the gate is false and your value is gone. **Then the platform records it as YOUR mistake**: the regenerated slot differs from the stored one, so `chrome_divergence_overwritten:site_component:head:<id>` is filed at `needs_human_review` — reading as "an operator hand-edited chrome and we corrected it". `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` the 08-24 GTM backfill wrote 13 heads at 13:13:52; **agritec.uk lost the tag at 19:20:53 the same day** when its lane added a tool page (`add_tool` → `nav_drift` → `nav_rebuild`), and the only `chrome_divergence_overwritten` head row in the estate's history is that one, to the second. The other 12 are waiting for their first nav change. `bugs_open/397`.
- **why it survives review:** every instrument you would reach for reads the cache. `curl | grep -c googletagmanager` reads the served page (copied from the cache). `rendered_html LIKE '%…%'` reads the cache. The pipeline's own re-render fan-out re-injects the cache. Only a query against `site_specs` — the one table the backfill never mentioned — can tell a durable site from a temporary one, and nothing about the symptom points there.
- **the tell:** the artefact carries your value and the spec does not — the four-bucket census in `analytics_gtm/scripts/check_gtm_state.sh --db` ("B ARTEFACT ONLY"). Also: served `gtm=1` where the 07-31 sites serve `gtm=2` — the header's `noscript` half is missing because the header template reads the same key and nobody edited that artefact.
- **the check, BEFORE you write:** open the component's `html_template` and `input_schema` — `grep` the template for your value; if it is inside an `{{if .x}}`, **write `x` to the spec the schema names and let the platform render**, and know that writing the spec fingerprint-drifts the site: `StaleSiteComponentsCheck` will file `needs_rerender` (`stale_chrome`, 20 ever, all dispatched) and `rerender-pages` force-rerenders every slot AND every page — one commit + one Actions run per page. So the durable fix is a rebuild, sized `SELECT count(*) FROM pages WHERE site_id IN (…)` **before** the first `UPDATE`. And **merge** into an existing `site_config` row (`data || …`), never replace: the 07-31 rollout replaced and dropped relojistas.com's `intent_probe`.
- **relations:** `bugfix-117` (template vs stored chrome — this is the third leg: template, artefact, AND the spec the template reads); CLC-030 `page_divergence_overwritten` (the page-level twin, 25 rows on apis.uk); MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] inverted — here a repaired artefact is not a repaired site; `bugs_open/397`
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `analytics_gtm` lane (session "google"), while checking what a GA4 publication would record; the backfill was the `apis_uk_bees_homepage` lane's, 2026-08-24, and its 27/27 was true when written
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `analytics_gtm` lane

### A served-page md5 behind Cloudflare is not a baseline — email obfuscation re-keys the bytes on EVERY response, so "the page changed" and "nothing changed" hash differently and identically at random
- **footprint:** any `curl … | md5sum` or `wc -c` "pin the served page BEFORE" step (`bugfix_311_component_keys/RUNBOOK_311_fix.md` "Pin the served page's md5 and byte count BEFORE" is the recipe lanes copy) · every site proxied by Cloudflare that renders a `mailto:` · `/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection` · `data-cfemail`
- **fires when:** you pin a served page's hash to detect whether a rebuild/deploy landed, then compare after. The page carries a `mailto:` (webdesign.uk's footer contact does), so Cloudflare rewrites it to `/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#<hex>` + a `data-cfemail="<hex>"` span + an injected `email-decode.min.js` tag — **and the hex key is fresh per response.** Measured 2026-08-25 on `preview.webdesign.uk/index.html`: baseline `15cd3681…` (34,913 B), re-fetched with the file provably untouched in vm-sites → `eff68431…`. A "changed" verdict with a zero diff. The inverse is also possible in principle: a real one-byte change can collide in byte COUNT with the obfuscation's variance.
- **the check:** compare the **origin copy**, not the edge: for vm-sites-served hosts `git -C ~/projects/vm-sites log -1 --format=%h -- <domain>/<page>` before and after (a new commit = deployed; same = not), or diff the served body with the injection stripped — `curl -s <url> | sed -E 's#/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection\#[0-9a-f]+#MAILTO#g; s#data-cfemail="[0-9a-f]+"#data-cfemail=""#g; /email-decode.min.js/d' | md5sum` — and prove the stripper works by running it twice on an unchanged page first (equal hashes) — that is the control the bare md5 lacks. For "did the copy change", grep for a literal the change ADDED and one it REMOVED; the sibling entry above ("Do not grep for `mailto:`") is the same edge rewrite seen from the other side.
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `webdesign_uk_build_service` lane, verifying the owner copy-brief rebuilds — the index hash moved while `git log` on vm-sites showed the file untouched since `444205b`; found by asking the repo instead of the edge
- **added:** 2026-08-25, webdesign_uk_build_service lane

### A CSS repair appended to a site theme expires at that site's next DESIGN run — the register says this was "fixed at source" and it was the other direction that got fixed
- **footprint:** `css_themes.css_content` · `persist_css_to_theme` · `render_css_from_spec` · `css-patch-agent` · `save_css_to_db` · `contrast_failure` · `dark_section_audit` · `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/543_webdesign_agent_persists_rendered_css_to_theme_row.sql` · `docs026_concept_register/register/styling-render-pipeline.md` (the webdesign-agent flow entry)
- **fires when:** you repair anything by appending CSS to a site's theme row — a contrast fix, a dark-section fix, a hand-applied one-off — and then reason about whether it is still there. Also when you read the register to find out whether that is safe.
- **the trap:** two agents write one column and only one of them reads it. `css-patch-agent` **appends** to `css_themes.css_content` (migration 318). `webdesign-agent` **renders from the spec and writes the result byte-for-byte into the same column** (`persist_css_to_theme`, migration 543) — and `render_css_from_spec` composes from the palette/layout/typography FK rows, so it has never heard of the appended rules. Every patch since the last design run is deleted. 543's four write guards (size, `origin <> 'seed'`, one linking site, `IS DISTINCT FROM`) all protect against other harms; **none of them notices the column contains repairs.** The work items stay `complete`, and nothing re-files them.
- **why it survives review:** the register entry for that flow carries a 2026-08-21 correction ending *"a per-site CSS repair used to expire at this flow's next run, roughly weekly, with no signal — **that is now fixed at source**"*. Read at face value that is a licence to append. 543 fixed the OPPOSITE direction — the patch agent clobbering a stale or empty theme row with a fragment (`bugs_closed/198`) — and **institutionalised this one**. A dated correction now sits beneath that line; if you are reading an older copy, or a doc that quotes it, you will get the wrong answer.
- **the tell:** patch markers gone from a site that provably had repairs. `(length(css_content) - length(replace(css_content,'css-patch-agent','')))/15` returns 0 while `site_work_items` holds `contrast_failure` rows at `complete`. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` agritec.uk: five repairs appended and git-committed 2026-08-24 20:54–20:55; row rewritten **2026-08-25 12:09:57**, one minute before a `needs_design` item completed at 12:10:29 (`webdesign-agent`, `reason='palette_changed'`); 0 markers left, and the served stylesheet (200, with an invented-path 404 control) holds none of the five rules.
- **the check, BEFORE you append:** ask whether the surface you are writing to is one the RENDERER READS or one it OVERWRITES. `css_themes.css_content` is overwritten. The palette/spec rows are read, so a repair expressed there survives by construction. If you must append anyway, record the expiry: compare `css_themes.updated_at` against your repair's `updated_at` before quoting the repair as live, and never treat a `complete` work item as evidence that its rule is still in the file. ⚠ **Do not read a zero marker count as proof of this mechanism either** — dartsonline.com and lendzy.co.uk both show 0 markers with completed repairs and have **zero** `needs_design` items, so their cause is UNEXPLAINED; that inference was made and withdrawn on the day this entry was written.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/396` (this, filed) · `bugs_open/390` (the repair that never applies in the first place — same symptom, different cause) · `bugs_closed/198` (the direction 543 fixed) · `bugs_open/296` §10.5 · migration `542` (the base-integrity gate in front of the same agent)
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `bugfix_390_cascade_attribution` lane (session "bug sweep"), found while measuring why contrast repairs do not stick; the register sentence was written in good faith about a real fix
- **added:** 2026-08-25, bugfix_390_cascade_attribution lane
