### Clearing `lock_type`/`locked_by` does NOT unlock a `page_components` row — `locked_at` is the only column automation reads, and stripping the type makes the lock HARDER while reading as unlocked
- **footprint:** `page_components.locked_at` · `page_components.lock_type` · `page_components.locked_by` · `site_components` (same five columns) · `datahelpers.AgentWritableSQLFor` (`platform/orchestration/datahelpers/chrome_render_inputs.go:91`) · `pageComponentAgentWritableSQL` · `CheckComponentLock` / `classifyComponentLock` (`platform/orchestration/actions/lock_helpers.go:67,100`) · `emitLockBlockedChangeItem` · `lock_blocked_change` · any hand-written `UPDATE page_components SET lock_type = NULL` / `SET locked_by = NULL` unlock-then-relock script
- **fires when:** you own a locked row, need one delivery to land on it, and write the obvious pair of scripts — unlock, dispatch, verify, re-lock. `lock_type` and `locked_by` are the columns that *describe* the lock, so they are the ones you clear. The row then reports `lock_type` empty and `locked_by` empty everywhere you look.
- **the trap:** writability is decided by one predicate and it names a different column — `(locked_at IS NULL OR (lock_type='timed' AND lock_expires_at IS NOT NULL AND lock_expires_at < NOW()))`. `lock_type`/`locked_by` are classification and messaging only. So clearing them changes **nothing** about the lock — and `classifyComponentLock` then treats `locked_at` set with no `lock_type` as **hard/permanent**, deliberately ("conservative — never silently overwrite what we can't classify"). You have made the row *less* writable and every column you can see says unlocked. **The re-lock script has the mirror defect and it is the dangerous one:** setting `lock_type='permanent'` over a NULL `locked_at` leaves the row fully agent-writable while the admin dashboard displays it as permanently locked.
- **why it survives review:** the two defects **cancel**. A wrong unlock that leaves `locked_at` set, paired with a wrong re-lock that never restores it, ends exactly where it started — so running the pair against the live rows looks like a clean idempotent no-op, and a dry run cannot separate them. Nor does the work item help: `apply_section_edit`'s lock gate is a **skip-result, not an error**, so the item completes `status='complete'` with `success: true` and the dispatcher records a normal delivery. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` two such items ran, both `complete`, both `success: true`, zero bytes written; the refusal is two levels down in `result->'response'->'edit_result'` as `{"skipped":true,"locked":true}`.
- **the tell:** the skip reason reads `is locked by ""` — an **empty** `locked_by` in a message that only prints when the row IS locked. That contradiction is the signature of this exact half-cleared state (NULL scanned into a Go string). Also: `page_components.updated_at` unchanged after a "successful" delivery.
- **the check, BEFORE you write either script:** diff your `SET` list against the framework's own admin unlock — `internal/core-manager/admin/page_admin_handlers.go:450` clears **all four** (`locked_at`, `locked_by`, `lock_type`, `lock_expires_at`), and `:491` locks by setting `locked_at = NOW()`. Then assert the effect rather than echoing your own write: `SELECT (locked_at IS NULL OR (lock_type='timed' AND lock_expires_at IS NOT NULL AND lock_expires_at < NOW())) AS agent_writable` must be `t` after the unlock and `f` after the re-lock. A `RETURNING` of the columns you just set can only prove you set them. Capture the original `locked_at` **before** unlocking and restore that value, not `NOW()` — it is the lock's provenance and the age any lock-review sweep reads. Put the post-relock assertion in a `DO`/`RAISE` inside the transaction (a block of `SELECT`s cannot stop a `COMMIT`) and prove it can fire by inverting its predicate once.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/058` (the lock gate itself) · `bugs_open/069` (the `site_components` chrome half, same predicate) · MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] (this is the sharpest instance: `complete` + `success:true` + zero writes) · [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]] · [[mutate-the-code-to-prove-the-guard]]
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `news_editorial_features` lane (session "news editorial"), running the lane's own pre-written instance-scope acceptance scripts; both had been reviewed into a handoff and a README as ready-to-run and neither had ever been executed. `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-25.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, news_editorial_features lane

### `--color-cta-bg` may hold a GRADIENT, so using it as a `<color>` silently discards the whole declaration — and the "safe" fallback declaration above it can never fire
- **footprint:** `--color-cta-bg` · `cta_bg` · `--color-cta-bg-ink` · `solidCTAFill` · `firstGradientStop` · `buildLegibleInkDefaults` · `platform/orchestration/actions/palette_specialised_slots.go` · `platform/orchestration/actions/render_css_from_spec_action.go` · `platform/orchestration/actions/derive_brand_head_assets_action.go` · `content_components.html_template` · `css_themes.css_content` · `.cta-btn-primary` · `.tool-cta-btn-primary` · `hero-services` / `hero-about` / `hero-contact` · `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/619_cta_bg_is_not_a_colour.sql`
- **fires when:** you write, review or copy any CSS that reaches for the CTA band's colour — a button ink, a gradient stop, a `color-mix()`, a tinted panel. Also when you audit a component and see a `var()` with a fallback and take it for a guard.
- **the trap:** `cta_bg` is the ONE palette slot whose contract admits a gradient as well as a colour — `derive_brand_head_assets_action.go:275` says so in as many words, and **10 of the fleet's themes hold one** `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]`. A gradient in a `<color>` position is **invalid at computed-value time**: the declaration is discarded and the property becomes `unset` — **inherit** for `color`, **initial/transparent** for `background`. Inside a CTA band the inherited ink is the band's own white, so you get white text on a white button (**1.00:1**, measured on three live pages including a paid front door) and a hero heading on the page's own paper (**1.11:1**). Nothing errors, nothing logs, and on any solid-`cta_bg` site every line of it is correct.
- **why it survives review:** the rule carries the standard progressive-enhancement pair — `background: var(--color-cta-bg, var(--color-primary));` then an enhanced `background: linear-gradient(…var(--color-cta-bg)…);` — which every reviewer's eye skims as "guarded". **It is not.** That idiom works for a declaration dropped at PARSE time; a `var()` declaration parses fine and fails after substitution, and IACVT goes to inherit/initial, **never back to the earlier declaration in the same rule**. So the safety net is dead weight, and three sibling heroes in the same package run the identical idiom against `--color-primary` — always a colour — and are genuinely fine, which makes the pattern look proven.
- **the tell:** read the measured BACKGROUND, not the ratio. A contrast tool reporting white on `rgb(245,243,239)` where the rule paints a blue band is telling you the declaration was *discarded* — if it had merely fallen back you would see the fallback colour (`#1A1A2E`) instead. `scripts/render_audit.py <url>`, or `getComputedStyle`. A ratio alone reads as "someone picked bad colours".
- **the check, BEFORE you use the token:** never write `--color-cta-bg` into a `color:`, a gradient colour-stop, or a `color-mix()`. Use the renderer-owned companion in the mandatory two-level form — `var(--color-cta-bg-ink, var(--color-cta-bg))` — the same contract as `--color-primary-ink` (46 consumer rows, 0 bare, `[MEASURED 2026-08-14]`). ⚠ **And do not "simplify" it to the gradient's first stop:** a stop is a FILL, not an ink, and it fails AA against the button's white face on **6 of the 10** gradient themes (`#3b82f6` 3.68, `#059669` 3.82, `#8b5cf6` 4.28) — only `#1e40af` (8.8) clears it, and that is the theme you will be debugging on. `--color-primary` is worse: illegible on **4 of 12**, worst 1.24:1. To census existing damage, grep by POSITION not by component name (`color: var(--color-cta-bg`, `gradient(.*var(--color-cta-bg`, `color-mix(.*var(--color-cta-bg`) — a by-name census returned 3 of the 4 affected rows and the fourth appeared only when a `DO`/`RAISE` verify block was induced against pre-migration state.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/398` (this) · VIZ-014 (the legible-ink companion pattern being reused) · VIZ-010 / VIZ-012 (the only detectors that can see it — every source-side check passes) · `bugs_open/396` (*a design run erases every appended CSS repair* — which is why the repair belongs in the component template, not in an appended stylesheet rule) · `bugs_open/396` (*deferred items are un-re-filable* — 7 of this defect's own detections have been stuck since 2026-08-11) · `bugs_closed/352` / VIZ-016 (the invented `H1.H1` selector that made the other 4 detections unactionable, then cancelled by migration 587) · `bugs_open/113` (palettes inheriting layout literals)
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `finetuning_uk_service` lane, from an owner report — *"a couple of the pages have no hero images which has meant that the copy is also unreadable"*. His causal chain was exactly right: no image ⇒ the hero falls to the CSS band branch ⇒ that branch is the broken one. The platform had already detected it on 2026-08-10 and lost it twice over.

### A classification spec with NO `content_features` key makes a site invisible to BOTH news mechanisms — and the step that writes the key cannot reach it for you
- **footprint:** `site_specs` (aspect `classification`) · `content_features.news_feed.recommended` · `platform/orchestration/actions/feed_news_recommendation_action.go` (`matchVerticalNews`, `evaluate_news_feed`) · `platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/check_news_feed.go` · `content-feed-trigger` (`scheduled_tasks.content-feed-refresh`) · `content-feed-orchestrator` · `seed_content_sources_action.go` · `content_sources`
- **fires when:** a site's news never appears (`/data/latest-news.json` 404, `content_sources` 0) and you look for the job that failed. Also when you add a site and expect the framework to decide about news for it.
- **the trap:** there is no failed job. `content-feed-trigger.find_news_sites` (6-hourly) and `MissingNewsSourcesCheck` (hourly rotation) both select on ONE predicate — `(data->'content_features'->'news_feed'->>'recommended')::boolean = true` on the current classification row — and a row with no `content_features` key at all is simply never selected, with no row, log line or finding. The writer of that key, `evaluate_news_feed`, (a) builds its signals from `classification.industry` / `site_type` / `category` and domain substrings and **never reads `industry_tags`** — `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` **0 of 31** current classification specs carry an `industry` string, 27 carry `industry_tags`, so that first signal is empty fleet-wide; (b) **writes nothing on no-match** (returns `recommended:false` to the caller and leaves the spec untouched, so absence cannot be told from "never ran"); and (c) ~~has ONE live carrier, `improvement-loop`, whose scheduled task `improvement-sweep` is `enabled=false` (last completed 2026-08-22)~~ **CORRECTED 2026-08-26: `improvement-sweep` was RE-ENABLED 2026-08-25 21:18Z (owner's word, executed by the loanzy lane, `bf42e9288`) and runs every 900 s — so the carrier now RUNS, and (a)+(b) alone keep the blind spot: on no-match the step still writes NOTHING, so an unflagged site stays invisible for ever. A hand-authored block is SAFE under the running sweep — no-match means no write, and a matching site only receives a deep merge.** Fleet correlation is exact: **9 of 9** sites with the flag have sources, **22 of 22** without it have none (as of 2026-08-25).
- **why it survives review:** the mechanism reads as data-driven and automatic — a deterministic industry table, an enrichment step "after classification", a trigger on a schedule. Every part exists and runs; only the join between the classifier's output shape and the matcher's input shape is missing, and a site that was never selected leaves nothing to grep.
- **the tell:** `SELECT (data ? 'content_features') FROM site_specs WHERE site_id=… AND aspect='classification' AND is_current` → **f**. If it is `t` with `recommended=false`, the matcher DID run and chose no — a different question (edit the table, or hand-author).
- **the check, BEFORE you dispatch anything:** hand-author the block (precedents: `dartsonline_traffic/SQL_2026-07-29e_arm_news_feed.sql`, `idea_uk_vm_site/sql/SQL_2026-08-25_arm_news_feed.sql` — supersede + insert, never `UPDATE data` in place), keeping `source_types` to what you mean (`rss`/`scrape` are skipped by the seeder; `api_news` is LLM-authored). If you set `separate_page=true`, the listing page must be TYPED `news-index` on BOTH `site_plan_pages.role` AND `pages.page_type` — a page NAMED `news-index` is not enough, and the plan re-imposes itself on `pages` at every save (the "THREE `pages` upsert helpers" entry above, `site_db_actions.go:1240`); otherwise `render_news_section` withholds the archive and the "More insights →" link, and `MissingNewsPageCheck` asks `content-gap-planner` for a SECOND news page. Then one direct orchestrator run with a receipt, and run it TWICE: `dispatch_sources` is async and the same run's triage/render read whatever has landed (first idea.uk run: triage loaded 0, snippet carried 1 of 12).
- **relations:** `bugs_closed/015` (mistyped `page_type` orphans a page from its machinery) · `bugs_open/230` (discovery has no recurring driver — the sibling silence) · `bugs_open/316` (feed cap/ordering, the OTHER reason a flagged site can starve) · `idea_uk_vm_site/RUNBOOK` Phase 6
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `idea_uk_vm_site` lane (session "idea.uk"), closing a 404 that had stood since the site went live and had been carried as "the dispatch never landed" for three weeks; the dartsonline lane hit the same wall 2026-07-29 and recorded it only in its seed's comment, which is not a place a session touching `site_specs` reads.

### `detected` is a QUEUE, not a shelf — `detected-item-promoter` dispatches any `detected` row whose (item_type, handler) pair has ever completed, every 15 minutes, whether or not `improvement-sweep` is on
- **footprint:** `scheduled_tasks.detected-item-promoter` · `site_work_items.status = 'detected'` · `write_audit_findings` · `triage_detected_items` · `294_TRIGGER_improvement_loop_v1.sh` · `IMP-054` (the detect-only design-audit trigger) · every `design-audit-agent` / `site-review-agent` / `offer-analyser` / `brief-fidelity-auditor` / `visual-design-auditor` / `content-quality-auditor` run, however fired
- **fires when:** you fire an LLM auditor "detect-only" — a one-shot `scheduled_tasks` row, the 294 trigger, a hand-run `execute_llm_prompt` + `write_audit_findings` — believing its findings will sit at `detected` for a person to read because the sweep is off. Also when you read `improvement-sweep.enabled = false` as "the rewrites are off".
- **the trap:** since 2026-08-15 (`bugs_open/083` candidate 2, owner ruling) a second promoter runs every 900s and promotes any `detected` row with a handler whose (item_type, handler_agent) pair has ≥1 lifetime completion and ≥25% success. `content_rewrite → page-build-handler` has thousands. So the audit you fired to *look* dispatches page regenerations within 15 minutes. **[MEASURED 2026-08-25]** 26 LLM-audit rows promoted between 08-20 and 08-24 with the sweep OFF; 0 LLM-audit rows left at `detected` (the promoter drains the queue).
- **why it survives review:** IMP-054 (2026-08-09) was written before the promoter existed and says, correctly *for its date*, that "a lone discovery run files findings nothing can ever see"; `triage_detect_items_action.go`'s header still says the loop's `triage_findings` is "the ONLY promoter". Both were true and both are stale by addition — the register status outlived its truth.
- **the tell:** `spec->>'original_pipeline'` stamped and `triaged_at` set on a row whose site had no improvement-loop orchestration that day; the promoter's own tick row in `doc_notes` names the pairs it promoted.
- **the check, BEFORE you fire an auditor to "just look":** `SELECT enabled FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE name='detected-item-promoter'` — if `t`, `detected` will not hold. Park is `deferred` + `handler_agent ''` + provenance in `spec` (`capability_gap`'s convention; `bugs_open/396` on why a named handler at `deferred` is worse), or file through `write_audit_findings` with `filing_mode: record` once that ships (RFC_056 §5). To see what the promoter would take: run its `pre_query` with the final `UPDATE` replaced by a `SELECT`.

### A `scheduled_tasks` row is NOT a single-flight slot — the scheduler stamps BOTH timestamps at FIRE, so every concurrency control on the row (per-row guard, `countInFlight`, `max_concurrent`, `timeout_seconds`) and every agent-side `notify_scheduler` stamp is inert, and "one execution at a time" reads as true from the readers

- **footprint:** `cmd/scheduler/main.go` (`stampCompleted`, `runTick`, `loadDueTasks`, `countInFlight`), `scheduled_tasks.last_triggered_at`, `scheduled_tasks.last_completed_at`, `scheduled_tasks.max_concurrent`, `scheduled_tasks.timeout_seconds`, `scheduled_tasks.interval_seconds`, `notify_scheduler`, `notify_scheduler_idle`, `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/582_dispatch_sibling_A_task_name_on_trigger_row.sql`, `583_dispatch_sibling_B_parameterise_notify_stamps.sql`, `584_dispatch_sibling_C_insert_trigger_2.sql`
- **fires when:** you reason about how many runs of a scheduled task can be alive at once, size a throughput lever on a task row, design a "sibling row" or a "timeout moves with concurrency" rule, or read `loadDueTasks`' doc comment ("prevents the same task from spawning multiple concurrent pods") and believe it.
- **the trap:** `loadDueTasks` (a READER) carries a convincing in-flight guard — `last_completed_at >= last_triggered_at OR last_triggered_at + timeout_seconds <= NOW()` — and `countInFlight` counts rows where `last_completed_at < last_triggered_at`. Both are correct code for a scheduler that stamps `last_completed_at` when the run ENDS. This scheduler does not: `runTick` calls `stampCompleted` (`UPDATE scheduled_tasks SET last_triggered_at = NOW(), last_completed_at = NOW()`) the moment `fireTrigger` has published — "For fire-and-forget tasks, mark completed immediately … we don't wait for the orchestration to finish" — since `892a289e9` 2026-03-17 (refactored into the named function by `dc2e4b61a` 2026-07-21, `bugs_open/048`). So every `fire_message=true` row re-fires at `interval_seconds` rounded up to the 30 s tick, regardless of whether its previous run is alive; `max_concurrent` and `timeout_seconds` never bind; and an agent workflow's `notify_scheduler` step (`UPDATE scheduled_tasks SET last_completed_at = NOW() …`) bumps a column the guard already passes. The dispatch_throughput lane read the two readers twice (two sessions, 2026-08-18), never the writer 80 lines above them, filed a 090 on the claim (it died at `max_tokens`), and shipped three migrations (582–584) on the premise. Measured 2026-08-25: the one original row overlapped ITSELF **361** times in 24.5 h.
- **the tell:** `last_triggered_at = last_completed_at` to the microsecond on a row whose run is visibly still executing. And Little's law on the row's own numbers — runs in a window × mean run duration ÷ window length — IS the mean concurrency; the lane's STARTER quoted "17 runs / 25 min / avg 218 s" (= 2.5 alive) and concluded "one at a time".
- **the check:** before citing any `scheduled_tasks` concurrency property, run the self-overlap query — `WITH t AS (SELECT orchestration_id, created_at s, updated_at e FROM orchestration_states WHERE owner_agent_type='<the task's agent>' AND created_at > now()-interval '24 hours') SELECT count(*) FROM t a JOIN t b ON a.orchestration_id<b.orchestration_id AND a.s<b.e AND b.s<a.e;` — non-zero on a single row settles it (rows are retained ~24–27 h, so the window is bounded). And `grep -n 'last_completed_at' cmd/scheduler/main.go`: the FIRST hit is the writer (`stampCompleted`) — read it before the readers. The rate knob that IS live is `interval_seconds`: 60 → 90 s cadence, 30 → 60 s, ≤25 → every 30 s tick `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]`; and fires spaced ≥30 s apart see the previous turn's claim (p90 time-to-first-claim 24.2 s) where fires 1 s apart co-pick the same site 94% of the time.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/398` · `bugs_open/048` · WDS-002 (corrected 2026-08-25) · `WRONG_CALLS.md` 2026-08-25 · MEMORY [[writes-the-field-is-not-reads-the-field]] · [[cite-the-arm-not-the-function]] · the sibling-parity entry below
- **source:** 2026-08-25, dispatch_throughput lane (session "throughput"), answering the council's round-2 (`db9b7cbf`) "prove two DIFFERENT sites, not two fires" objection — the census that answered it showed the row overlapping itself. `docs024_key_docs_latest/dispatch_throughput/NOTES_dispatch_throughput.md` 2026-08-25 §5.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, dispatch_throughput lane

### The `build-pipeline-trigger` row has a byte-copied SIBLING — an `UPDATE scheduled_tasks … WHERE name = 'build-pipeline-trigger'` edits half the dispatcher, and the other half keeps the old query with no error anywhere

- **footprint:** `scheduled_tasks` rows `build-pipeline-trigger` and `build-pipeline-trigger-2`, `scheduled_tasks.pre_query`, `docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/213_dispatch_gate_matches_dispatcher.sql`, `052_build_pipeline_trigger.sql`, `584_dispatch_sibling_C_insert_trigger_2.sql`, `584_dispatch_sibling_C_insert_trigger_2_VERIFY.sql`
- **fires when:** you change the dispatcher's `pre_query`, `interval_seconds`, `target_topic`, `timeout_seconds` or `enabled` by name — including applying `213_dispatch_gate_matches_dispatcher.sql`, which sits UNTRACKED in the working tree since 2026-08-12 18:39, was never committed or applied (live `pre_query` md5 `200246f7…` is the pre-213 form, 2026-08-25), and targets `WHERE name = 'build-pipeline-trigger'` only.
- **the trap:** since 2026-08-24 (584) two rows share `concurrency_group='dispatch'`, `target_agent_type`, `target_topic` and a byte-identical `pre_query`, differing only in `name` and `input_data.task_name`. Nothing links them — the sibling was `INSERT … SELECT`ed from the original once. A by-name UPDATE succeeds (`UPDATE 1`), a post-check on the named row passes, and the fleet then runs two DIFFERENT dispatch gates in alternation — the one you fixed and the one you did not. Agent-side edits (`find_dispatchable_site`; `sql_for_agents/284`, `285`) reach both rows because both rows point at one agent; row-side edits do not.
- **the check:** `SELECT name, md5(pre_query), interval_seconds, target_topic, timeout_seconds, enabled FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE name LIKE 'build-pipeline-trigger%';` must show ONE distinct value per column across the rows. Re-runnable as `DO`/`RAISE` (assertion 1 of 5): `sql_for_agents/584_dispatch_sibling_C_insert_trigger_2_VERIFY.sql`. Write the migration as `WHERE name LIKE 'build-pipeline-trigger%'` (or `WHERE concurrency_group='dispatch' AND target_agent_type='build-pipeline-trigger'`) and assert the row count you expect. If the sibling has been retired (owner decision pending 2026-08-25 — the lever may move to `interval_seconds`), the parity check passes trivially on one row; that is fine.
- **relations:** WDS-002 (corrected 2026-08-25) · `bugs_open/398` · the entry above · council round 2 architecture seat (`db9b7cbf`: "two copies of logic that must stay in sync is itself a small accumulating cost")
- **source:** 2026-08-25, dispatch_throughput lane, on finding `213` untracked in the tree while answering that objection.

### `du` as a normal user cannot see `/var/lib/docker`, and reports `4.0K` rather than an error — every disk census on this box has been a census of a quarter of it

- **footprint:** `du -xsh`, `du -x /`, `/var/lib/docker`, `/var/lib/containerd`, `docker system df`, `docker builder prune`, `~/.cache/go-build`, `df -h /`, any "the disk is filling" investigation
- **fires when:** you size a filesystem with `du` — top-level sweep, biggest-consumers list, before/after cleanup table — as an unprivileged user, on a machine that runs Docker. Which is this one.
- **the trap:** `/var/lib/docker` is root-owned and mode 0710. `du -xsh /var/lib/docker` returns **`4.0K`**. That is **not an error, not a zero, and not a refusal** — it is exactly what an empty directory looks like, and the `2>/dev/null` on every `du` recipe in this estate discards the one `cannot read directory` line that would have corrected it. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` the real contents were **539 GB of Docker build cache** (6,052 records, 437.9 GB reclaimable) plus **104 GB of images**, i.e. **~64% of a 937 GB disk**, invisible to every figure this lane published for three days — including a confident before/after cleanup table.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** the sweep *succeeds*. It returns a plausible, well-formed, sorted list of consumers whose largest entries are real. Nothing is missing from the output; the output is simply of a different, smaller thing than you asked about. A 98.7 GB clean-up was measured, reported and celebrated against a denominator that excluded the actual dominant consumer.
- **the check, and it costs nothing — RECONCILE `du` AGAINST `df` BEFORE BELIEVING ANY DISK CENSUS:**
  ```bash
  du -xsb / 2>/dev/null | awk '{printf "du:  %.1f GB\n", $1/2^30}'
  df -B1 --output=used / | tail -1 | awk '{printf "df:  %.1f GB\n", $1/2^30}'
  # 2026-08-25: du 226 GB vs df 754 GB. A 528 GB gap means YOU CANNOT SEE THE DISK.
  docker system df                      # the part du cannot reach
  du -x / 2>&1 >/dev/null | head        # and READ the denied lines instead of discarding them
  ```
  **Rule out deleted-but-open files first** — the other classic `du`/`df` divergence, and it was ruled out here (`lsof -nP | awk '/\(deleted\)/'` → 0.9 GB, not 528). If that is small, the gap is something you cannot read, not something being held.
- **⚠ AND DO NOT PRUNE THE IMAGES TO MATCH.** `docker system df` reported **1,034 images / 1 ACTIVE**, which reads as "1,033 are dead". It is not: images share layers, and docker's own reclaimable figure was **11.41 GB, not ~90 GB** — it did not move at all across a prune that freed 537 GB of *cache*. Meanwhile `push-*`/`deploy-*` are git-blind and ship **whatever is tagged locally**, so a locally-built-but-unpushed release image is a session's work and `docker image prune -a` destroys it (`v1.0.1337` was 9 hours old and unverifiable from the session — registry credentials must not be fetched, owner 2026-08-23). **Small upside, unbounded downside.** `docker builder prune -a -f` is the safe half: 539 GB → 1.272 GB in 6 minutes, images/containers/volumes untouched, and a `FROM scratch` build afterwards proved an empty cache costs time and not capability.
- **the third reaper-shaped hole, and the only one that is ABSENT rather than slow:** Go's cache trims at 5 days (and still gained **50.5 GB in 25 h**); `systemd-tmpfiles` reaps `/tmp` at 10 days against a 4-day fill; **Docker's builder has no automatic eviction by default at all.** That is how it reached half a terabyte unremarked. `docker builder prune --keep-storage <N>GB` is the bound.
- **relations:** MEMORY [[a-bigger-container-is-not-a-bound]] (same lane, third repeat of measuring the container you already know about) · [[a-closer-census-cannot-see-what-it-succeeded-at]] · the `/tmp` recipe entry above · `docs024_key_docs_latest/tmpfs_exhaustion/` · OPP-005
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `tmpfs_exhaustion` lane, from the owner asking "is /tmp full again?" — it was not, and following the arithmetic rather than the suspicion found a 528 GB hole in the lane's own instrument.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `tmpfs_exhaustion` lane

### A `NEVER-REPO-PATH` citation naming a file you can `ls` is an UNCOMMITTED file, not a dead citation — and the category that says "no file, ever" is the one you are least likely to double-check

- **footprint:** `scripts/report-register-citation-rot.py` · `NEVER-REPO-PATH` · `DOC-078` · `docs/agent_docs/docs026_concept_register/` · `citation-rot reports` · `link auditors` · `dead-path sweeps`
- **fires when:** you run the citation-rot report (or any path-existence check) and read its `NO FILE, EVER, UNDER THAT NAME` list. That list is short, sorted, names the entry and the field, and is phrased with more certainty than any other category in the output — which is exactly why it gets acted on without a second look.
- **the trap, and it has TWO independent causes that produce an identical line:**
  1. **The file exists and is simply not committed yet.** The report reads register entries from the **working tree** but resolves paths against **git history** (`HEAD` ∪ everything-ever). A file that is `git add`ed but uncommitted — or untracked — has no history, so a perfectly correct citation to it reads as *"no file, ever, under that name"*. `[MEASURED 2026-08-20]` **2 of 7** entries in that category were this: `SEO-005` citing `platform/orchestration/actions/head_assembly.go`, which was sitting in the tree with status `A `. Both cleared themselves on 2026-08-25 with **no citation edited**, when the owning lane committed the file (`4abcd55a4`).
  2. **The report's own normaliser mangled a live path into a dead one.** `clean()` strips line refs, anchors, possessives and backticks. Any citation form it does not understand is not a parse error and not a skip — it emits a *different string*, which then legitimately resolves to nothing. `[MEASURED 2026-08-20]` **1 of 7** was this: `FIX-061` cites `scripts/migration/run-migrations.sh:65,:283`, the regex understood `:151,227` but not the repeated colon, stripped `:283`, left `:65,`, and `rstrip` produced `…run-migrations.sh:65`. The file is tracked and clean. Fixed in `a9665268f`; **the class is not fixed** — the next unhandled citation form fails the same silent way.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** every other category in this report hedges. `MOVED-AMBIGUOUS` says the file exists and the citation is imprecise; `NEVER-UNROOTED` and `UNJUDGED-DIRSHAPE` say outright they are not judged. Only this one asserts a fact about history, and it is the one the lane's handoffs quote as the corpus's stability evidence (*"still exactly 4"*, three handoffs running). A false positive here does not read as noise — it reads as **a lane that cited something that never existed**, complete with an entry id to blame. Both failure modes above arrived pointing at innocent lanes.
- **the check, and it is two commands before you believe ANY line in that list:**
  ```bash
  # 1. ask the WORKING TREE, which the resolver never does. 'A ', '??' or a plain ls hit
  #    means uncommitted, NOT dead. Nothing to repair; it self-heals on their commit.
  git status --porcelain <cited-path>; ls -la <cited-path>
  # 2. prove the normaliser did not invent the path — compare AS-CITED against NORMALISED.
  #    If they differ, the report is judging a string the register never wrote.
  grep -n '<entry-id>' docs/agent_docs/docs026_concept_register/register/*.md
  git log --oneline -1 -- <cited-path>     # tracked-and-clean + reported dead = cause 2
  ```
  **Only after both come back negative is it rot.** `[MEASURED 2026-08-25]` on the day this was written, **0 of the 3 newly-reported dead citations were rot** — the category went 4 → 7 → 4 without a single citation being repaired.
- **the transferable shape:** a checker that reads its CLAIMS from one universe (the working tree) and resolves its FACTS in another (git history) will report the seam between them as a defect in the claims. Ask which universe each half of a check lives in before believing a mismatch, especially when the two are normally identical and only diverge for minutes at a time — that is precisely when nobody is looking.
- **⚠ if you change the normaliser, MUTATE to prove your test can fail.** The regex above already had a self-test case for the form it handled, which is what made the unhandled form invisible. The guard added with the fix was verified by reverting the regex on a scratch **copy** while keeping the new case, and watching that one case fail with exactly `NEVER-REPO-PATH` (10/11, exit 1). A self-test in this file has passed vacuously before — 2026-08-17, `landmines-keys-check.py`, where `parse()` starts at the `# Entries` marker so a mutation above it registered nothing.
- **relations:** the `git rev-list --objects` entry above (same report, same category, third distinct way its universe acquires holes — and its own ⚠ about grepping for words only YOUR entry contains applies to verifying this one) · MEMORY [[live-and-committed-are-independent-facts]] (a tool shipping from a FILE cannot see it is UNCOMMITTED — this is that trap seen from the reader's side) · [[mutate-the-code-to-prove-the-guard]] · [[a-pass-from-a-blind-check-outlives-the-blindness]] · `DOC-078`
- **source:** 2026-08-25, concept-register lane, from re-running the handoff's verification table cold and finding the sharpest category had moved 4 → 7. None of the three was rot.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, concept-register lane

### `dockerd --validate` prints `configuration OK` for an INVALID VALUE — it checks key names only, and the failure it misses stops the daemon

- **footprint:** `dockerd --validate`, `/etc/docker/daemon.json`, `deployments/docker/daemon.json`, `builder.gc`, `reservedSpace`, `maxUsedSpace`, `systemctl restart docker`
- **fires when:** you write or edit `daemon.json` — a BuildKit GC policy, a registry mirror, a storage driver — and reach for `dockerd --validate --config-file <path>` to check it before installing it as root. Which is the correct instinct, and it half-works.
- **the trap:** it validates **key names**, not **values**. `[MEASURED 2026-08-25, Docker 29.2.1]`
  ```
  {"builder":{"gc":{"enabled":true,"policy":[{"reservedSpace":"not-a-size"}]}}}  →  configuration OK
  {"builder":{"gc":{"enabled":true}},"bogus-key-xyz":1}                          →  the following directives don't match any configuration option: bogus-key-xyz
  ```
  So a pass tells you that you have not misspelled a *setting*. It tells you nothing about a misspelled *size*, duration or enum.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** `configuration OK` is the same string you get for a genuinely correct file, and you are about to act on it with **root**. **An unparseable `daemon.json` stops `dockerd` from starting** — on a box whose entire release pipeline is `make build-*`, that is the build estate down, discovered at the next build rather than at the restart.
- **the check:** never install on a bare `configuration OK`. Restart and **prove the daemon came back in the same breath**, with the rollback already typed:
  ```bash
  sudo install -m 0644 -D <repo>/deployments/docker/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json
  sudo systemctl restart docker
  systemctl is-active docker && docker info >/dev/null && echo "docker is back"
  # rollback, if not: sudo rm /etc/docker/daemon.json && sudo systemctl restart docker
  ```
  There was **no pre-existing `/etc/docker/daemon.json`** on this box as of 2026-08-25, so the rollback is a delete, not a restore — check that before assuming the same.
- **the generalisable half:** **an "OK" from a validator is evidence only once you have watched that validator say NO to something.** Feed it one deliberately broken value first. That is the whole cost, and here it converted a green tick into a known-half-blind green tick before it was run as root on shared infrastructure. Same shape as a mock that cannot assert a negative, and as a self-test whose control never proves a candidate existed.
- **relations:** MEMORY [[mutate-the-code-to-prove-the-guard]] · [[a-post-fix-zero-needs-a-demand-control]] · [[a-doc-comment-is-not-an-enforcement-mechanism]] · `deployments/docker/README.md` (the install runbook this produced) · the sibling entry above on `du` not seeing `/var/lib/docker`
- **source:** 2026-08-25, `tmpfs_exhaustion` lane, found while preparing a root-run install for the owner — the control was run *because* it was about to be root, not because anything looked wrong.
- **added:** 2026-08-25, `tmpfs_exhaustion` lane

## `pages.deployed_at` is UPDATED on every redeploy, not set once at first publication — so `deployed_at > <time>` measures RERENDER CHURN, not "published since"

- **footprint:** `pages.deployed_at` · any `WHERE deployed_at > …` / `deployed_at BETWEEN …` · "pages published since X" · "was this site built before Y" · blast-radius counts over `pages` · `site_discovery_rotation` reconciliations
- **fires when:** you reach for `deployed_at` as a birth date. The name reads like one, it is NULL until first deploy (so it behaves like one on new rows), and there is no `first_deployed_at` beside it to warn you.
- **why the wrong result looks exactly right:** the number is plausible and LARGE, so it reads as a big finding rather than a broken query. **[MEASURED 2026-08-25]** hunting for sites affected by a selector defect, `count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.deployed_at > r.last_selected_at)` returned **24 of 24 domains**, most with double-digit counts — which reads as fleet-wide breakage. The real population was **two**. Proof it is mutated: `dartsonline.com` pages have `created_at` **2026-07-06** and `deployed_at` **2026-08-24/25** — every rerender rewrites it.
- **the check:** compare `created_at` to `deployed_at` on any long-lived site before trusting a `deployed_at` window. A wide gap on old rows means the column tracks the LAST deploy. For "has this ever shipped", use `deployed_at IS NOT NULL` — that predicate is sound and is what `render_sitemap` correctly uses. For "shipped since X" there is **no column**, and the honest answer is to say so rather than approximate it.
- **relations:** [[a-stale-page-holds-every-improvement-since-it-rendered]] · the `last_triggered_at`/`last_selected_at` family — same shape: a timestamp that advances for a reason you did not have in mind.
- **source:** portfolio_positioning lane, 2026-08-25, caught BEFORE the bad query reached a handoff
- **added:** 2026-08-25, portfolio_positioning lane
