### A hand-filed work item copied from a completed row can be UNCLAIMABLE for ever — the claim gate reads two COLUMNS (`status`, `handler_agent`), and a completed row no longer shows its promotable state

- **footprint:** `site_work_items` (hand INSERT of any item type) · `claim_work_item_action.go:135` · `handler_agent` · `swi_no_handlerless_promotable`
- **fires when:** raising a work item by hand and copying its shape from a completed row of the same item_type — which is exactly what the `page_rerender`/`page_id` entry above tells you to do. The spec copies fine; the claim eligibility does not, because it lives in columns whose claim-time values a completed row no longer displays: the claim query takes `status IN ('triaged','approved')` only, and the `swi_no_handlerless_promotable` CHECK requires the `handler_agent` COLUMN (not the spec key) to be non-empty at any promotable status.
- **the tell:** none — that is the trap. A `pending` item with an empty `handler_agent` inserts cleanly (`INSERT 0 1`), violates nothing, and sits `pending` for ever. No error, no log, no reaper interest; it reads as dispatcher latency for as long as you are willing to wait. (Measured 2026-09-02: the same shape at `triaged`+handler was claimed in ~2 min; mine at `pending`+empty sat 7+ min until read the claim query.)
- **the check:** before filing, read the CLAIM GATE, not the template row: `grep -n "status IN" platform/orchestration/actions/claim_work_item_action.go` — then file at `status='triaged'` with `handler_agent` set as a COLUMN (copy its value from the completed row: `SELECT handler_agent FROM site_work_items WHERE id='<template>'`). If you already filed at `pending`: `UPDATE ... SET handler_agent='<h>', status='triaged' WHERE id='<id>' AND status='pending'` — safe, the CHECK admits it once the handler column is set.
- **relations:** the `page_rerender`/`page_id` entry above (this is its column-side sibling — its own advice, followed exactly, walks you into this one) · MEMORY [[detection-works-schedule-and-dispatch-do-not]]
- **source:** hit directly 2026-09-02, site_delivery_and_editor lane, filing the guides-index rebuild (item 7f1f4993) from bccedf9c's shape
- **added:** 2026-09-02, site_delivery_and_editor lane

### A design preference pre-seeded into `design_intent` before a FRESH build is SUPERSEDED by the classifier — `pinned=true` does not hold — while the same value seeded into `mission` survives, because nothing on the fresh path writes `mission`

- **footprint:** `site_specs` aspects `design_intent` / `mission` · `site_specs.pinned` · `write_site_spec` (`site_spec_actions.go`, `siteSpecDeepMerge`) · `domain-research-classifier` · `resolve_composition_pallette_action.go` / `resolve_composition_typography_action.go` (the cascades) · any `SEED_*.sql` written from the `oufe` pattern · `082_submit_domain_unified.sh` FRESH path · `bugs_open/438`
- **fires when:** you pre-seed design values for a site you are about to submit through 082 with no `--from` — the documented, encouraged move ("seed the site row and its specs, then dispatch"). You put palette, typography and `layout_preference` into `design_intent`, set `pinned=true`, and dispatch. No symptom: the seed row is written, the verify block shows it current, the classifier runs green.
- **the trap:** the classifier writes `design_intent` too, and `write_site_spec` supersedes the current row (`is_current=false`) after deep-merging — **scalar keys are overwritten by the incoming value, and `pinned` is a column on the OLD row, not a property the merge reads.** `[MEASURED 2026-09-02, gamedesign.uk]` manual `design_intent` 17:04:35 `pinned=t` → `is_current=f` at 17:11:32; the classifier's own row carried `#F5F0E8` where the seed said `#F4F1EA`, and `layout_preference: soft-editorial` was simply gone. The composition then tag-matched from prose and chose `magazine-grid`. Meanwhile the SAME palette seeded into `mission.preferred_palette` reached composition byte-for-byte (`palette_source=mission_hint`, the first time that rung had fired in production, fleet baseline 30/1/0) — **not because `mission` is protected, but because on the fresh path nothing writes it** (`persist_mission` reads a key 082 never sends, `bugs_open/438`). Durability by accident.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** your seed IS in the table (superseded rows are kept), `SELECT … WHERE aspect='design_intent'` without `is_current` returns it, and the classifier's replacement is usually CLOSE to what you asked for (it read your brief), so the served site looks roughly right and the loss of the one key that mattered (`layout_preference`, or a specific font) reads as "the planner chose differently" rather than "my seed was discarded".
- **the check:** seed a preference **only where its cascade reads it and where no later writer of that aspect runs before composition.** Today that is: palette → `mission.preferred_palette` (rung 1, unwritten on the fresh path — until 438's fix repoints `persist_mission`, after which even this needs the in-data `locked` key that 438 proposes); typography → BOTH `mission.preferred_typography` and `design_intent.typography.reference_values`, and expect `design_intent` to win because its cascade is reversed; layout → **nowhere durable yet** — `layout_preference` has no cascade rung outside `design_intent`, so state it in the brief's prose (the tag-match reads `style_direction`) and accept the planner's pick. After the classifier runs, verify with `SELECT aspect, COALESCE(source_agent,source), is_current, pinned FROM site_specs WHERE site_id=… ORDER BY created_at` — a `manual … f` row beside a `domain-research-classifier … t` row for the same aspect is this landmine, fired.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/438` (§6a-bis: "a seeded design preference is only durable if it lands where no later writer supersedes it"; the repoint-alone fix would DESTROY the only durable seeding surface) · `oufe/SEED_2026-07-25_oufe_site_and_specs.sql` (the pattern, correct for `evidence_base`/`imagery_style_guide`, which the classifier does not write) · MEMORY [[webdesign-colour-churn-landmine]] (superseded on the "pin" point by the owner ruling 2026-09-02: `reference_values` is NOT a pin, by design)
- **source:** 2026-09-02, gamedesign.uk lane, first FRESH build with a hand-seeded composition; full account `docs024_key_docs_latest/gamedesign_uk_rebuild/NOTES_gamedesign_uk_rebuild.md` (17:20Z and 17:38Z entries), values in `SEED_2026-09-02_gamedesign_uk_site_and_specs.sql`
- **added:** 2026-09-02, gamedesign.uk lane

### 1,651 `undeployed_asset` rows sit at `unresolved` BORN THAT WAY — they are parked non-convergence, not handler failures, and "draining" them dispatches 1,651 deploys that cannot fix what the rows describe

- **footprint:** `site_work_items` (`item_type='undeployed_asset'`) · `check_undeployed_assets.go` (`findUndeployedAssets`, half 1) · `asset-deployer` · any backlog triage / queue-drain sweep · `status='unresolved'`
- **fires when:** you triage the `unresolved` backlog — the fleet-wide "needs investigation" signal — and meet the largest single block in it (`[MEASURED 2026-09-02]` **1,651** rows, 1,086 of the icon ones born since 08-23, more every sweep). The obvious reading is "the handler keeps failing"; the obvious remedies are re-triage them (dispatches asset-deployer per row) or read them as 1,651 missing files (they mostly are not — e.g. all 12 on mortgagecalculator serve 200, that lane's 09-02 handoff).
- **the trap:** three mechanisms compound. (1) The check's half-1 evidence is PURPOSE-PREFIX and SITE-wide — `rendered_html LIKE '%/assets/images/'||purpose||'[.-]%'` — so "no page references anything of this purpose" is read as "not deployed", which conflates a WIRING gap with a DEPLOY gap. (2) The remedy is `asset-deployer`, which re-commits bytes and cannot make a page reference anything — so the item completes (or not) and the state it fired on persists. (3) The recurrence brake (`insertWorkItem`'s two-strike arm) then files the re-detected item DIRECTLY at `unresolved` — `created_at = updated_at`, `result = {}` — so the rows were never claimed, never failed, never touched: the platform noticed the non-convergence and parked it where the parking looks like handler failure.
- **why the wrong answer looks exactly like the right one:** every row honestly describes a real state (an asset nothing references), `unresolved` legitimately means "attempts exhausted" on other types, and a sampled re-deploy genuinely succeeds — commit sha and all — which reads as "the drain is working" while changing nothing a page renders.
- **the check:** born-parked is one query — `SELECT count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='undeployed_asset' AND status='unresolved' AND created_at=updated_at;` — and a row in that set had NO attempts, so its history cannot tell you the remedy fails; the mechanism above tells you it cannot succeed. Per-page truth comes from `check_unrendered_page_imagery`'s census (IMG-077, three states with three different owners: 412 wiring / 357 fragment rows / composition), not from this backlog. The backlog's disposition is an owner decision recorded in `bugfix_114_imagery_wiring/PLAN_2026-08-22_imagery_wiring.md` (2026-09-02 revision) — do not drain it as if it were work.
- **relations:** `bugs_open/114` (the class: deployed and never referenced) · `bugs_open/412` (the wiring gap the deploys cannot close) · `bugs_open/357` (the fragment rows behind many tool-page members) · MEMORY [[a-complete-work-item-is-not-a-repaired-artefact]] · 016b §9's "a gate's 0 findings has two causes" — here inverted: 1,651 findings with one wrong obvious cause
- **source:** 2026-09-02, bugfix_114_imagery_wiring lane (resumption); full evidence: `docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_114_imagery_wiring/NOTES_imagery_wiring.md` (2026-09-02 entry)
- **added:** 2026-09-02, bugfix_114_imagery_wiring lane

### `/code-review` (and any bare-diff reviewer) on this tree reviews EVERY session's uncommitted work — its findings name files you never opened, in the second person

- **footprint:** `/code-review`, `scripts/pattern-check.py --commit`, any "review the current diff" tooling, `git diff` with no pathspec, the working tree of this repo
- **fires when:** you finish a task, run `/code-review` to check your own work, and read the report. There is no symptom and no reason to suspect anything: the findings are specific, correct, well-evidenced, and about **other people's code**. Measured 2026-09-02: a run at the end of a migration-only task returned **15 findings, ZERO of them the running session's** — they named `save_page_meta_description_action.go`, `voicetells.go`, `registerwords.go`, `check_unrendered_page_imagery.go` and migration `694`, none of which that session had touched.
- **the trap:** this tree is shared by ~10 concurrent sessions and the working directory holds all of their WIP at once. A reviewer told to read "the current diff" reads **the union of everyone's half-finished work**, and reports it to you as if it were yours. The danger is not the wasted read — it is that **acting on a finding means editing another lane's code mid-flight**, which is the one thing `CLAUDE.md` most consistently forbids ("contribute into the bug file, do not compete"). A reviewer is also blind to WHO owns what, so it cannot warn you.
- **and the failures it reports may not be at HEAD at all:** two of the 15 named **untracked** files. An untracked file is not at HEAD, so `go test` failing on it is a **working-tree** failure belonging to whoever is writing it — **not a red HEAD**, and not something your commit can fix or break. Check `git ls-files --error-unmatch <path>` before reading a red test as an estate emergency.
- **the check:** before acting on ANY finding from a diff-scoped reviewer, ask whether the file is yours — `git status --porcelain <path>` plus `git log --oneline -3 -- <path>`, and `scripts/who-owns.py` for a bug number. If it is not yours: **route it as a CONTRIB into the owning lane's directory, never fix it.** To get a review that is actually about your work, scope the reviewer to your own paths rather than running it bare. ⚠ The reviewer's own scope note may tell you the tree churned mid-pass (HEAD advanced 3 commits during the measured run, and two findings were edited underneath it) — that line is load-bearing, not boilerplate.
- **source:** 2026-09-02, `deferred_work_item_park` lane (`bugs_open/396`), after a `/code-review` at the end of a migration-only task
- **added:** 2026-09-02, deferred_work_item_park lane
